Recaptured.  I guess...

Honestly, this place's sorbettos and gelatos rival Capogiro in Philly and any of the joints in NYC.  The Biscotti, Vanilla, Irish Whiskey (tastes like Bailey's) and Banana varieties rocked my world.  I had a first-class affogato with a delicious espresso pulled just for me.  EVERYthing is home-made - cakes, novelties - even Pizzelle.  Can't wait to return and so glad a local chick turned me on to this place. Cheaper than Rita's.  No comparison.  JUST GO!!!!

Believe it or not we had an excellent time at cracker barrel  with our party of 5.on a not-to-busy Friday night (5-7 minute wait for a table).  The little one loved her food (fried shrimp) and she and my MIL shopped in the gift shop and bought "Mad Libs" and an old-style box of Cracker Jack.  (The little one had never had cracker jack before and wondered about the prize.)  After a carb and fat loaded meal (not good for the diet at all) we relxzed on rocking chairs out front (for sale) and played checkers.  The staff especially Judi (trainer) in the gift shop and Justin or server were all terrific.  Is this my favorite place?  No way.  But it beats Denny's or Perkins any day and you can get pancakes for dinner!

COnveniently located in RTM, this is a great place to grab inexpensive cut flowers.  The staff is friendly and very helpful.  Note:  The also give a discount to PHS (Pennsylvania Horticulture Society) members and often run deals during the flower show.

A solid 3 stars, maybe even 4  - food is very basic (possibly a little bland) but the spring rolls and bun were tasty and the traditional Vietnamese Coffee hit the spot on a cold day.  grilled Lamb over bun was succulent and tasty - albeit a small portion and $12.95.  Quick service got me in & out even on a busy Thursday lunch rush. Nearly every table was full - and this after years of being open is a great sign.  Prices are higher than in Philly (Chinatown, Vietnam,m Vietnam Palace, Pho Cali) but considering where we are - I am beyond thrilled to have a non-pizza lunch alternative.  Can't wait to go back and try the sumer rolls.

This is our go-to Rita's - for it's spacious parking lot, clean picnic tables and benches, and sweet teen-aged girls running to show.  Our 8 year old and I both get kiddie sized (ASK)  water ice or custards - and the kiddie portion is PLENTY in my opinion.  I love the coffee custard but is is GONE (forever??) now - so I get chocolate or swirl.  DD often gets lemon, blue raspberry or swedish fish flavored "wooder" ice.  The blendini is fun, too. And now they have sundaes (unlimited toppings like hot fudge, "jimmies"/Sprinkles, whipped cream and a cherry).  ASK for the kiddie size - it's cheaper, smaller and just as satisfying.  Indulgent and a diet breaker for sure - but a summertime must in PA!

Nope.  Now we go tot he Giant in Aston which is far better - albeit more crowded.  This Giant has out of date dairy products (have seen that twice now - so READ THE DATES!!!) and a picked-over produce department.  Step up your game, Giant in Brookhaven!

After not coming to the Aston diner in years, our party of 6 had a very nice lunch (specials are a good value and come with soup and dessert) for under $70.  Service by "Barb" was great and we enjoyed the food.  Burgers, grilled cheese, Chicken Caesar salad, Cobb Salad with shrimp (instead of chicken) [$14.95] with mammoth portions (took some home).  Glad things have improved. We'll return,

Good, greasy, basic pizza - a little expensive for what it is. Plus they sell gelato, subs & salads.   I had a single slice with spinach (very good spinach topping by the way) for $3.25 to go.  BIG parking lot and a large bar.

Tacos al Pastor - I dream of you...  They are slowly improving the dining area - but still needs work. meanwhile, for $2.50 a pop I get tacos al pastor - the REAL DEAL and a luscious side of guac (also $2.50).  Pico de gallo here is fresh - but super spicy with jalapeno chunks and raw onion - so bring breath mints.  Horchata is also great.  LOVE IT HERE.  Please open one in Media/Aston!!!

I have to agree.  Carrie, our "minder" Jen and the staff of Monster Minders are, indeed, pros.  Sure, they cost more than having your neighbor do it, but they walked our 14 year old pug every morning for about 6 months prior to our move to the burbs.  I am very thankful to Monster Minders for being there when we needed them.  Being able to book online is great, too. And automated billing to your credit card is super-easy!  Thank you, Monster Minders!  Woof Woof!

Meh.  2.15 for a bottle of Dasani?  I shoulda gotten a latte for $2.19 instead.  Mediocrity at its best.  I am so NOT a fan of Cosi.  After eating in them in NYC in the early 2000's when this chain emerged - it seemed cool at first.  And - if the bread is fresh and hot (before it solidifies into cold cardboard) it actually tastes pretty good.  The hungrier you are the better it'll taste.  Meanwhile - the overpriced sandwich fillings are mediocre at best. There are better places to waste (I mean spend) $9 bux.  Sorry.  Not a big fan.

When I went to Penn, this was THE Wawa - complete with the welcoming comittee of "usual" homeless guys - the same ones day after day.  They do alot of business at this well-travelled location.  \Smokes, coffee, junk food, sandwiches, ice cream - everything a college kid might need at the last minute.

OK - I haven't actually gotten to EAT the food here just yet. Today my friends and I stopped in to Mr. Pasta.  The place was dead-empty (no dine-in people at all) and just one guy in front of us who had ordered some cheese ravioli - which he says he gets all the time and LOVES.  My friend and I looked at the cases of fresh home-made "to go" pastas.  Alas, they are cash only so we had to leave and come back another day. But we WILL be back.  And soon.

We needed an oil change - stat  - and poor planning had us arrive at Pep Boys 40 minutes before closing.  They took us right away and had us in and out for $26.95 plus tax.  No issues.  Oh - and Klaus (manger from the Wilmington location) is now up here and is very knowledgeable about parts.
It's big - it's (relatively) new, it's fairly clean.  Pretty nice as major stadium venues go.  As always, wish there were more ladies bathrooms (and cleaner) and healthier food choices.

I had a lovely first-ever experience at Fresh Market. All 4 staffers I spoke with were friendly and helpful.  They carry Stonewall Kitchen Jams and Sauces - so I snagged a $7 jar of swanky peach jam.  I love stonewall - and if I buy it here I don't have to pay shipping.  They also had HINT water on sale for $1 a bottle - so I got 8 bottles. I also picked up 3 bottles of Australian Water infused with flower essences.  I am a Bach Flower Essences Practitioner so I am curious to see what it tastes like (should just taste like plain water) and if it works.    They also carry Vosges chocolate bars and other high end goodies. Produce looked great - albeit pricey and meat case looked good but I doubt I wll buy any.  I liked it here alot and will be back. It's a little pricey - but it's closer to my house than Whole Paycheck (aka Whole Foods).

Carrabas is Carrabas - and as chain Faux-talian goes it's fine.  Mid priced (dinner for 2 with one beer each and no dessert no app was about $45.  They also have promotions all the time - the one they offered when we were there was a $13 deal for a soup or salad and 2 (yes 2) plates of pasta (one for now and one for home.  Whatever,  My friend had the soup which he enjoyed and I had a very boring "house salad" with iceberg, a few shreds of carrot and 2 pieces of celery and 3 olives. No cuke, no tomato.  Just BORING.  Hot bread (good for white bread) and herbed olive oil followed.  The pasta plates are enormous.  Carbo loading at its finest.  Not gourmet - but in the Spingfield Mall - this is the best you'll get (There's a Ruby Tuesday and a Sbarro) for a sit-down meal.  Oh - and the place was FULL of kids on the Thursday night we went.

I went to Slainte (after passing it a gazillion times) yesterday when I had an hour to kill waiting for a bus.  I just so happened to arrive during happy hour (Mon - Fri 5-7 PM) and got the $5.00 bar snack - Cheesesteak Eggroll.  It was very salty - but fried crispy and most folks porbably would have loved it.  Meanwhile the regular menu was not cheap - but I was impressed by the selection of desserts and half & half 20 oz "Irish Style" pours.  (Black 'n Blue, Stoudt 'n Ale, etc.)  As I am not a drinker, a good pub is wasted on me - but Slainte is a nice environment - Eamon my server was a doll -  and I would come back here again - but next time - a green salad!  Clean bathrooms too - which is more than I can say for 30th Street Station.

Gorgeous - but it's a shame that there are just so many homeless around - and dogs pee in it.  Meanwhile, it's a treasure - and now that PHS (PA Horticultural Society) is re-planting the elm trees (they died), it will be even more special.  A Philadelphia landmark.

We bought our 2007 Hyundai Sonata from Fred Beans.  Over the years my family and my husband's family have each bought many different cars - new and pre-owned - of different makes from Fred Beans.  Between them and Foster & Kardane (and we were friendly with the Kardane clan back in the '80's) they pretty much OWN the D-town automotive scene.  Competitive prices and salespeople who don't make you feel like a target.  Good repair work, too.  I'm a fan.

I returned to Jay's a few weeks ago - and this time I put them to the test.  I ordered the sushi/sashimi "pick 3" - and had Salmon sashimi (very good), Yellowtail nigiri (Good - but not orgasmic) and Ikura.  I am VERY picky about Ikura (- it has to be "poppin' fresh) and this was very, very fresh and good. BUT - I get the feeling not too many people order it.  I also reprised the fair Eggplant Lady (appetixer) and she deserves a starring role.  Jay accomodated me with very light on the sauce (both in the shrimp mixture and on top) and 2 lusciously crispy eggplant slices.  It was raining so the place was not crowded, but the delivery was HOPPIN'. (Yes, they deliver, thank goodness!)  Also Jay showed me several goreous salt-molds he makes to serve on the sushi platters.  (Kinda like ice sculpture - but made with molded salt.)  Martin was there, too.  Nice guys at the bar.  I can't wait to take my 5 year old and husband here.  They will love it.  Oh - and did I mention the pick 3 sahimi/sushi was $8.50?  What a deal - the items I ordered would have cost $15 a la carte!

OMG!!!!  I can't even believe I am the first person to Yelp this.  Do I dare tell you all how really, really, really great this place is?  It's crowded enough as it is - if I tell you I'll never get a table.  OK, I'll tell you a little bit. It's a no-decor, little atmosphere place run by a genuinely NICE family (the hostess/daughter is marrying the pizza chef in August 2008 in Brooklyn).  They make their own mozzarella, and bake fresh brick-oven pizza on a thin - but not-too-thin crust.  The shrimp scampi is ENORMOUS - they give you over a dozen shrimp. It is garlicky & oily - so if you order it light on the garlic 'n oil it's even better (IMHO).  The Veal Parm is a flam-family (that's FLAMILY) staple and my mom & I can easily split it.  (Comes with a side of pasta.)  Fresh (onion-y) bruschetta arrives on the table nearly as soon as you are seated.  Cappucino is light and frothy.  (mmmn, mmmn good.)  A great place for families and kids.  I LOVE IT HERE!!  So much!

Average CVS - we stopped in for passport photos but had to wait a really long time to get them because only 1 person know how to take them.  Meanwhile it had everything we needed and its own parking lot - which helps in downtown Media.

After attempting to come here 3 other times (the crowds are crazy - especially on weekend mornings because this is a NEW place in an underserved area) our party of 4 got in for brunch on Sunday 3/17 (St. Paddy's Day).  In addition to the full diner menu they had corned beef & cabbage and corned beef omelettes on the menu.  Angela, our over-worked server, was friendly and terrific.  She got all of our orders right and got us in and out in short order.  (The longest part was the wait for a table.)  Aston needs more restaurants, and I surely hope the Aston Diner succeeds. The booths however (as Jamal P. states) are meant for huge fat people.  I weas sitting miles away from the table and you can't move the booths nor the table.  Next time I want to be seated NOT at a booth.  I ordered the $7.95 Aston Special - a breakfast platter with one (big) pancake, 1 slice of french toast (great), 2 sausages and 2 strips of crisp bacon (a little hard).  Very fresh tasting food.  I am pleased and will return. But I'm coming on a Tuesday and not sitting in a booth.

Pho, summer rolls, iced coffee, vermicelli, broken rice plates, all the staples in a quick-service format. Mid-priced and great for lunch. Come right when they open at 11:30 to beat the lunch rush.  New digs with a clean restroom. For now.

Just had an amazingly AWFUL experience at Mixx. It was about 7 PM on a Friday night - but the place was slow (about 3 tables occupied).  I ordered the sushi/sashimi combo. When it arrived (After the iceberg lettuce salad) the "white tuna" (likely escolar - certainly not albacore) sashimi tasted fishy.  The server had it replaced with yellowtail - which was good.  Then I tried the tuna, snapper and salmon. All were cut poorly and less-than-fresh (not spoiled but certainly not prime).  I ate only the sushi and left most of the sashimi behind. What happened next was really weird.  The $23 platter came to $24 and change - so I looked for cash and decided to leave a horrible tip.  I left $26 and proceeded to leave the restaurant.  Then a lady came out (not my server) and chased me down to give me my "change".  I said (over my shoulder(, "No, it's for him".  She thrust the change at me and said "No!" "I'm not a beggar."  She was really pissed off at my horrible tip.  Oh well.  There is no way in hell I will return here.  There's a reason most of the maki is covered in mayo, spicy sauce or crunch.  You can tell the quality of a place by its sashimi - and this place is sub-par.

My faith has been restored in Bistro St. Tropez - or maybe it just tastes better when somebody else is paying??   We attended a corporate luncheon (small group - 7 people) here and had great, attentive service - and best yet - much improved food.  Although they do now charge ($3.00) for the delicious hot rolls and pesto, the salade Hache (a chopped salad with chicken and shrimp - a tad over cooked) was fresh and tasty.  The classic Soupe a'l'oignon was rich in flavor, not too salty and had crisp crouton on top.  Mmmn!  The desserts were best of all (and I have NEVER had room for dessert here before, but somehow today I managed it) - ice-cream filled profiteroles and a chocolate mousse cake were shared by all.  Two leaves & a bud tea capped off a hearty lunch.  How we all need a nap, now! Off to the conference room...

I am honestly much, much happier than I ever thought I would be. I braced myself for the worst when my husband, 7 year old and I had a desparation lunch here after marathon shopping at Tar-jay and Christmas Tree Shops.  The little one had chicken fingers and fries ("safe"), DH had a chicken sandwich. I had rib tips and mac and cheese (Calorie hell.)  The rib tips were pretty awful (dried out and then barely re-succitated with a spicy-sweet sauce) .  Won;t get it again.  Here's the surprise - a very decent crock of mac 'n cheese.  The sauce was white and creamy (kinda-cheesy) and topped with yellow and white shreds of melted cheese.  The kid loved it.  Service (believe it or not) was great. We had a spill (my fault) and they hurried to clean things up and replaced our french fries quickly and for free.  Female server (can't remember her name) brought extra napkins without having to ask.  Very nice! It was not crowded (2:30 PM on a Sunday). Bathrooms were decently clean, too.  I've had better - but I've had Soooooo much worse.  I might even come back!

Mandarin Garden has been here For Eh Ver!  And the good food (not the needs-a-makeover decor) is why.  Consistently good "classic" Chinese American mid-priced food.  A local landmark - and right near the train.

Went here today for cake & ice cream with my 4 year old and we had a grand time with great service (sometimes service here is flaky but today it was not).  She had birthday cake ice cream, and adored it.  We split a GI-NORMOUS slice of chocolate layer cake - or shall I say we split 1/2 of the slice and took the other half home - it was THAT huge - and for $4.75 a slice it should be.  Not only was it huge, the loist rich cocoa-rich cake had a delicious chocolate buttercream icing that was finger lickin' good.  A great snack on a sweet summer day.

My faith has been restored. Stopped in solo tonight out of sheer craving for sushi.  I sat, alone, at the bar and chatted with Alan, Don (sp??) and my lovely server Amanda.  FANTASTIC service - and very good, fresh fish.  I am more of a purist and do not care for gloppy sauces - but the Tuna Tartare (with a bit of chopped mango, avocado and fried shallots mixed in) was perfect.  Fresh tuna - chopped - not minced.  The plate was garnished with at least 4 sauces though.  (All delicious - miso, cilantro oil, mayo, red wine reduction)  3 pieces of yellowtail sashimi (one order) and one temaki (hand roll) and I was stuffed.  I shall return - happily, now!

Lots of fun and nature's beauty for the whole family.  We take the kids here for a 'feeding the ducks" play date and mini hike (2-5 year olds) and they just love it.  Especially in good weather (not too hot or humid or raining).  Don't miss it!

Well, I got dragged back to "the pube" for a free event for a charity that I support.  While I love the charity and am thankful to the Public House for sponsoring the event, the food and beverage service here is sub par. Mediocre chicken wrap (with an odd mayo-ish sauce) was inedible.  Hummus and veggies were safe - but blah.  It's still not my thing.
This is a big Target with everything you need.  They even have a small Starbucks up front.

Do not get the "new" Shrimp!  Ick!!!  We came in at a time when almost every item on the hot bar was running low.  I tried the Surf & Turf bowl for the first time the the shrimp were old and rubbery.  There was hardly any steak left so the lady scraped out the "required" amount of dried out beef cubes.  The black beans were also old but then they brought more and she plopped a scoop of "new" beans over the dried out old ones.  I thought about asking her to re-make the dish but did not.  I should have!    Awful!!!!   Waste of $8.40 plus tax.  Cold items (Salsa, etc. were fine).  So sad because I often really enjoy Qdoba - for those fast food times in my life.
A generous co-worker bought a huge Mocha cake with rich, delicious buttercream frosting on it and we each had a slice.  HEAVENLY.

Absolutely wonderful and a real lesson for our 8 year old about "how the other half lives".  The show, fairgrounds, food (tea sandwiches an crustless white bread) and staff or volunteers are wonderful and the horses are magnificent.  We enjoyed the carriage event and seeing ladies in crazy hats.

Meh.  The place needs an interior overhaul.  SHAB-BY!  And the restrooms are up a creaky set of stairs and really need re-painted.  Oh - but the food.  It's just OK.  We have been twice - one lunch and one brunch - and I never need to go back.  The "Oatmeal Brulee" was really weird.  A gloppy pile of oatmeal surrounded by a "creme anglaise" of sorts garnished with berries.  Sounded better on paper than it was IRL.  The burgers and pastas for lunch were better and are a safer choice.  They were very accomodating to our large group with 3 small children and the bartender mixed a TASTY bloody Mary - but hauling kids upstairs to "go potty" while half-drunk is a feat in and of itself.  No need to return...  Unless you re-model.

Love these guys!  The name-sake ravioli is delicious and affordable - usually frozen and many varietys.  Great tortellini, too - meat or cheese (I love the meat).  Take it home and cook it up!   The real deal - straight from sou-philly.  Oh - and they support the Mummers - so go to P&S!

MGK is pretty much all I listen to - with occaional tune-ins to MMR & YSP.  DiBella does the AM show and I love Andre Gardner and Breakfast with the Beatles.  It seems like MGK now is like YSP or MMR were in the late '80's. Classic rock at its comforting best - plus they have "Get the Led Out" at 7 PM and Jones for the Stones.  All good stuff.

The beauty uber-store.  I really miss the flagship location in New York (it closed) but tnow there are Sephora's popping up all over.  Believe it or not, Sephora has really streamlined their brand selections over the years.  They used to carry TOO MANY brands.  Now it's just about right.  Since I am in the beauty bix and hate paying retail - I usually browse and try products here - but buy elsewhere.  However, I will say that in a pinch I run here for things I really need now - like Caudalie, MUFE (Make Up For Ever) and Ojon Hair Care.  This is like the grocery store for me.  Can't survive without it.
Somewhere between Meh and A-OK. Ye Olde Theatre.  I also hear they may rip it down and move the theatre into the Granite Run Mall itself.

Sorry - but i have had way, way, way better Afghan food.  I love Afghan food - the bread is usually sooooo good.  Sansom's was dry and re-heated in a toaster oven.  The rice (reheated as well) was good, but not great.  The salad - scooped out of a tupperware - obviously pre-prepped way in advance was wilted and over dressed.  The Chalaw Kadu (Normally a fave) was so greasy I had to pick out the chunks of pumkpin from the sauce and discard it.  I was the ONLY person in here on a Thursday night - and finally another single diner came in.  The place was dead - and I bet I know why. Get it together, folks.  I'm sticking with Kabul. (And oh, how I miss Pamir - now closed - in NYC)

3 or 4 max, for mediocre "typical" pizza joint food (wings, mozz. sticks, salads with iceberg lettuce, chicken parm) and often super crowded.  People just LOVE it here and it has been a Media, PA institution.  Plus they have a ton of beer - so thus, the crowds.  It is the best ever?  No.  But it is a solid choice for couples, singles and families with kids (and yes, there are alot of those) to grab a mid-priced pizza-joint meal.  The pizza itself is fine.  Not a holy grail and not bad - the Sicilian is great if you are willing to wait for it. Do not be in a rush and then order a Sicilian pie.

I am not a big CB fan - but the Blackberry Pancakes (when they have them seasonally) are great and our kid loves that gift shop.  We were headed home after an exhausting day and stopped in on a Saturdy night at about 7:15 PM and were thankfully seated right away.  I had the pecan crusted catfish off the "lighter options"menu with (frozen) steamed brocolli and (slightly watery) cheese grits.  The fish itself was tasty.  Kiddo loved her mac 'n cheese and chicken tenders. DH was less than thrilled with the gluey chicken 'n dumplings.  But dinner for 3 was $30 - so cheap. Carbo-loaded and OK. But NOT gourmet.

This Wawa location is right on Baltimore pike.  (No gas station - I am assuming it's a fairly old location).  Wawa is the quintessential coffee/beverages/gis/snacks place along with hoagies and prepared foods.  A truly convenient convenience store and very PA!

It's a shame the majestic Elm Trees had to be chopped down due to Dutch Elm disease - but the PHC (Penn. Horticultural Sociaty) is replanting Logan circle.  I only wish they could depose the homeless people in a humane way.  A gorgeous fountian - but people literally bathe in it.  Yick! I gotta be careful when my kid & I play here.
I think you mean Dimitri's.  See my other review on this small, cash-only Greek staple with terrific baba ganoush.

We had mediocre service from the "internet car" guy (there are 2 people dedicated to web-based pricing) and test drove a Ford Fusion.  Nice car - but we wound up purchasing a Hyundai instead.  Not a great dealership. Not overly impressed.

The food tastes fine - and the cafeteria style of "design your own" burritos, tacos and quesadillas is catching on fast -but don't be fooled.  It's still fast food - and it is super-duper HIGH in calories.  A typical burrito has 1100 - 1600 calories.  (Naked will reduce it by 330 - as the PLAIN TORTILLA is 330 whopping calories alone.)  That said - I do enjoy the Naked Chicked Burrito, no cheese, small (70 cal) taco-sized torilla on the side.  It's just too hard for me to "hold the guac" and save 220 calories.  That guac - for fast food guac tastes muy bien to me.  By the way - I think Jack-in-the-box owns Qdoba - I know Chipotle is owned by McDonalds.  FAST FOOD - people. Eat under a health advisory.

We used to get pizza from Allegro's all the time when I attended Penn in the mid '90's.  It is not a holy grail by any stretch of the imagination, but they make a decent, greasy pie and sell 6 packs of beer - which is essential during graduate school.  It also feels somewhat safe in there - the UC area has improved alot in recent years - but I was there when McDeath and the Wawa on Chestnut had "hatchet man" out front.  Anyhow - a good place to order a quick pie to go.

5 stars for the food!  What a fabulous find in a Girard Ave. location. We enjoyed our dinner here very much!  I had a Pineapple Strawberry Daiquiri (BYO Booze) and some amazingly good ceviche - shrimp and tillapia.  My husband's chicken enpanadas were so good, too (I got a bite!).  For entrees he had a tender and flavorful shredded pork with super-fresh corn tortilla black refried beans and rice. He liked it alot.  I really loved the Eggplant Tower - a great vegetarian (NOT VEGAN - it's overloaded with 2 kinds of cheese) choice served over white rice and a home-made tomato & onion sauce.  Desserts are very well done here, too at $6-$6.50 each we tried the banana crepes and cheesecake bunuelos.  Delicioso! We can't wait to come back (The crab & shrimp enchiladas and Carne Azada are calling to me.)! They also do weekend brunch - which sounds marvelous.  Service by our sweet cambodian server (He's a doll!) was attentive and great.  And a big thanks to Eversave (the groupon knock-off) without whom I never would have tried this place.  A super-great find!

A must-see tourist (and local) attraction - but not for small kids - way too boring. You can get through the Museum itself in 2-3 hours, if you take a tour of Wyeth's studio ($8 extra charge) allow another 75 minutes.  Cute cafe inside but no cpecialty coffee drinks - just coffee, tea and very good food.  (Shrimp & Grits and Kombucha were both available.  Interesting.  An older crowd, for sure.

Barb-Lin Carpets has been a core Doyltestown business for years 7 years.  They offer all sorts of flooring options - not just carpet - and will install it, too.  A good local source for carpetting and floors.

OMG!  Dr. Dubin moved into a gorgeous new office at the Medical Tower at 16 & Walnut.  His staff is wonderful - and they even threw a lovely dinner party tonight for his patients who have referred people.  (And next week there is a cocktail party for all of the patients at large.  Who ever hears of a dentist doing these thing?  Dr. Dubin is a great dentist (first and foremost) and also a lovely person.  My next cleaning is in November - and (believe it or not) I can't wait!

I am not a huge Indian Food lover but I do like Makhni (Butter!) Chicken.  The lamb was just OK.  Tofu was the best choice to me.  I got a rice bowl but you can also get a wrap or salad.  For whatever reason it ran me $9.80.  For that price I'd rather eat at Chipotle.  (No beverage)  Price is too high for fast food Indian.

On its literal last legs - everything is in disrepair/neglect due to the impending closure.  Good news?  Cheap ticket prices and no crowds. Bad news?  Don't eat any of the stale old food and do not use the rest room if you can avoid it.  Ick!  It's like viewing a movie in an abandoned, decaying theater.  Sad, sad, sad. Depressing.
Medium size post office with a lobby with an automated self-serve machine (thank goodness) and slow moving lines at mid-day on week days.   Glad they are here.  Wish they had later (evening) hours.

I am permanently hooked on eyesite for HIGH quality, high end eye wear. The glasses you buy here are a fashion investment - this ain't no Lenscrafters, baby.  Gene and Alya (forgive me - I bet I got her name totally wrong) are the best. I literally say - pick something for me - and they do.  And it's always FAB-u-lous.  This last time I splurges and not only bought my glasses here - but also a pair of real prescription sunglasses (not a clip like I usually get).  I feel like the fat, Jewish version of Jackie-O.  Wow. Wow. Wow.  If you like Modern Eye (and I do) and Alain Mikli in NYC - try Eyesite in Philly.    Worth every dollar spent. (And I dropped almost $1K this last time.  OUCH.)

Fuel House just opened in March 2014 and offers Zumba Fitness and Barre classes.  Individual "walk-in" classes are $10 or you can get 10 classes for $80 - but you have only 2 months to use them. (If they had said 3 months I would have totally done it.)  They are still working out the kinks in their schedule - but so far I like it and I will be back.

A great place for a quick lunch with a multitude of choices.  The "small" salad is HUGe - and you get to choose your own ingredients.  The have hot pasta and baked potatoes, a few hot entrees and sides each day, subs, hoagies, soups, chili and great sandwiches and wraps.  And the catering a great and cost effective.  Try the STRAWBERRY SHORTCAKE.  (mmn, mnn!)  Also a great spot for breakfast - they do oatmeal well.

Well, Jay was not here tonight and I bet he'd freak if he was. The place has gone downhill - and quickly.  My tuna dumplings were stuffed with Kani Salad (fake crab) not lobster as shown on the menu.  The weird, overbearing, barely-english-speaking waitress leaned in sooooo close to me it was a BIG violation of my personal space.  To top it off, she cleared my plates and brought a check - assuming I was done.  I was actually contemplating ordering 1 more roll or a piece or something - but i was so put off, I just paid the bill and left.  The 2 sushi guys behind the counter were friendly enough - but they were so busy filling takeout orders (dead for eat-in, busy for take-out) that their work was just SLOPPY.  I am unimpressed, Jay.  Get it back together!  You have some great items on the menu.  They need to be executed better - less kani stick and more REAL seafood, please.

Passero's morning (and 3 PM - 4 PM ish) crew is wonderful - they move the line quickly and get my order (which varies0 correct easch and every time.  I love the iced coffee, cafe au lait and teas here.  Such a world of difference here vs Charbucks. I also love Old City Coffee - but Passero's is right in Suburban station so I can stop there to (and from) work so easily.  Love it here!

Lily and Erin (the owners of ACW) are two sweeties who MAKE sweeties! The cupcakes are custom decorated - and the cake itself is moist and yum-a-licious.   Need cupcakes for your kids party? Come here? Need something more upscale or elegant? Like for a wedding? They do that, too. A real find!  I especially love that I never have to bake again!  (I am lazy and need home-made cupcakes at least twice a year for my kids school) ACW to the rescue.  Give these ladies a try - MUCH better than Brown Betty!  (Sorry, Brown Betty - their cake is moister.)

Stopped in for dessert & coffee at the lovely bar - and service by Brittany was first-rate.  We shared the molten vanilla cake (like a chocolate lava cake but vanilla and caramel) $11 of pure bliss and a luscious cappucino.  The perfect way to enjoy the view of the city at sunset.  Oh, the fat & calories...  ...Delightful

I had not eaten in a Cracker Barrel in over 2 years - there are none near us (save for this on) and I usually don't need all those carbs.  That said, out party of 3 had a lovely Saturday supper at about 4 PM.  It was busy but not crazy - no waiting - and my whole-wheat blackberry/blueberry pancakes were loaded with REAL fruit and so tasty.  Very inexpensive, too.

I came here out of sheer desperation and they carry Eukeneuba small breed senior. What I noticed - the place smells AWFUL and there are tons of puppies and PIGS ($399) for sale.  This ain't right! Stop supporting puppy mills.  2 young adults (late teens?) seemed to be running the place.

Lily has a new partner now and brand-new digs in Port Richmond. Her cupcakes won her the $10K prize on Food Networks Cupcake Wars - and she also appeared on Cupcake Champions.  Her decorations are gorgeous - but more importantly - the cupcakes taste amazing!!!  We love you, Lily!!!
I met Dr. Hopper because our kids go to the same school and when he explained his patient care philosophy (No Inurance needed) I was an instant believer.  I am so glad to have him "on call"!

I always forget about Bistro St. Tropez.  It is tucked away in a design show-room building on about 22 or 23 & Market.  On the 4th floor.  You really have to remember that it's there.  Meanwhile I have been for lunch 3-4 times and have had salads (excellent) omel;etes and sandwiches.  All were very good and mostly specials pr plat du jour.  Reasonably priced, too - and fresh lemonade.  (I adore a good Arnold Plamer.)  This is a nice lunch option.  Don't forget about it!

I called the Brookhaven PetSmart to see what their hours were (for grooming as well as for the store) and the phone rang and rang and rang - no answer.  Finally, somebody answered and I was able to schedule an early (8 AM) nail trim for my mutt.  Griffon (the groomer), Rob (store manager) and Ellen (who opened the door  - as I was literally the first person there that day) were all terrific.  Now that the Springfield PetSmart (one of 2 in Springfield) closed, we'll be coming here for grooming, food, treats, supplements and whatever else our pooch might need.  Still, nothing can compare to the prices at DelChester Feed up in Newtown Square.  PetSmart is kinda like "Giant Food" for us.  We have to go, so it is nice to have a new (opened late 2017), clean, reliable PetSmart nearby.  Thank you Griffon.
Fun to take the bridge by train - can get crowded by car.  you can see the river and the Camden Riversharks stadium.  Nice.

A family favorite for years - and now our kid is nearly 9. Salmon over angel hair with fresh tomato and spinach is divine.  Veal parm platter is large enough for 2 to share. Cappucino is some of the best around.  (GET ONE!)  We love coming here at lunch time (when there is less or no line).  The owners just had a 2nd baby - Congrats!
My kid loves it!  Free entertainment just blocks from our house.  Nice at Xmas, too.

Upgrading my review - the staff here are lovely and we attending a competition here (The annual "Challenge Cup" and it was so smoothly run and wonderful.  For a single surface and old (1938) facility, it's still a great rink.

I had a better experience here with the tuna "Pizza" (On an egg-roll wrapper??) but you must ask for sauces on the side - they drown it in THREE sauces - Eel sauce, Kewpie Mayo and Wasabi Mayo.  I also had an "East" roll made with cooked shrimp (safe), frozen tamago (figures) and cuke.  Tasted good, actually.  Yikes!  Better than my last visit here.

Ate here one day at about 2 Pm for a late lunch out of sheer desparation with DH and 9 year old kiddo.  Kiddo bitched and moaned at first b/c she wanted Subway.  She wound up very happy with her basic chicken & cheese quesadilla - no pico. She also liked the guacamole. And demolished the side of black beans.  (Who knew - kiddo eats beans?)  DH & I each had "the usual" naked burritos (burrito bowls) loaded with beans, rice, meat and toppings.  A calorie binge - but worth it. We got in and out and back on track.

No issues - although i tend to visit the Giant on Twp. Line more - this is actually the closest major supermarket to my office so it's handy when I need food (frozen meals or snacks) or bottled beverages.

OK, first let me make it perfectly clear that I don't DO truck food, but today I was absolutely STARVING and this cart (Near Drexel/Hahneman) on the North East corner of 15 & Race - which usually has a huge line every day - was nearby.  So for $3.50 I took a leap of faith and got beef w/ broccoli (no sauce) over brown (aka fried) rice.  It's good.  Really!  I might even come here again.

Friends don't let friends spend fourbucks on Charbucks! That said, I occaisionally splurge on a $3.00 iced latte served up by Brie (sp??) at the Passero's in Suburban station. Or a lovely Cafe au Lait for $2.45 in the afternoon.  The roasted-bitter espresso they use still has a good flavor and the service far supasses that of Charbucks.  Passero's is some of the best coffee in the city (that and La Colombe) - so I will be back.  Budget permitting. Love it here!

I don't get to come here very often any more - but when I do I try to come when the place is DEAD EMPTY - like today - a random Thursday at 2 PM.  Dead.  As a result?  Fan-tabulous service from Stefan (from Serbia) and the lovely bartender (Jamie?  James?).  Seriously - great, great service.  The food - as always - is solid but mabe just a few tweaks could up the game even more.  I especially enjoyed the crab salad (made for the burger of the month - but I asked for a side of it and they were so kind to oblige me).  Jose, baby, you done good!

Customer service and fine, fine, high quality eyewear from Gene at Eyesite is a luxury and a treat for me.  I now own 4 pair and I literally walk in and just have them pick out a style for me.  Really.  They always get it just right.  LOVE this place.  When I hit it big I am coming back for more!

I generally hate Cosi - the bread is like hot cardboard - and the food is not my thing, but I stop in to this one every once in a while for iced coffee.  A good friend lives near this one so we'll meet here, grab some iced coffee and hang out with or without our kids in tow.  The restroom is abhorently filthy though.  Yick.

I love it here when I get here at 11 AM and the lunch rush has not hit yet. Today I ordered by phone and waltzed in and out with my Green Lemonade (a must), Sweet potato fries and a veggie burger.  So hip.  So city.  So veg.  So cheap?  (Not so much - $15.64 for those 3 items)  LOVE IT!  Want the Fifth star?  Get a BATHROOM, please.

I am so not a Cosi fan. The bread tastes like stale cardboard a minute after it cools - and g-d know what its doing inside my stomach.  The prices are high as are the caloric contents.  This particular location - inside 30th Street - is often crowded and the service is awful.  Not my thing, baby - and 2 stars is being nice.

We attended a corporate party at the DuPont country club and it was great.  The club itself seems as though it has been around for-eh-ver.  Old school ballroom decor.  Nice restooms, dancefloors, place for a band, terraces.  Good for weddings, parties and large events.  Food was surprisingly good - pasta station, carving station, crepe & dessert waffles with BIG fresh berries.  Also a sushi bar brought in by Okura in Hokessin.  Good stuff!

OK - here we go again, I thought as I hesitated outside the door of the el-cheap-o "Dollah-a-minute" Chinatown Massage joint.  The ladies inside literally came outside to convince me to come in.  "Chi-Gong", I said.  and pointed to the words "Energy Treatment $10" on the menu posting the prices.  "Chair massage?"  "No, Chi-Gong", I said.  My "therapist" (there aint no credentialing here, I am certain) Lili spoke almost no English - but I gotta say - when the  bell rang after 20 minutes of PERFECT acupressure to my neck, back, lowerback and arms, I replied "Yes, 10 more minutes, please" when she asked me if I wanted more time.  This is a legitimate place - not a "happy ending" massage parlour.  Safe, decent, and best of all if you ask for Lili - you will get a true pick-me up. She knows which meridians to use, and even gave me an auricular (ear) and scalp massage (no oil, no mess).  I am pleasantly surprised.  I expected a horror show - and this place - for a cheap Chinatown massage joint, is A-OK by me.  P.S.  Ms. Gao (Owner) if you are reading this - if you would spruce up your decor and signage - you could really have a better review from me.  I hear you are a REAL Acupuncture practitioner and that is a great thing.  Please give your place a makeover, play a little music (so we can't hear the person in the next "room") and change the lighting (florescent) and you could really have something.  I will be back to check up on you!!!

3 or 4 stars - I guess 3.5 is about right.  The shops have a "mall-like" feel and Godiva, The Body Shop, Crabtree & Evelyn, Yankee Candles, Jos. A. Bank are all represented.  There is also a (jam packed and often dirty during peak hours) food court with Saladworks, Peace-A-Pizza and Cafe Spice among many others.  It's a good place to run into during the workday - and great if you need a last minute gift from Bath & Body Works or Icky Vicky's.  Oh - and there's a med-spa on the 2nd floor and Aveda on the ground floor.  Oh - and Douglas Cosmetics.  I love them!

Never disappointed at VW - especiallyy when I split a burger with a friend (the kitchen will gladly cut it in half) so I can indulge in a 1/2 order of lobster mac & cheese.  Decadence!   No room for anthing else - except for a $14 shot of whiskey.  Mmmmn Mmmmn good!

We came here for the 3rd consecutive year to place our balloon order for our little one's birthday bash.  They were out of some of the Mylar designs we wanted.   Also the costumes for kids were NOT cheap - ours cost $24.95 - which isn't awful - but Target had similar cheesy costume for cheaper.  Masquerade definitely has way better selection of sizes and types of costumes though.  Asusual in October it is a PACKED madhouse.  We got there at 10:20 - they open at 10 - but drove by at about 9:50 AM and there were people waiting to get inside.  Wow!

While no longer owned by the Luberto family, the food is still magnificent here.  Our favorite Italian spot in the D-town area.  Try Chicken Marsala, Veal or Chicken parm, Crab Ravioli (a special - if they have it, get it) or anything in pink vodka sauce.  Delicious! And big portions to take some home.  Casual.
Bought a second Hyundai Sonata from FB (A 2012, we also have a 2006). Got about $500 in "credits" for buying a second time (whoopie!). So far, so good - we've had the car about three minutes.

Yummy treats and the ability to get a birthday cake for the office in a pinch make SPS the go-to bakery for our office.  Cupcakes can be a little dry - so get them early in the day.  They MAY be under new management - not sure as some of the signage changed.  NOTE:   IT IS NOW CALLED SWISS HAUS.

I have a love/hate relationship with DB (David's Bridal.). While I elected in the end NOT to get my bridal gown through them, my bridesmaids both got decent (cheap - but hell, they'll NEVER wear them again - let's face it) bridesmaids dresses there.  The customer service can run the gamut from "fend for yourself, bitch" to "your humble servant".  It depends on who you get and WHAT DAY AND TIME (i.e. do not TRY to get good service on a weekend in "bridal/prom" season).  Meanwhile - you can buy color swatches here for $1 a piece and go have a dress made in whatever color your bride has forced upon you.  I had my girls wear a cobalt/royal blue shade called "Royal Velvet".  They were allowed to pick any dress they wanted as long as it met 2 criteria:  1.  Had to be floor length 2.  Had to be Royal VElvet.  Surprisingly enough both gals selected strapless styles - and they are NOT small women.  They both needed fitting and the alterations were done correectly the first time.  A-men.  Thank god the weddig planning is over.  P.S.  Do NOT give them your email address, like I did, or your will be on Every frikkin' bridal/newlywed email spam list around for months and months.  My wedding was in June 2008 and I still get emails from DB related businesses.

I have to give props to the 20th Street location of Whole Foods.  They did an event with my daughter's school and we raised just under $5K.  This was an awesome gift and a great way to work with the community.  Whole Foods - you have my undying support.

Sorry, but I just was not impressed with the food.  We had several small plates - and a really bitter greens-based salad.  Also a dessert panini which sounded much better on paper than it actually tasted.  The service was fine, if a bit dis-interested,  and the decor and vibe call for a 4 or 5 star rating but the food was not worth the price, and not especially memorable.

Have been here twice - both time for work-related happy hours. Good service from the sweet Irish barkeep - Connor - and a good big shot of Tullimorew Dew.  (Sweet and smooth.)  Food is just OK.  Love the witty quotes/sayings on the blackboard that changes every day.

Andie, Amber and Especially BRIAN WONG are fantastic. The entire team at elements provides top-notch massage therapy (and OK facials - they still need work and I can explain why...) in a relaxing environment for decent prices (Not over-priced/over-hypes like Joseph Anthony, and not "budget massage" like some other places.  Definitely NOT like Massage Envy/Hand & Stone (The "USA Today" of McSpas).  Go.  See.  Brian.  Do it now.  Your body with thank you. He is a gifted healer.  I even send my 12 year old competitive athlete to him (I stay in the room with her the entire time.) and it has helped her so much.  We love you, Massage Envy. When you get "rich and famous" please don't forget us!

I agree with David B.  I am lucky enough to live near Viso's (cousin's of Termini??) in Aston and Testa's is OK - but not the best I've had.  That said the cakes here are great for an office function and they can customize easily.  Chocolate dipped cannoli were slight soggy.  Breakfast "Danish" pastry were heavier than some.  OK but not awesome.

4 for the food and 2 for the service.  A friends and I had lunch (which came out to about $90 - and we ordered 3 non-alcoholic drinks that were $8 each.  OUCH!).  Keshia, our server was very nice, but clearly overwhelmed as she had the entire upstairs all to herself to manage.  Our lunch took far to long, and my friend was stressing out b/c she had to go back to work.  Meanwhile, the salad with petite jeweled vegetables was great (the veggies taste like candy!) and the veggie (pasta-free, cheese-free) lasagne was good too - but it had a bit of a "harissa-like" spice that crept up on me after a few bites.  The side of tabouleh was lightly lemony and sublime.  Great food, excellent drinks but too high of a price point and too slow for lunch-rush service.   Try the Persephone - a souped-up mojito with 10 cane rum, pomegranate and a bit of jalapeno. (I got mine virginized and it rocked!)

MUCH better experience this time - very friendly service and almost NO LINE - but it was 4 PM on a HOT (100 degree) Summer Saturday.  My 11 year old got a TRENTA aka "vat" of green iced tea.  We needed this!

I love Trader Joe's at holiday times for inexpensive food-oriented gifts or for throwing a party (great frozen treats and hors d'oeuvres ), I also buy a few frozen lunch meals here like the Shells with Brie and Asparagus and the "Reduced Guilt" Mac 'n Cheese.  That said, I can't give TJ's 5 stars because I can not get ALL of my grocery shopping needs met here.  Yeah, yeah, you can get bread, milk and eggs and WAY overpriced meat here - but I can't do that.  I shop at TJ's for "fun food", Whole foods for "organic" food and Giant for "normal middle class" food.  Glad we live in the USA and have options.

I can not say enough great things about Gene and his staff.  My frames that I bought 2 years ago still look good as new. Plus he adjusts them for me whenever I drop in.  The next time I need glasses (probably next year) THIS is where I will go.  It's GREAT.

Wow - such awful reviews for this place.  Sure it's sky-high prices - but you are paying for the convenience factor.  Decent produce, frozen foods, dairy, meat and prepared foods.  I go here for emergency purchases, certainly not to do my everyday shopping.  GLad they exist.  Grocery stores are few & far between in Center City.
Go Phillies!!!  Let's win this year's World Series.  OK? "Nuff said.

Took el Kiddo (who is now 9) back to Comacst for the Christmas 2013 show - and it was very nice this year.  Some parts were the same as in prior year's and at least one segment seemed new.  The show is once per hour (sit on the floor unless you are lucky enough to snag a bench) and lasts about 18 minutes.  Free and fun for kids and families.
New owners?  Looks a little nicer inside.  Good values - but be picky and inspect for mold or old berries.  Pre-cut veggies and some take-away items also.  Convenient.

Excellent lunch-time fare - but man, oh, man the crowds at 12:45 are just CRAZY. Meanwhile our order came quickly and the gals up front and hard working gals and guys in the back really know how to WORK IT.  Excellent Customer service. Great Food. - I have the Udon Salad and a Green Lemonade.  I'll be back - and SOON!  (But next time at 11:30 or 11:45 - I can't deal with the crowds.

A nice, relatively new and very clean Qdoba with amazingly no line at 12:15 on a Monday. I zipped in and out with my taco salad bowl.  Good stuff - no issues.  3 ladies running the front counter were pleasant and delivered great customer service.  I will be back - and likely soon.

I was a patient of Dr. Dubin's (JFK Dental) before they moved here and eventually he retired.  Leanne - the office manager is just terrific.  We moved to the "burbs - so I don't come here any more - but I was a patient for years and had some great cleanings by caring hygienists and staff.  Love. This. Practice.  (Miss Dr. Dubin, though - he is living the life in Mexico now.)

I am radiating goodness.  i will say it again.  I am radiating Goodness!  I knew right away that Brian was going to be an exceptional massage therapist.  Not only does he take great care of his clients, he is very knowledgeable about numerous techniques. I can not wait to come back again as see him for treatments.  I feel amazing! So glad to have discovered elements.  And Andie (sp??) at the front desk is terrific, too. So happy!
Ditto and Tritto wehat they already said!  I usually get the (enormous) platter. You get what you get and you don't get upset!  Mama's Falafel is good, too.  (Right down the street.)

A lovely old-school, well-run condo with modest-to-high monthly fees - and a pool in the summertime.  Garage parking is available for an extra charge - but there is plenty of free parking in the lot out front.  There are 3 buildings and you can walk to "downtown" Old Jenkintown and to SEPTA - but I'd  get lazy and drive.

Still some of the best coffee in the city - and still a line (that moved pretty quickly) every morning in Suburban Station.  Pricey but so much better than Dunkin or Charbucks.  The Café au Lait and Lattes (the will used your favorite type of cows or nut milk) are so delicious.  Like dessert in a cup for breakfast (and I don't even get any flavored syrups - just a plain latte or au lait is so creamy and sweet.)  Yum!!!!

CHOP is a godsend - and we just HAPPEN to live in Philly.  They have the BEST doctors in the UNIVERSE who are specifically trained in rare illnesses and conditions of children.  I pray we don't have to go here often - but we already have had one harrowing experience which involved taking our daughter (then 4) to the CHOP ER after she fell from a shopping cart in Superfresh.  She was bleeding from her nose - but did not hit her head.  WE were seen in triage within 3 minutes and then waiting about 10 minutes to be put into an ER room.  Then the real waiting began.  The Nurse saw us right away - but we had to wait 40 minutes to see the doctor.  By then the bleeding had stopped and she was pronounced OK - and she was acting her "normal" self again.  Meanwhile we REALLY had to wait for the billing information to be processed.  That was a drag because now it was after 10 PM   (we arrived at 7:30 or so initially) and our tuckered out 4 yo just wanted to go home.  (and so did we.)   And they spelled her name wrong - more waiting to correct that.  So 5 stars for great doctors and state-of-the art facilities (the give you a pager prior to triage) and 2-3 for lousy administrative skills.

Now our dd is 7 and this place is still a multi-generational family fave. The pizzas, pasta and (my fave) veal parm are served in huge portions (prices are not cheap but an entree for $14.95 feeds 2 easily.)  Oh - and don't miss the cappucino here - it really is a well-kept secret - what a treat!  Be prepared to wait on weekend nights.
I agree (as I usually do) with Alice L.  This is pretty much what we did growing up as kids.  The park is great in Spring & Summer - but at Xmas t is a historical treat.    Great park!

I am never disappointed with Elements.  My daughter and I both get massages here with Brian Wong and recently I tried a facial with Candace which was very relaxing and used (good) Jan Marini products.  The front desk is great - especially Holly and Brittany. There was a lady who was not great but she seems to be gone.  Prices are fair and the service is just terrific.  If you want to see a truly gifted healer go see Brian Wong at Elements in Media.

Can't say enough great things about Maki Motors.  Maki did a complete interior detail on my old vehicle and made it look like a new car inside.  Amazing.  Not cheap but to me, well worth it.  He was prompt, polite and thorough. I will call him again when it's time for an exterior detail.  Great work!

Due to our just OK experience before, I was very reluctant to try Square 1682 again - but a voucher for a free app (we chose the Lemon Hummus - very good BTW) and a close friend who works near there convinced me to return.  We sat upstairs with Keshia again - and this time service was great because there were only 2-3 tables occupied.  The chopped salad at $13 is a bit steep for lunch - but fresh and tasty. But I wish I'd had the salmon (my friend got it and it looked - and she said it was - wonderful).  Close to 4 stars this time but for the price ($45 for lunch for 2 no dessert, no booze) is just too high.  This is clearly an expense account place. And for a "hotel restaurant" it's great.

This is a review for corporate/banquet events and not for staying at the hotel. I attended a 150 - 200 person conference here ate it was very well run and the food, service and facilities were far better than similar hotels at similar price points.  The dinner was just OK (salmon was kinda dry) but the buffet lunch was actually GOOD.  I have eaten many corporate "rubber chicken" dinners - and the Crowne Plazaz K of P handled our group very well.  No issues with audio/visual, A/C temperature was good (not too hot, not too cold).  I would definitely consider holding a future event here.

I love the larder for bulk foods and gift baskets.  Back in the late '80's and '90's they were the only game in town.  They have teas, coffees, spices, grains and candies.  It's alot of fun to poke around - though nowadays you can get alot of these items more cheaply on line or at Wegmans (There WAS NO WEGMANS back in the day).  The ladies who originially opened it (they've been around a looooong time) I think no longer own it.  But the gals working there are always pleasant and helpful.  If you are in D-town and need a gift basket of food items or just want some yummy treats for yourself, check out the Larder for sure!

I have past by this stripmall bar a bazillion times but never wanted to go in. Last night my friend who is a Delco native, dragged me in there for her old high school reunion.  The bar was PACKED with middle-aged ex-Sun Valley graduates.  Renee, the lovely and gorgeous hostess, sat us at a table.   At 9 PM a live duo began jamming out 70's and 80's covers.  They were pretty good, too.  Best of all, we even got Mary, our overworked server, to smile.  She brought us some surprisingly delicious food including a Mammoth-sized wedge salad.   I literally ate a head of lettuce.  Lettuce and vodka.  I was a happy camper.  So pleasantly surprised by this neighborhood jawn with solid food, drinks, live music and terrific service.  We love you, Mary!

This is the Giant near Arch Road and 202 in East Norriton. Salad bar, Hot food bar with decent fried chicken. I come here when I need an inexpensive lunch and am too lazy to pack from home.  Not luxurious and the sushi bar is just OK, but it's fine.  Glad it's here. Nicer than ShopRite.

We stopped in (had a 6:15 reservation) as a party pf 5 for Opera Night (a $4 charge PER PERSON so be aware) on a crisp autumnal Monday.  Not too crowded (the Monday night and $4 charge helped with that I am certain!) and the service was just fine.  Note:  Please tell people when they call on Mondays about the $4 charge.  We had no idea until we saw it on the menu.  We heard 3 arias by Heidi and one included a very talented tenor - can't remember his name.  Caprese salad makes a good app for 2 or 3 to share - delicious fresh mozzarella balls and a mound of lettuce (lettuce??) and fresh basil in the center.  Entrees included an uber-rich gnocchi Gorgonzola, spaghetti carbonara, ravioli marinara, chicken parm (for the 9 year old - and she loved it) and my dish - Shrimp Scampi.  Delicious and HUGE - nearly everyone took something home.  No room for dessert - but other people's looked great.  We love Fellini's and are so happy that they are now open for LUNCH on weekends - so maybe, just maybe, we can take our parents there next time.  Since then we have been back for weekend lunch a few times and it is very good (Try the Linguine alla Vongole).  The only complaint?  My 9 year old does not like their hot chocolate.  Says it is bitter.  However, I love their cappucinos!

This is one of the best CVS's I go to.  Love that Extra Care card with it's Extra Bucks.  Also if you have a prescription at any CVS you can re-fill it at any other CVS.  This Doylestown branch (near the train station) is clean and well run with friendly staff.   I'll be back!
So grateful to have these guys on our street - mulch, gardening supplies, rakes, hardware.  NEEDED!!!  Also propane for our grill.  Definitely check them out.

Large Starbucks right near 476 - so fairly convenient but the trafic at rush hour is bad.  Drive thru is available but we opted to order inside (and use the restrooms).  No issues.  Got in and out fairly quickly.  Parking lot was PACKED.  Alex (cashier/barista) was very good. Seating area was clean and comfy.

If you liked Vic's in the OLD Days (when Vic & his wife first opened) you'll like Jay's.  Jay (and Martin) worked with Vic for a while.  Many of the crazy (and a bit over-sauced - get your sauce on the side - problem solved), calorie-laden specialty rolls are just like Vic's but sub lobster for crab and have different names.  My first visit (a few minutes ago) I ordered 2 things - tuna dumplings (divine) - and the eggplant lady.  Both are apps. - but that was just perfect for little ole me.  The $7.50 order of 2 hand-flattened tuna pouches came bursting with a slightly sweet, slightly spicy mixture of lobster (real) and crab (fake) salad with masago and avocado.  Creamy, fattening, non-traditional goodness.  The $4.25 eggplant lady (I will re-order this for sure) had 2crispy-thin tempura slices of purple japanese eggplant.  The eggplant was luscious, crisp slice was topped with chopped shrimp and (fake) crab salad (more avocado, masago, kewpie - like my hips needed THAT!), topped with sliver-sliced avo and eel sauce.  (Next time - no sauce.)  This is NOT a place to get traditional nigiri.  (The tamago is frozen, and there's no way that Inari is home made)  It is a place for "fun-food" rolls as a treat.  Purists won't like it, but Phat-Philly types should LOVE it here.  The service was Excellent - but Jay is new and eager to please.  I anticipate visiting againsoon - and I'd bet money on it that the 6-seat sushi bar (and tables for about 14 more - It's bigger than Vic's - andthey actually serve you your drinks) will be MUCH more crowded.  So in summary:  Sushi-newbie?  Great place for you.  Fresh-fish, sashimi purist?  Probably not.  For me - there is a time and place for everything.  Tonight was my time for the 2 month old Jay's.  I sure hope the quality doesn't deteriorate in 6 months.

A surprisingly GOOD experience with Dorjee (our Teppan chef) and our server. Excellent Sunday-lunchtime service for our table of 10, celebrating a birthday.  The lunch menu is a good value - the "Lunch Boat" - I chose salmon - a teeny piece of salmon - comes with sashimi, edamame, tempura (all in small portions - perfect) and soup/salad.  My daughter (age 12) devoured the tuna tataki app. and a plate of nigiri.  We enjoyed the food and service, while watching the onion volcano. Nostalgic.

A hair's bredth away from 5 stars - the food, deluxe cocktails and service are 5 star - the cramped, crowded digs and icky single bathroom make it down to 4.  We stopped in for drinks and were not at all disappointed. Wonderful bartenders who explained every exotic sounding thing we asked about.  Great selection of draught beers and ales (even a cider on tap).  Love it!  GET THE BURGER!

Wow - nobody's yelped Poor Richards yet?   This branch is the "new location" - the original location is on State Street right in the middle of Doylestown.  For 35-40 plus years Poor Richards has been a Doylestown staple.  Poor Richards is a unique shop.  Is it a gift shop?  An antique shop?  A craft lovers place?  A furniture store?  It's abit of all of these things.  A great place for tourists and locals alike to poke around and make discoveries. Great decorative items for home and hearth - and often you'll find the perfect gift here, too.

A fine kettle of fish, indeed!  Otolith provides sustainable seafood (much from Alaska) - in my case, specifically salmon as a CSA-type "Share" to my group of women from the PWCG (Philadelphia Women's Culinary Guild.)  This year, I am sharing my share through Panache Foods - a home-delivery service of fresh, local produce.  Can't wait to get my individually-wrapped 1 lb packs of fresh, delcious, heathy, sushi-grade salmon!  YUM!

#ServiceStarShoutOut  Maki is amazing - I had him come a second time - this time for an exterior detail (and he vaccuumed the interior also - which I always need). I really hope to use him again on my new car once it needs detailing.  #ServiceStarShoutOut

A strong 4 stars for Village Whiskey from me! A good friend and fellow yelper squeaked into the bar at around 8:45 PM on a snowy Tuesday.  There just happened to be 2 great seats waiting for us.  (I don't know if this place is worth a long wait)  Service from Sasha was excellent and she is so friendly and helpful. We started off with an order of fried pickles and shared the DELICIOUS pickled artichokes.  (These are the best thing I tasted that night and worth a re-order)  My companion had a delectable veggie burger topped with a fried egg (Wowza!) and guacamole.  The lady next to us had a beef burger topped with an egg as well and they sure know how to fry an egg here! (Incidentally the couple next to us also shared the duckfat fries topped with shortribs and cheese sauce - looked so heavy - like a heart attach on a plate.  I bet it ROCKED!  Anyhow, we continued with an order of "tater tots' that were so rrefined they'd put Ore-Ida to shame.  And an order of pickled golden and red beets that I wound up barely touching and had packed up to go.  The best thing to me?  The delicious lemon oil-scented whipped ricotta that accompaied the pickled dishes.  Also a tasty tapenade and fresh, thin slices of baguette.  Nice!  I will definitely come back here.  What a cute (albeit small) "retro" feeling place.

Even with the mixed reviews I had been wanting to try Spasso for over a year. Last night - a slow-as-heck Monday night was the night to do it.  While this may be a truly 3 star place, I am giving them a 4 for the excellent service we got (along with $4 cape-codders) at the bar.  The caprese salad was not the best - it was served with iceberg lettuce (who does that??) and was swimming in low-grade olive oil. For $5 on happy hour it was fine.  Normally it's $8.50 and I would not order it again. (Which is a shame because I love a good caprese.) Bartender was cute and very personable also.  Dinner was better - we were seated right away (dining room was only about 1/4 full) and our (young, pretty) server was perfectly fine.  Food was actually great - veal with spinach and crab-meat served with al dente fettuccine.  Large portion so I took 1/2 home.  My friend had veal parm - which looked average.  (Veal was deep fried underneath the sauce and cheese. Chocolate mousse cake was OK for dessert but the cappuccino was Excellent.  I can certainly understand why some don't like it here as there are many unprofessional chinks in the Spasso armor.  The dining room below the chair rail MUST be re-painted.  It is a deep brown color and everywhere a chair has bumped there is a white chip out of the paint (looks bad).  Also the female servers and hostesses tend to collect in a gaggle at the hostess stand or by the kitchen and chat (they were bored and it was slow ) - or out back for a smoke.  Not truly a 4 star place - morel like 3, 3.5 but we had a great night and I am feeling generous.  I'll be back for happy hour for sure.
Always 5 star advice from the Petrillos about what type of dryer to buy or when to replace a dishwasher.  Got appliance questions?  They know their stuff.  It's a family business that I support.

OK - there are many, many things wrong with La Creperie - but I will start with the positives.  1.  Our server Christine - was incredibly sweet, attentive and accurate. 4 stars for her!  2.  The actual crepe itself is tasty - not too greasy nor too dry and is made of white flour (not buckwheat which the true Breton crepes are made). 3.  Our large party of 8 was accomodated with separate checks  OK where to start on the bad stuff.  1.  The ancient rattan chairs are incredibly uncomfortable.  So much so, that I had to switch to a wooden chair (there are a few available so try to sit at a table with the cheap wood chairs).  2.  They got my order wrong (A salade Le Melange with no onion and fresh tomato subbed for sundried).  Once corrected the fresh tomatoes were rotten and tasted so bad that I could not eat the salade.  3.  The prices are INSANE for the quality.  My Lemon & Sugar crepe was $6.75 - which is OBSCENE.  The rotten tomato salade was $12.  That's over $20 when you add tip & tax for a salade and a dessert crepe - no beverage.  4.  The restaurant was dead-empty except for our large party of 8 from when we arrived at 7:00 until after 9:30 when we left.  (This could be viewed as a pro and con in one.)  I think there is a REASON people are not coming here.  Yes the quality is better than "crepe maker" in 30th Street station - but the crepes at Profi's in Reading Terminal Market as just as good, way cheaper and (if you can deal with crowds 7 stools) possibly just as comfortable of an atmosphere.  My next stop with be Beau Monde (who's prices are even HIGHER) for true Breton crepes.  I pray I am not disappointed.  Sorry La Creperie, but ya let me down.  Save for Christine.  She's been there 3 years - one night a week - and she is terrific.  She even adjusted my bill for the inedible salade.  (I feel so very French spelling salad with an "e").

I shop at the Wilmington TJ's when I am working near there.   The parking lot gets crazy around lunchtime on weekdays - but other than that the lines are never ridiculously long and the staff is great.  So friendly.  They have lots of cool "fun" foods at TJ's.

3-4 stars, even, depending on what you order.  The "Dark Side of the Moon" cake looked great - but alas, I could not justify the calories.  I settled on a DELICIOUS and huge salad of 4 grilled shrimp, fresh mozz., roasted red peppers, tomatoes & cukes atop a bed of crisp (not at all rusty) greens.  So perfect!  DH enjoyed the french onion soup but IMO it was not as good as the FOSoup we get in our fave NYC diner.  But for Wilmington?  This is a darn good diner with a wide variety of choices.

I rarely ever get to the Comcast Center anymore - so today a friend and I met at 11:40 AM - just in time to beat the lunch rush and the long lines.  La Scala made her vegetable sandwich on focaccia (huge and fresh) to order, as did they my chicken florentine - no cheese.  HUGE portions. - Worth the 12-15 minute wait for the cooked-to-order hot meals.  $10 a pop after tax - but big enough for lunch and dinner!

It's all about the Dr. and location. We saw Dr. Nordone in the MEDIA, PA location and my 16 year old had all 4 wisdom teeth removed under general anesthesia and had no ill effects.  She received great care.  But I would never go into Philly for this.

A delight ful lunch at a table (A TABLE!!!!!) at 11:45 AM on a Tuesday - before the crowds began, along with a stellar veggie burger (with guacamole) and divine pickled beets with heavenly (or devil-ish??) lemon ricotta has made me give them that ellusive 5th star.  A friend and I also shared the tater tots with a smoked onion creme fraiche dip (yum-city!) and our service was spot-on!  The bathroom was even cleaner - again - we were there at 11:45 AM on a Tuesday. By the time we left at 12:45 PM - the place was PACKED.  Go today!  Get a burger!  Get some pickles. (Beets, green beans or tomatoes - all are great.)  Get happy!

Our office uses Crocodile Catering (and a few other companies) because that are reliable (never late - which is key here) and have "safe" choices.  Salads are fresh and sandwiches are plentiful.  We usually get a cold breakfast (bagel platter and cut fruit bowl or a Sandwich/Wrap platter with salads for lunch.  I have not tried any of their hot food options.  A solid option for business/corporate catering.

OMG!!!!  We ate here (again) tonight - party of 7 including my 4 year old daughter.  Reasonable prices and just terrific Italian-American fare.  Everything from my little one's hand tossed mini Margarita pizza to classic Chicken Parm to my MIL's Lobster ravioli (a special) was wonderful.  Friendly service and just GREAT!!  Everyone in Dublin and Doylestown (and all points in between) should know about this fabulous find!

I agree with Meg C - completely.  It is fun to browse here and get ideas, but for practical and price I shop elsewhere.  I have, however, ogtten a few novelty pans here for seasonal cakes.  I also got a great off-set spatula here years ago before I had opened my culinary eyes wider.

GORGEOUS.  Shi-Shi.  Pricey.  That about sums up floribunda.  They will do large or small event floral design.  Fresh or silks arrangements.  They do great things for rich people who need home decor.  The ladies who run the show are nice.  The do have a parking lot but it gets full quickly.  Check them out.
Saget;'s customer service - especially from John - the manager - is top notch. They hand deliver and pick up my cleaning every week (or other week) right to my door.  LOVE THEM!

I stand by my words - I have now tried 6 local dry cleaners and Victory is the BEST - bar none. I have even used their tailoring services several times (twice for small repairs on an emergency basis) for my daughter's fragile and expensive figure skating dresses and costumes (lots of sparkly things that can be pulled off.  The tailor-lady (I wish I knew her name!) is just amazing and has literally saved my kids neck (she adjusted a neckline at the last minute) just before a performance.  Missy and the other ladies behind the counter are terrific. And the cute golden that comes in from time to time.  LOVE. IT. HERE. As much as one can reasonably love a dry-cleaner - without it becoming weird.  Or creepy.  Anyhow - you need dry-cleaning or alterations? Prom gown stuff?  Wedding gown stuff?  Big, heavy comforters or rugs that if you try to clean at home will break your machine?  Stains? This is the place.

Another wonderful (and huge portion sized) meal - this time for lunch on a Sunday at Fellinis.  The Shrimp Scampi, Veal Parm, Caprese Salad, Chicken Scarp and Linguine with Crabmeat (in a red sauce) were all terrific.  Great service, and re-done restrooms!  Love it here.
No issues yet - and I have completed 2 orders so far. Open on Sunday!!! Drop off by 11 and pick up by 4.  10% discount if you pay at drop off.  So far, so good.

5 stars for our service today from Lallo. Also the new dinining room is great.  Some of the BEST cappucino we have ever had.  The only thing preventing 5 stars?  Too loud!  Crazy-loud - even at lunch time.  (The ceilings maybe?)
While our beverage service was fine, the downgrade goes toward the filthy restroom.  It was truly awful.  Please clean the restrooms more often and more thoroughly.  Ick.

Thank G-d for CHOP - the Children's Hospital of Philadelphia - one of the finest Children's Hospitals in the nation.  Yes, mistakes are made, no hospital is perfect - but when our (then) 4 year old fell out of a shopping cart and nearly broke her nose their emergency and triage teams were speedy, accurate and so caring.  The only bad part?  The administration - we waited over an hour for them to get our insurance info - with a very tired 4 year old.  We just wanted to leave.  This could have been handled better.  But the care we received?  Top-Notch!

This is NOT the Beauty Nail at 223 Pennell nor is it Sky Nail sown the block (next shopping center). Beauty Nail is a relatively clean, well-run, inexpensive ($10 for a traditional mani, $25 for gel) salon.  I did not get a pedicure here. Tina was very competent and I came when the salon was not busy (3 PM on a Wednesday).  $10 minimum for credit cards and you must tip in cash. I will be back - but my go-to salon for now is China Nail in downtown Media - closer to home for me.  Netiher of these salons compare to 4 sisters (the new one at 22 & Chestnut) in Philly.  I love it there! But Media manis are cheaper than Philly manis - at most places.

Alicia - you crack me up! As a CB West Alum I felt safe enough about not seeing any North Penn alum, but I digress.  Back in the day Michael's was a great inexpensive place to grab coffee and some decent food - especially breakfast and diner fare.  Better than Perkins and more homestyle.  Now that I guess I am (ahem) an adult, and along with the years, Michael's has lost its luster.  Could use a redo on the decor.  Food is still decent diner grub.  And inexpensive.   I would feel OK taking my family here for brunch or lunch.  Not sure if I want to relive any late-night antics from my youth, though.

Pina's Pizza has 2 or 3 locations around Doylestown, but this location in Chalfont is where my family are regulars. So much so that Anna Maria set out Diet Cokes for my parents before the car was even parked.  She knows us all by name. So the service is always 5 star.  The food is good - solid Pizzeria staples and cheese-steaks.  Deliciously garlicky garlic knots (with chucks of garlic - you will need to brush after wards!) and fresh salads.  The cheese on the caprese is fresh and wonderful.    Portions are generous.  We love it here and return over and over.  Plus - Anna Maria gives us mini canolli for dessert. Wow!

I hear this place is owned by Chau (Nail by Chau around the corner - which I used to go to quite often for manis only).  This place is downright grungy.  Went here twice for manis.  No way I'd get a pedi here.  You get what u pay for!

I can't say enough good things about Victory - the folks who own the place and those who work here treat me so well (and candy for my 9 year old when we come).  Even their dog is wonderful.  And they clean and alter clothing just right!  Prices are high - so come on a discount day or pay in cash for 10% off.  (Stil pricey after that!)

A true CLASSIC dive-bar - but luckily the low, low prices ($4.95 for a patty melt - no fries) and decent "greasy short order" cookery match the dated '70's décor.  Gretchen is a great bartender and the locals all gather round to down a few beers and grab a quick smoke out back.  NOT a yuppy-Media-bar at all. This is one of the TRUE Media originals. Family owned - great customers and low-brow food and décor.  Just what I need when I want a CHEAP drink.

Fellini's Media is a BYO located in an historic building - the site of an old Cigar Shop.  The place is PACKED especially on weekends - we showed up (no reservation) on a Saturday night at 7:45 PM and lucked out.  The placed was a cacophony (sp?) inside, but we managed to snag one of the 2 outdoor tables on a September night that was not hot and not cold.  FAB!  Rose and Chris (and about 3 other server/bussers) were terrific - and man, were they workin' it.  Our bread, butter, ice water and bruschetta arrived right away.  Soon after, our HUGE, moderately priced entrees - Chicken Contadina for the husband, Penne Sophia Loren for me.  (Took half home - so nice, I'll eat it twice.)  A great spot for sure, in Media.

I am not much of a fast food eater - and I don't touch hot dogs, but on a whim I ordered a (nearly $10) patty melt here - a calorie bomb for sure - but it was tasty.  Just too greasy for me.  I skipped any fried sides and dared not order a (1000 calorie) shake.  I think my cholesterol quotient for 2021 has been achieved.

Note:  No credit cards.  Also they close at 10 or 10:30 on weekdays.  I stopped in after the place I wanted to go to was closing at 8 PM.  It was 7:40 PM and I needed dinner and a quiet place to take a 1 hour conference call.  The young peppy (gorgeous) server was attentive and kind. I did not get the $3.89 breakfast (served all day) deal - but that is alot of food and I will consider it when I want breakfast.  Mashed potatoes are from a box (so the server said) so I got a baked potato, ffrozen green beans and a surprisingly OK steak dinner.  Plus a large diet coke with Vanilla syrup in it.  (They can also put cherries in your soda).  Very reasonable CASH only prices. Dated decor - but I bet it's fun when you are wasted on a Friday or Saturday night.  It's been here for YEARS.

5 Star service from Vera (hostess) and our amazing and attentive server, Kaitlyn.  Wow - we were seated outside on a hot, sticky, humid Father's Day and Kaitlyn was just on point!  Our party of 6 truly enjoyed the sweet potato fries and fried brussels sprouts (sans bacon) which we all shared and wolfed down.  For entrees we enjoyed a variety of burgers (brioche buns), flatbread, "power bowl" and a "healthy" salmon on pita called "The Edinburgh".  I would totally come back here.  Great place for families at lunch and a different, noisier crowd at night.

OK, I am torn between 3 & 4 stars.  Food is 3,  Drinks are 4.  I would definitely come back for drinks - especially the "Blush" a rum, sugar, lime and pink grapefruit juice cocktail.  So refreshing.  They also make a REAL "Dark & Stormy" that packs a robust gingery punch.  Soooooo good.  Meanwhile, 4 of us lovely ladies had drinks & dinner here last night.
