Service was good by the servers, but the bus "girl" was too aggressive in removing plates before we were finished.  She got the hint the 2nd or 3rd time we guarded our plates.  "No, we're not finished quite yet".  After a round of refreshing drinks (best part of the evening for me, anyway), we started with a $3 bar snack of duck liver, spread thinly on 2 crisp toast points.  It was a little gamey.  Would not re-order.  The best appetizer by far was the gnocchi.  Now I realize the reviews here on that gnocchi are mixed, but we told them light on the oil and it was great.  Served with REAL morel mushroom.  2 of us split one order and another lady had an order all to herself.  Honey & Whiskey glazed petite chicken wings were very tasty, but also small and boney.  (Large portion, small wing size.)  2 of us, myself included, had the tilapia po boy.  My friend loves this sandwich, i  thought it was just OK.  I wanted to try the lobster BLT special, but the night we went (a Sunday there were NO SPECIALS at all.)  Quel Dommage.  After our meals, we had a dessert course.  A nice cheese plate came with red grapes, walnuts and 3 generous cheese selections including Morbier and Stilton.  The rest of the gals shared a chocolate/peanut butter mousse, which was chilled, dense and not at all goopy.  It was served in a perfect circle with a dulce du leche beneath it.  Not too peanutty, but full of milky chocolate flavor.  The booths are made of a hard wood and look great but are small for a party of 4 and not comfortable.  This can actually help the restaurant to turn tables - as you won't sit too long (ha, ha!).  The bar was packed at 8:30 PM on a Sunday.  Nice to see in this crappy economy.  I will return to P&K but it is not a holy grail. Oh, and it's not cheap.  (but not horrible) $40 each for the 4 of us.  Oh, and we love the "pabbit" logo - pig/rabbit.  Reminds us of the divided we fail logo where the Democratic Donkey and Republican Elephant are merged.  CUTE.  Nice job!  Please don't let it slide.
Chicken Caesar salad and Matzoh Ball Soup (sans balls) were both great and delivered to my door by a caring friend.  I would definitely try them again.
2 words are all you need to know:  Strawberry. Shortcake.  End of story. Has been serving up law firm cakes for years.  Decades even.  Yes, please!

Stopped in on a whim for a quick bite and boy am I ever glad!  They have alot of great Korean food (bi-bim bap with tofu is a winner!) as well as sandwiches and salads.  The owner/lady/cashier is a doll.  Love it here.

I loathe McDonald's and fast food in general, but I did go here once out of sheer desparation, hunger and broke-ass-ed-ness.  I got a $1.00 McChicken Sandwich, no pickles - It came to $1.07 and I just barely had the change scraped together.  What a humbling experience.  I pray it won't happen again.

We arrived just before Happy Hour (5 pm) officially starts and what an amazing evening of food, drinks and stellar service we experienced.  We began with expertly mixed drinks, tasty devilled eggs and always terrific pickled beets. Service from Katelyn was just perfect, but what really stood out was when Candace presented us with those delightful pickled beets, served in a mason jar on a beautiful wood platter accompanied by delectable whipped ricotta and olive tapanade.  We also sank our teeth into a well cooked yet juicy burger on a potato roll with cheddar, lettuce, tomato and house made dressing.  Recalled that backyard barbecue from childhood.  I am not a burger person, but Village Whiskey after 10 years, is still nailing it.  We love you, Candace!!!! Clearly, after 21 years in the biz, you KNOW what you're doing.  Brava!!!

Had not been to Fellini's in a few years - yes years. Went with a group of 5 ladies about a month ago and again tonight. We sat in Juana's section both times - and Juana is a terrific server.  The food can vary from a 3 to a 5 depending on what you choose.  The burrata appetizer (special) and caprese (on the main menu) are always safe and delicious lower-carb choices.  The pastas are terrific but alas, I can't do the carbs any more.  Solid "classic" Italian-American dishes.

A nicer ambience than El Primo (right behind it) but higher prices, too. We had a muy authentico lunch including excellent Guacamole Morita, Tacos al Pastor (terrific flavor and the tortillas were fresh) and a sope on a scrumptious home-made masa base.  Many choices of meats and great veggies.  The star of the show was the whompin'-huge Burrito Suizo ($14 but 2 people can easily share it).  Friendly service and a great choice for super-tasty Mexican fare.
Went in to get passport pictures taken. Their camera was broken.  I left and went to Walgreen's nearby.

There's a very special place in my heart for the crummy ole 'WYCK.  First of all - they served me drinks when I was about 15/16 years old - but that was many years ago - I won't say HOW many.  So a star for the underage mem'ries.  It's also the place I had my first ever Rob Roy.  You can get all the old school cocktails here - and beers on tap and in bottles.  The food is surprisingly good and safe.  They used to serve a tasty cheese ravioli - but that was a long time ago - not sure if they still do.  But man, that Rob Roy - what was I thinking????
Pros:  Drive Thru  Cons:  Hurried service and over crowded.  Your typical Starbucks -not bad and not outstanding.

This is far and away the BEST Dry Cleaners in the area - and I have tried 4 or 5 other places.  Service (with a smile) is prompt and courteous - they even let my 9 year old used the (staff only) restroom once during an emergency.  Cute dog is there during the day.  My clothes are already clean, pressed and ready for pick-up.  Love it here!

Year after year, week after week, Victory cleaners gets it right. Every time.  I actually look forward to (what????) dropping off and picking up my dry cleaning to chat with Missy and the other lovely ladies.  The owner is (very cute - ahem) terrific, too and even worked with me when I lost my job.  Tip - Bring cash and pay in advance for 10% off. Or - Ladies Day is Tuesday (I forget which day is men's day) and your order is 10% off.  Excellent service. I have tried 7 (yes, seven) local dry cleaners and even though they are not the closest one to my house, I go out of my way to come here.  Seriously - they're that good.

We refer to Masquerade as "The BALLOON Store" because for us - that's mostly why we come.  They do balloons for all our parties (Helium Latex and Mylar.)  The latex Balloons come in a wide variety of colors at two for 75 cents.  Mylar are 1.99 each.  My daughter also loves the large selection of toys here.  Warning:  During the Hallowe'en rush this place is INSANELY busy.  Call ahead or come in ahead to pre-order prior to pick up.

I had been a couple of times to the Bazter's in Paoli - so I was surprised to see a Baxters in Malvern.  This location has a large bar area and multiple dining areas.  Friendly servers (Tracy was a doll) and cheap (5 wings for $2.75) happy hour specials.  Decent French Onion soup and good strong cocktails.  (I had a Tanqueray and Tonic with lime.)  Not gourmet - but for a bar, it's just fine.
Came on a slow holiday Sunday and the place was empty and just did not appeal. Soft serve was available.  We may try again another time.

OK - there's a brand new (about 3 months old)  Wings to Go on the North East corner of 15th & Vine (where the Korean Deli used to be).  They serve Wings, Boneless Wings, Chicken tenders, Fried Shrimp, Quesedillas and Chili along with about 20 different dipping sauces from Mild, Medium & Hot to Suicide and Homicide.    We tried the tenders and Buffalo Shrimp (so good, so greasy, so what!) along with the Honey Barbecue and Golden Garlic Parmesan sauces.  As junk foods go - I am not a "wing man" (er, wing woman??) but the shrimp were fresh-fried and so tasty.  They are steps from my home so I bet we'll be back.  My 4 year old just loved the shrimp - to the exclusion of the boneless wings that we ordered for her.  She just wanted to eat shrimp.  Next time we'll get 15!!!  Best for take out - but there are a few small booths and tables.  The owner, Angela is a sweetie and very hard working.  I sure hope they make it!

Well, Jay was not here tonight and I bet he'd freak if he was. The place has gone downhill - and quickly.  My tuna dumplings were stuffed with Kani Salad (fake crab) not lobster as shown on the menu.  The weird, overbearing, barely-english-speaking waitress leaned in sooooo close to me it was a BIG violation of my personal space.  To top it off, she cleared my plates and brought a check - assuming I was done.  I was actually contemplating ordering 1 more roll or a piece or something - but i was so put off, I just paid the bill and left.  The 2 sushi guys behind the counter were friendly enough - but they were so busy filling takeout orders (dead for eat-in, busy for take-out) that their work was just SLOPPY.  I am unimpressed, Jay.  Get it back together!  You have some great items on the menu.  They need to be executed better - less kani stick and more REAL seafood, please.  .

I agree with Joy G.  The cannolli are filled to order, the taralli are the real deal, sfolliatelle,  EVERYTHING is delicious and amazing.  Be sure to order in advance for holidays like Xmas and Easter - they get BUSY.  Can't wait to visit the original location.
Need to clean the restrooms, aisles and seats. GROSS.

They are pretty much the only game in town but you have to self- vacuum and everything is automated.  Decent for a quick wash.  If you go in the morning (especially weekdays) there is little to no line.  I need a good car wash so I hope they stay open - they are the only game in town.

I had no issues but I quickly ran in at 11:30 opn a Tuesday for a bag of Eukeneuba dog food.  The sales associate (young female) had no clue about the difference between Small Breed and Small Bite and fortunately they had the item I needed.  I came here in a pinch but in future I will stick to Delchester Feed - best prices around (in divey digs - but a great guy runs it) or my local PetSmart in Media/Spingfield.  Glad it's here but it needs some TLC and the staff needs some customer service training and product tutorials.

I went here to get some marinated mozzarella bllas and tomato salad for an event at my child's school.  The salads were fresh an tasty - but a little high on the prices.  In a pinch, I would go back again.  The pastas looked delicious.

I just had my daughter's birthday party here and it was FAB-U-LOUS. Allegra and the staff were all top notch and tereated us like family.  We had the entire upstairs party space which is lovely and roomy enough for our group.  The hand-frosted cupcakes tasted as great as they looked and the sugar rush was enjoyed by kids & grown-ups alike.  Can't say enuf good things about having an event here.  THANK YOU!!!!!

I have never eaten in the restaurant, but this review is for the EXCELLENT job done by Karen and her team.  They catered a dessert corporate event for my company and everything was beautifully presented and delicious.  The desserts included moist two-bite cupcakes in chocolate, vanilla and (was that) carrot with a coconut frosting.  Decorations were so cute.  Lemon squares, brownies and a gorgeous key lime tart.  Along with lemonade and iced tea (I, of course, made an Arnold Palmer) it was just right for our event.  Brava!  I now have NO excuse to not come and eat at Curds & Whey.
the owner was sooooo sweet to me when i tried on and nearly purchased a Lela Rose gown.  Stunning clothes.  LOVE IT!!!

The Cookery Ware Shop has been a Peddler's Village shop for years & years.  The service is GREAT and they have EVERYTHING you could possibly want.   Better than Williams Sonoma - family owned, great selection.  Con?  Tourist pricing - but again - no worse than Williams Sonoma which has high retails prices.  I got a crepe pan here 3 years ago and used it until it literally died.  Great little gadgets, too.  Fun for the home cook.  For the professional chef?  Not so much (it pains us to pay retail).

OK, I think I may have found my new spa-home in Philly. I followed long-time Massage Therapist, Rachel Garcia, over here from my old place, and for Rachel's massages I would follow her just about anywhere.  Love you, Rachel G! (Love Anna, too.)  I had a long, luxurious 90 minute aroma-therapy massage (Swedish with a bit more pressure just where my back needed it) and hand-selected citrus and lavender essential oils. There are over 40 oils you can pick from and they'll blend you up a customized synergy for your treatment.  Nice touch.  BLISS.  The waiting area was spacious - and even though there were 6 (yes, six) people waiting for 10 AM appointments on a Sunday, it was quiet and calm.  I was NOT offered a robe or to change, so I guess they just have massage clients change in the treatment room - which I am OK with - but it may not sit well with everyone.  One lady was wearing a robe (she was having a facial, I guess) but the rest of the 5 of us "lowly" massage clients just sat in our regular clothes.  They also sell Yeah-Baby slippers - which are super comfy.  The spa uses Yon-Ka skin care products and carries a nicely stocked array of aromatherpy products, candles and gift items.  I succumbed to a Persimmon scented jar candle - which at $6.50 (small/votive size) wasn't too bad.  There was NO pressure to buy - which was GREAT.  The owner (Jeff?) seemed cordial and the boutique person/receptionist (Stacy? Stephanie?) was very welcoming.  I will come back for a SERIES (Saves you $10 - $30 depending on the series you pick) of treatments next time.  If you are a tourist visiting Old City or a local who lives near here - Terme di Aroma is worth checking out.  And - they validate parking for select garages/lots.

Eh.  Meh.  A. A.  (Absolutely Average). For the Price?  ($8.95 - $12 with tax 'n tip no beverage) The Lunch special is fine. I got the Chicken coconut Soup (Good but i have had better - and I have had worse), Dumplings which alas, came out deep fried - will NEVER do that again - next time I will get the boring iceberg salad.    Entree choices are standard - I got Masaman Curry and again, I have had better and worse.  This one was sweeter than some with a good deal of curry paste and a slew of carrots as filler.  5 tiny chunks of soft tofu.  Sauces all tasted bottled.  Like "cafeteria Thai".  Disappointing.  Would not rush back here.  There are so few Thai places around that I will try them all until i find a decent one. I bet they just don't exist.
I was here, too, for jury duty.  It was far from thrilling - bring a couple of book.  You'll have to surrender your Blackberry at the door.

Just like the Haru mini-chain in NYC.  Over-priced and over-hyped.  Nice maki and fresh fish with a good selection - but NOT a Holy Grail by any means.  The ceviche appetizer, King Crab dumplings and Yellowtail hand rolls are always tasty.  Still, I love Shiroi Hana best for its un-pretentious feel and super-fresh fish.
Hit or miss.  And lately it's been ALL misses - but when you find something it is sooooooo cheap.  You have to be willing to buy used and dig thru the masses of strange clothing.

OMG this target is so clean and new.  It even has a small starbucks and a Pizza hut in the front.  Compared to the Target on Columbus BLVD this one it pretty ritzy.  I found what I needed so I can't say that I agree with @robyn h.
I use Megabus when I can't get onto Bolt Bus. They are both good, cheap options to get to NYC fast from Philly.

Just fine.  A-OK - not stellar and not bad.  Sweet - run-of-the-mill Thai staples - and they make a decent $9.95 lunch platter with a small cup of soup, mini appetizer (salad ro a few pices of dumpling or other treat) and entree.  Curries are fine - and Pad See Ew is my fave.  It was better when it was Thai Chef - but I am glad they are still here for a once in a while option.  I get take out Thai from Thia Singha House.
A much needed upscale version of wawa - with sandwiches and convenience foods, plus beverages and yogurt.  Sorely needed so I am thankful it's here.

The Porch - the newly constructed slab of fresh sidewalk and tables & chairs - provides FREE miniature golf all during July 2012. Concerts at lunchtime. A new Farmers Market on Wednesdays (11 AM - 2 PM thru beginning of October) complete with Mom Pops (YUM - read that review next!).  Check them out - and let's help get 30th Street re-re-revitalized.

M. Butterfly was the first "real" sushi bar to open in D-town.  Now sub-lplanted by Ooka and other competitors, they are definitely on the high end for price and quality.  The sushi here is just plain better than Ooka - but you PAY (dearly) for the organic wild slamon (we did a taste test and ordered nigiri in the "regular" sake and the "organic" and there were distinct differences in color, flavor and mouth-feel.).  They also SOMETIMES have "real" wasabi root - ground fresh. For $5.00 an order (which they didn't tell us when they asked me if I wanted fresh wasabi (which of course I said "yes".).  The $5.00 was a little shock to us when we got the bill.  But not nearly as shocking as the total.  WOW.  I was getting better, cheaper stuff in NYC.  Ah well - they are doing their best.  Very good fish and good meals - just bring money - you'll need it.

This review is for Mexican Post Express (the one in the bottom of the Comacast Center).  I am so happy they now have a Mexican option in the Comcast Center.    While I am not a huge fan of the sit-down branches of Mexican Post (we have often been to the Cherry street location, which is near our home.), the Express offers a less expensive option and is great for lunch.  They also participated in the Yelp Spring Festival and had muy delicioso Spinach Flauta.  I hope they'll add it to their every day menu.  (But somehow I doubt that.)  So, muchas gracias to Mexican Post Express for offering the hungry lunch crowd a quick and tasty burrito, taco or enchilada.

Curds & Whey catered a small dinner party (9 people) for a charitable organization that I support.  The salmon, cold broccoli/craisin salad, pasta salad and enormous cookie/rugelach platter were all terrific.  The salmon was moist and perfectly cooked - accompanied with a garlicky-herby-yogurt sauce.  YUM!!!!  The owner is somehow related to one of the ladies on "the board" of the group I am in so, I bet that's why they use them - but related or not - this food was "as good as it gets".  Great job C&W!  One day I will come and eat there - I can't wait!

This is the Perkins where my then-unemployed friend and I (in our late teens) experienced that great grease-fest of '90.  We ordered a fried appetizer combo of mozz. stix, chicken things and other fried stuff.  And coffee.  Lots of coffee and cigarettes.  (You USED to be able to smoke in a pancake house, but alas, no more.)  What a regrettable meal. I shoulda just had pancakes.

3 or 4 stars from me for Coffee Beanery inside the Concord Mall.  The lady attending the counter on a quiet weekday morning at 10 AM was personable and we had good service.  I have an Iced 1/2 caff latte and my friend had an iced (regular) coffee.  No issues.

OK, as many of you know I loathe chain restaurants, but I tried (I really did) to keep an open mind when a colleague of mine - who likes it here - wanted to have lunch here.  (She also graciously paid for lunch - and she is a good friend.)  After our server took our orders she quickly brought drinks and water.  The Philly-tap water tasted just awful.  So I drank my diet coke and kept quiet.  (I am a big water drinker and had a bottle of brita-ized water with me.)  We passed on the 2 for 20 deal and both got salads. I had the Shrimp/Avocado salad and the salad, was really not good.  Strangely enough the lettuce was just fine, but the shrimp were so oversalted/seasoned.  Also the avocado had obviously been chunked much earlier in the day as it was brown and slightly dried out.  Eew.  And thank god I got the gloppy green avo-based dressing on the side.  It was awful.  Thus, my faith in Applebee's has yet to be restored. Next time I'll go to Shiroi Hana across the street.  What possesed me?  Oh yeah - a colleague wanted to come here.

We were here for a corporate event and the place really needs some SERIOUS help.  Disgusting public restrooms. Shabby, dated ballrooms. Mediocre service.  I bet it was the cheapest place the group could find - so that's why they chose it.  NOT recommended.

Such a cute little pink shop.  And the scents wafting from the window on a crisp fall day just made me HAVE to go in.  (Note:  they have sporadic hours - so read the door).  Super-friendly gals (and one guy) were baking and glazing before my eyes.  Ganache coated cookies, cupcakes, tarts.  Love it.  So glad I walked by and walked in.  Bring cash - they don't take plastic.

Absolutely thrilled with the food, drinks and fabulous service for my picky-picky all female happy hour party of 11.  Hottie bartender Paul is still there and mixes up terrific margaritas, Palomas, Mojitos and more.  Order before 6:30 PM (weekdays) and get a happy hour "classic" marg for just $5.  Also a bunch of $5 apps and $2.5 single tacos.  (The fried shrimp is good, but really bad for you.)  Tableside guac (Pricey at $11, Jicama sticks are $2 more) is always a big hit.  We had STELLAR service from Israel and all the hostesses.  Can't wait to do it again.

Therapist - 5 star, experience at the spa - about 3. The waiting room at 9:45 AM on a summer Saturday was like a zoo - with 9 people waiting for their 10 AM appointments,  Over crowded and not relaxing at all. They don't even give you a robe & slippers - it's basically a waiting room - not a spa lounge at all.  However, all was forgotten once I entered the treatment room (nice) and had a great aromatherapy massage. $80 (Tips must be in cash - not on credit card so know that before you go.)  I will be back.

Yum, yum, yum, yum, yum!  Yum.  Oh yeah.  Did I mention this is the real italian sorbetto / gelato.  The sorbettos are all dairy-free and still have a fabulous rich texture.  The flavors - sublime - like Blood Orange (the real McCoy), and Campari Grapefruit.  Last year they had a summertime offering of Lemon Opal Basil.  Want something fattening and decadent?  Get a cone (the euro-style crisp cone) with a scoop of Dulce du Leche or Butterscotch and 1 scoop of deep, dark, ciocolatto sciurro (bitter dark choc.).  FREE home-made whipped cream is UNSWEETENED and compliments most selections.  Or - get a BRIOCHE, baby!  And fill it with frozen bliss.  The unsweetened whipped cream is complimentary.  You can feel your arteries clogging with each decadent mouthful.  OK, gotta go do cardio now...

Not bad!  I went here for lunch today with an old friend and colleague of mine who loves it here.  She had a 4 star Chicken Parm (1/2 order - was huge) and I had a really small, but tasty piece of Lasagna - the $6.00 lunch special.  Lunch for 2 with tip was $26 - can't beat that!  I will definitely be back.

We had a perfectly fine experience at the Springfield Mall outpost of Tar-jay. DD got some "littlest pet shop" toys, I got an OXO vegetable peeler and DH browsed for Nintendo DS games.  All in all - mid-length lines (not short but not disasterous) a decently clean rest room and predictable target merch made for a decent experience.  We shop Target - here and otherwise.

I went here only once - as it did not warrant a return visit.  (There are better Italian places nearby and not so nearby.)  But we had a nice, passable - albeit not very memorable - meal here on a cold winter night.  I had a very nice salmon dish and my (then fiance now) husband has a pasta dish with sausage and peppers.  Both were just OK.  (Mine was better than his, IMO.)  We also tried the "wedding" soup which was way, way too salty.  The servers were pleasant enough and attentive.

We had a wonderful event here for 32 (yes, 32) people with a set menu and everything was great.  Eduardo and a team of about 4 servers/bussers were expedient and muy friendly.  The Salmon Manchamanteles ("messy Mole") was terrific.  Vegetarian Enchiladas and Skillet tacos looked great, too.  Sides of rice with pepitas and black beans with cotija were brought to the tables for all to share.  Dessert of tres leches cake or flan was simple.  Prices run higher here - but it's a yuppie/affluent area. Can get VERY loud. Mike (Mark?) the red headed bar tender was patient and wonderful.  You can even take your kids here.  For real!

Stopped in for lunch and would up ordering the eggs Florentine - and they were PERECT.  So satisfying on a cold wintery day.  It was very busy (They do a big lunch business).  A go-to lunch spot or for "breakfast all day".  Old-school décor.  Pay up front.

Ok, now normally I would have given Under the C 4 stars - as the prices are HIGH (you are paying for that gorgeous high-rent store in the Comacast Center, BUT...  (and I usually have a really big BUT)  Now that we have met Bruce - the world' best fishmonger - the get 5 stars and our business for sure!  Bruce showed my 5 year old's Pre-K class the lobsters in the lobster tank, and even let one of them hold one.  Alas, my little one was not that one -but Bruce came to the rescue.  My little girl got her picture taken holding a huge lobster. Plus she loves to eat the cooked shrimp.  And we love the convenience of having fresh tilapia, salmon and snapper to take home.  We are glad you are here, Under the C.  And we love Bruce.  GIVE HIM A BIG RAISE!!!
Friends of mine from High School own this fabulous local farm - and Halloween/Harvest time is a great tome to visit - also good for spring plantings - flowers, seedlings and trees/shrubs.  Terrific!

Much akin to the Tubby Olive - but better prices (and a few different sized bottles) and better tasting balsamics.  Olive oils seemed similar and some identical to Tubby Olive.  Also sells a few tapanades and Italian (pricey) honeys.  A fun place to taste and shop. Try the Meyer Lemon infused Oil and the Fig or Cherry Balsamic.  Yum! (And great for a gift for that food lover in your life.)

This is a review of the Panda Express in Granite Run mall. And maybe 4 stars is a bit much - but they were definitely more than 3 on the evening we went.  We are NOT fast food people, - and usually fast food Chinese is very low on my list. But DD loves the Orange Chicken (yes, it's fried) and Honey Walnut Shrimp (also fried - and shrimp dishes cost extra at PE) so we went here. Steamed veggies on the side (instead of lo mein - that they call chow mein - or fried rice).  Clean, friendly staff - brought us our kids meals - free refills on fountain drinks.  They even have their own restroom (cleaner than the one in the mall).  We'll be back! (But not too often - it's not so good for our diets.)

Hadn't been to Capogiro in a while - and thank goodness I went today.  They have FRESH BLOOD ORANGE JUICE (squeezed to order - while supplies last - and blood oranges are around) and Blood Orange, Pomegranate and Papaya Sorbetti in stock this week.  RUN - don't walk for a taste of mid-winter sunshine.  Philadelphians - we are truly blessed to have Capogiro right in our own backyard.  Some of the best gelati and sorbetti on the Planet (better than many in Italy and NYC!).  Go, Go, Go!!!

This store has GAP, GAP KIds & GAP Body in it (2 stories). I have purchased "typical" GAP items here for my little girl - lots of jammies back in the day - and a pair of jeans for myself.  No big whoop - it's the GAP for goodness sake - but saf, disposable clothing for casual wear.  Not a great bargain - but not too expensive either.  Spacious fitting rooms.  Good luck getting help though. Check out lines can be long during weekend and holiday shopping rushes.  Try going at 11 AM on a Tuesday.

We have been Zoo members for 2 years now - as we have a 3.5 year old. For members, the zoo is a great deal.  The free parking alone is a great bonus.  We also don't feel pressured to see the entire zoo in one day, as now we can visit whenever we wish.  The Zoo also has a "treee house" just for members - but it is not airconditioned and gets very hot..  Also they do not sell milk - only sodas - so if you are nutrition (and cost) conscious - pack drinks and snacks for your family.  It is shameful that there are not more healthy choices for kids to eat here.

I've seen many a show at EF and the smaller ones are better. The sound quality is not as good as some other venues and it has the typical "concert syndrome" that comes with large crowds and inadequate ladies room facilities.  Meanwhile most times I was too drunk to notice and enjoyed the shows anyway.  So come early, stake your claim, smuggle in a bottle or two of water (you'll need it) and hold in your pee until the end of the show.  Enjoy!

I am not a big Indian Food lover - but I do love the breads. That said, a group of 4 coworkers (including me) went for lunch here and indulged in the $8.95 lunch buffet.  Everything was fresh (We arrived right after 12 noon) and not too picked over. I enjoyed the Chicken Tikka Masala (very mild and basic), rice, Saag Panir and fresh naan.  Galub Jamun for dessert is always a treat - and Chinnar's is good.  We also ordered a freshly cooked (off the menu) order of Aloo Paratha (Bred with potatos) and that was terrific.  I prefer to order freshly cooked meals over the buffet - but for $8.95 you can't beat the selection and value.  Next time if we come for dinner I want to try a lamb dish. And yes, we'll be back - likely soon.

We have lived in the Packard Motor Car building (a Reinhold property) for over 4 years.  We enjoy the convenience of the location and many of the ammenities the building provides.  The property is generally well-maintained and well managed.  We do have a FEW gripes - the most significant being the energy-wasting drier that is very, very old and will not be replaced.  Other than that, we love our gorgeous apartment (many units have been recently renovated and look great) and enjoy living here.  UPDATE:   We moved out after 6 years when we bought a house in the 'burbs.

ZERO Stars for what we referred to as McDEATH when i was a grad student at Penn.  There have been shootings, stabbiong, roberroes and muggings here over the many years.  Yet somehow - McDeath remains open.  Let's not even talk about the "hood" demographic servers and patrons alike.  And of course the scads of loiterers and homeless, down & out West Philly types.  AVOID.  AVOID.

So pleased with the service and beverages (hot coffee drinks, iced lattes and smoothies).  They also have free (but very slow internet) computers to use.  The (male) owner is very kind to us and my 9 year old loves the hot cocoa in winter and pina coloda smoothies.

3.5 atars for food - I gave it 3 - because it's just not THAT wonderful.  I had eggplant salad and a falafel platter.  Good - but not as good as Mama's.  Will elaborate more later. (Pressed for time.)

This Indian outpost in the Liberty Place food court serves up decent, CHEAP Indian food.  Not the best ever - but certainly a good option considering the other choices in the food court.  They always have samosas as well as vegetarian and chicken entrees that rotate.  (Chicken Tikka is usually available)  Good rice!

Oh, this is a conflicted 4 star review - and brace yourself - it may be a long one.  My husband and a close (vegetarian) friend of ours finally took the plunge and went to Chifa for dinner on Halloween night.  Decor is 5 star - and gorgeous.  Everything from the restroom to the blue & white tiles on the walls, and tons of flickering votive candles at night.  I do have to say that the service was EXCELLENT - from the hostess and our server, Melissa, right down to the ceviche chef.  Everyone was friendly and accomodating to our various requests and questions.  From reading these reviews, I am sure by now you know that Chifa serves small plates (perfect for sharing) and that some are smaller than others.  You may also have read about the hot, cheesey bread balls served with a spicy guava butter.  They are, indeed, AWESOME and I scarfed down 2 of them without even realizing it.  We started our meal with a round of delicious - if overpriced ($12 a pop) - cocktails.  The guys had glorified Shandies - Ginger liqueur, fresh lime juice and beer.  I had a virgin Pineapple Ginger concoction that was made w/ REAL, fresh golden pineapple.  It was so tasty & refreshing.  Then came the famous buns.  The BBQ tofu bun (we subbed tofu for pork belly) was so terrific - possibly the best bite of the night.  The tofu was crisp and blissfully glazed in a hoisin BBQ sauce.  A dash of spicy mayo on the white steamed bun.  Yum.  The Pork belly was (likely sous-vided - they have gone sous-vide CRAZY here.) very fatty - but hey - it's pork BELLY.  Belly as alot of fat, right?  Well, I preferred the tofu.  Anyhow - we progress onward - out came the egg mcmuffins - no really, I can't remember the name, but they were corn arepas topped with Oxtail, a PERFETLY done egg (a bit runny but not slimy), crisp bacon and (here's where Chifa loses major points) tons of gloppy peppery sauce.  Thankfully, and thanks to YELP, I knew to order my food with "sauce on the side" or "Light on the sauce" - and this was my mantra for the evening.  My veggie friend had the Chinese Broccoli, and as others have said, it was way too oily.  Literally swimming in a sesame oil sauce.    He also had a vegetarian version of the Chaufa rice.  I tasted a bite and it was complex and delicious - if a little heavy on the (surprise) salt.  Yes, folks, it's true.  Chifa has potential to be a real, true 5 star joint, but they are too heavy handed with the salt, oily, sauces and seasonings.  The ingredients they use are top-quality and need to be able to "sing" for themselves.  I am not saying to under season them, just please don't OVER season them.  Next came the (much, much anticipated) Lobster noodles.  I knew to ask for this "light on the sauce" and it was still swimming in a rich, creamy, slightly red-peppery sauce.  Succulent and buttery-sweet hunks of lobster and fresh, green peas.  The noodles were perfectly cooked.  I would totally order this again (and the tofu buns, man they rocked).  But next time I'd go even LIGHTER on the sauce - I can't imagine how over-sauced it would have been had I not asked for light sauce.    Ok.  Whatever.  You get the point.  Anyhow - we're not done (Oh, and by now I CANCELLED our order of $38 wagyu steak - as I knew I'd be too full to eat it.) - Out came the curried goat (get it  for one - it's more than enough).  This is a unique dish - and not my fave - but hubby liked it.  Served with freshly sliced bananas and more of those light fluffy buns along side.  Plus a weird crispy lentil cake.  And next came the (yes, they are greasy) scallion pancakes.  Not the best I've ever had - but the cauliflower sauce (yes, really) was super tasty.  Oh - and Chifa is really weird about "coursing out" the meals - the served us a single bowl of broccolli after the buns and before anything else.  If we return, I will try to tell them what we want first (Like, the Waygu!!!)  By now we are all pretty stuffed, but we just had to have some Chai tea and Banana-Pumpkin funnel cake (too greasy for me - but somehow, I ate it!  Ha!).  The banana ice cream quenelle along side it was home made and PERFECT.   The odd honey-anise tuile?  Not so hot.  Thankfully, once again, I asked for the strange spicy peanut sauce ON THE SIDE.  Garces must be commended for his creative menu, but I fear there is just a little TOO MUCH going on in each dish.  Too much salt, too much sauce, too much fat, etc.  Also they sure are getting full usage out of their brand new sous-vide machine.  Nearly all the meats are sous-vided (and yes, they are tender to a fault) - but what about some good ole pan-searing?  OK, I am a spoiled, jaded, ex-Manhattan brat - but I really did enjoy our 2.5 hour meal here and WOULD return - especially now that I know what to get and what NOT to get.  Chifa, you are sooooo close to 5 star - but some of the dishes were really 2-3 star.  (Brocolli, Scallion pancakes, Desserts need work.)  We'll drop in for buns 'n beer

Great customer service from Dontae and my food was ready in a flash - even during a busy Thursday lunch rush.  Line moves quickly.  Tables get crowded, so I carried out.  Excellent choice in fast food if you stick to grilled nuggets and super food side.

For $15.95 we purchased an ice cream pie (fed our crowd of 7 easily with a few slices left over) - graham cracker crust, cheesecake flavored ice cream and garnished with whipped topping (likely cool-whip-type) and pecans.  Much more popular for Thanksgiving than pumpkin pie.  Delicious.  In fact - we liked it so well we ordered it again for Christmas Eve dinner/dessert.  Great job on the ice cream pies, ladies!
Our 4 year old (who has been coming since she was 2) loves it here. What chilkd wouldn't?  There is so miuch for kids to do here.  It's great! We are members.

I'm sorry - but I LOVE the flower show - and have been 6 years in a row. Some years are far better than others.  A few tricks?  Never go on a weekend - take a 1/2 day off from work and go Tuesday or Wednesday after 1 PM.  Bring bottled water with you so you don't have to buy it there (convention center prices) - you can even pack a lunch.  Buy roses (and irises etc.) from the Marketplace ($6 - $7 a dozen is a steal). and bring a shopping bag with you.  Great bargains on gardening tools, too.  (PHS members get a 10% discount at MOST - not all - stalls).  Go!  It's worht it - and if you become a PHS member your tickets are included in the membership price.  (Makes it really worth it).

We held a conference here - including a breakfast buffet and lunch buffet. Service was good - a little "slow on the draw" in some areas but every request we made was eventually addressed.  Main "room" felt a little "barn like" with a high ceiling and thus hard to keep adequately cool (without being freezing).  Alternated from too hot to too cold when the A/C cycled on and off.  Had over 200 people in attendance.  Food was tasty and hot items were hot (and cold items kept chilled).  No water glasses on tables (you had to pour your own).  Not 5 star by any means - but a strong 3.5 stars.

Oh, this poor mall. The era of the American circa 1983 mall is over.  It's a shame, too - because it's so close by - and we will be coming here for the few restaurants and shops that are left - and the movie theatre.  I hope they can revive it.

Ok, my DD and I went here on a weekday afternoon at about 4:30 when the place was all but empty and finally got some service.  Sghe had (very tasty and huge) chicken fingers % fries - for $9.95 and I had the sesame noodles with tofu.  (Too greasy and at $13 one of the cheaper choices).  Wow is it expensive here for yuppified diner food. The food was good, but not worth the price and NO WAY would I wait in the enormous weekend brunch lines here.  It's just NOT worth that.  Meanwhile, the cool servers gave DD a big bowl of fresh summer berries and banans gratis (thank you so much!) and the nice hispanic line cooks let her tour the (clean, professional) kitchen.  Close to 4 stars but the prices made me go with 3.

Located inside the bank - you can get a luscious latte, a hot white chocolate mocha, salted caramel cocoa and other caloric coffee treat as well as muffins and bagels. They also have a limited amount of salads/sandwiches and soups for a quick lunch.  My tall (small) iced latte was not too expensive ($1.90 with tax) and our 8 year old enjoyed her cocoa with whipped cream and tiny chocolate chips on top.  Female barrista was friendly and fun.  Great service and a clean restroom. We'll be back - and soon!
This is a very nice, well run, clean Chipotle.  My Chicken Burrito Bowl was a bit too spicy for some reason today - but otherwise - it's just the way I like it.

We are spoiled because our "home rink" is Icework in Aston - a 4 surface facility complete with a BAR and a snack bar, however my child is a figure skater and competes and occaisionally practices here.  Skaing Club of Wilmington is also home to some seriously talented coaches (many of whom also coach at other area rinks) and of course, the Great Johnny Weir.  We are grateful to live near so many facilities where my skater can practice and compete.  SIngle ice surface, OK locker rooms.  Limited ice time due to ONE icde surface for USFSA and hockey needs.

Cafe Riviera provides a lunch buffet of hot items (with cold pasta or green salad along side) for our corporate cafe once a week and man, is it ever delicious.  The meatballs, Italian sausage (with peppers and onions) and Chicken Cacciatore are classics and so well executed -even for a mass buffet.  So pleased - and now I wanna go to the restaurant!

A very solid 4 stars. We dined last night as part of a large (11 people) private group with a set menu.  Mr. Pete at the bar is a love, and kept the Prosecco & Chambord flowing. He also made virgin "bikini cocktails" for my 7 year old.    Michael is terrifc and got the little one some non-truffled fries and chicken fingers - which she (of course) enjoyed.  For the grownups, crispy artichokes were punchy with lemon - delish - but the plain arugula bed they lay on was boring and bitter.  Entrees were much better with a luscious campanele pasta with a rich mushroom sauce.  The chicken, served with tasty brussels sprouts (I'm a fan!) was delighfully presented.  Our friends had the fish which also looked great.  We could not stay for the dessert course - but we will be back - and hopefully soon.  This would bve a great place for a party or private event. Fantastic waitstaff (Dennis, you rock!). Accomodating, friendly and fun.

While we actually wound up dining at PYT - I sure wish we'd have stayed here.  PYT was a frikkin' disaster (read my review).  Anyhow - DH & I walked in (and wound up walking out) today. The menu of custom pies and steaks sounds terrific - but (the main reason we left) it was hot a heck in there. (No A/C?  Or maybe just the heat of the pizza ovens?)  Also the 3 thin-crust pies that were available for "by the slice" - plain, veggie with onions, and some sort of brown meat - did not appeal.  I would come back here - but only to carry out. Too hot on a summer day to eat in here.  (Sorry)  The man behind the counter was perfectly nice.  Oh - and I would order a freshly baked pie - not a slice that has been sitting around for god know how long.  (We walked in around 3 - which is smack dab between lunch and dinner.)

This is a nice, BIG, B&N location complete with a Starbucks cafe on the 2nd Floor.  B&N did a great fundraising event for my kids school - donating 5 to 10% of the days sales to the school.  A good place to kill time when the weather is bad - you can sit & read and have a coffee.

This is the new outpost of NCC in the Duane Morris Building on 18th Street.  It is more spacious than the Walnut Street Branch and has the same basic menu of items.  (Yum-my!)  It is much larger than the 13th Street store and can accomodate private parties upstairs.  They also have a bakery onsite and thus have a few more varieties of cupcakes and baked desserts available.  The new NCC also has elaborate tea party set ups complete with gorgeous china teapots and cups/saucers for sipping tea (Harney & Sons) or that awesome sipping chocolate.  (A little goes a long way.)  Oh, my hips!!!

This building needs an overhaul INSIDE.  The ancient infrastructure is failing.  C'mon people.  You powerwashed the exterior - and it looks great - now lets fix the ancient restrooms, corridors and grungy stairwells INSIDE.

For family theatre and accessibility to the arts, you can't beat the Arden.  We are subscribers and just saw "The Borrowers" and are planning to see "The Flea & The Professor" this spring.  Small theatre (2 stages - a small one upstairs and a larger mainstage) and there really are no "bad" seats.  Lots of fun for kids and adults, plus they offer unique classes and programs for all ages - and the FUN (forget what it stands for) lets your kid be an usher for a day and have a backstage tour.  Neat-o!

3.5 stars tops for this Old-School Deli/Butcher Shop (although there was nothing going on at the back counter on the Monday that I ate lunch there - butcher hsop part was dead).  Very friendly service - although they get crazy-busy for lunch. Breakfast is served all day but dinner items are only after 5. It was LOUD in there.  I had a patty melt (no grilled onions??  You'd have to ask I think) with Cheddar Cheese instead of American.  Cooked to order and nicely done.  A 20 oz. bottle of Diet Coke (which is what was plunked down in front of me when I ordered a diet coke) and a glass of ice along side ran $1.99.  You pay at the front counter.  Not a bad place - but not a holy grail either. I'll be back. I wish that butcher shop seemed better - I love to support REAL butchers. There are so few of them left.

I was dragged here by 2 coworkers who actually LIKE it here - I think because it is very cheap - $4.50 - $5 for a personal pan pizza at lunch - and quick.  I have never been a pizza hut person and have not eaten Pizza Hut food at all in the past few years - except for once when My (then) 9 year old demanded it.  Blargh.  First of all the service is non-existent - Gail tried her best but even with only 2 dine-in tables everything from ordering to serving food to especially getting our credit cards back was painfully awkward and slow.  Gail is a sweetheart - and has good taste in 70's music (which, by the way, was blaringly loud - not at all "background" music) but she can't handle the lunch crowd all by herself.  The toothless guy making the pizzas was also pleasant but left to fend for himself.  Not a fan. And I will only go back when dragged back.  The good part?  Super cheap - even with tip. The bad part?  A greasy, salty MESS of a pizza.    Maybe I could attempt wings next time? I am frightened.

Took our 7 year old to see Robin Hood - and she also participated in the FUN (Family Ushering Night) Ushering program.  She loved it!  A great production with 5 actors playing 14 characters. Neat!  We even got a chance to talk to the actors after the play - and saw them again eating dinner at Revloution house.  Arden is expanding to a new building for theatre camps and classes. Can't wait to see it!

They did our 3 tiered, multi flavored wedding cake and the results were picture-perfect and so yummy.  They are pricey - but you get what you pay for.  Customer service was terrific from initial cake tasting and consultation, through color and design selection.  Perry (the pastry chef) is a master!  We loved our wedding cake.

This review is specifically for the terrific makeover I received at the MAC counter by Cynthia.  She is a bit older, experienced makeup artist and made me look FAB.  I like many of MAC's products and the $55.00 minimum purchase to have your look done is really no biggie - once you pick out a few items.  I spent more like $100.  (Ssssh - don't tell my husband.)  Anyhow - give Cynthia a try at MAC - she knows what she's doing and is not pushy at all.  I really enjoyed meeting her.
They closed.  I knew it was only a matter of time.

Hate to be a nay-sayer - but I don;t know how this place stays in business - there are way cheaper sources for cookbooks and many places like Amazon, Half.com and ebay for used copies.  I rarely buy new books anymore - especially a true cook book which will get beat up and spattered on in my kitchen.  I am glad they exist and love to browse here - but I buy elsewhere. Sad but true and I wish the (very pleasant) owner luck.  SOmehow they have lasted.  Not sure how.

Went for lunch again with a coworker. Chicken Tikka Masala is excellent.  Freshly-baked Naan (even on the buffet - you can get a fresh basket of naan included).  A lovely selection. Price is now $9.95 for lunch - we must have goten a special or something last time it was $8.95.  Not a big deal. - for $10 you can eat yourself silly.

I am not a big Panera girl - but I have eaten in quite a few of them.  Went here for lunch when it was crowded but not crazy (when it's crazy I won't go.)  Monday - Friday ferom 12 - 1:30 the joint is packed with pharmaceutical folks wolfing down their salads, soups and sandwiches.  I got a 1/2 size salad (plenty) and a cup of delicious lemon chicken orzo soup. I wish they offered that one more.  Salad was on romaine and it was boring but fine. Soup was very good. Came out for about $10.  A good quick-fix for lunch.

I was having a challah emergency (and they only bake real Challah on Fridays - appropriately enough) but I got 2 braided Briche rolls that looked like little round mini-challahs and it worked out fine.  Thank goodness they were there!  I have also had the odd croissant and breakfast treat here - very good stuff - especially their almond croissant.  Soooooo flaky & buttery and good.

MEH!  So Meh-diocre.  A casino usually has great food. Not at Sugarhouse.  It has middle-of-the-road burgers and a few snadwiches and plates.  Not my bag, baby.  Honestly?  Were it not for proximity - I would NEVER come to Sugarhouse - I'd sooner go to AC or even Bethlehem, PA.  Philly fought long & hard to get a casino - and THIS is what they get?  Sorry - Unimpressed.

I have not been to moshi moshi in a very long time, and I needed some quick take-out tonight, so I stopped in and noticed a few things:  1.  The menu has changed (smaller) 2.  Prices went up a wee bit (but it has been over a year, I think.) 3.  My favorite Toro Ginza roll is now gone- but he will still make it, if you ask.  I ordered 2 rolls, - a crunchy tuna and an albacore & avo.  Both were fresh and fine.  service was prompt.  The dining room was very slow on a Thursday nite.  It's still OK - just a 3 star place.  Shiroi Hana is better (IMO).

Not sure if the puppies here are puppy mill puppies - but if they are that is SO WRONG on so many levels.  Our dog is a rescue dog.  We come here because of its convenient location and because they stock Eukaneba small breed senior food which is what my pug eats.  The prices are average and service is your basic disinterested and clueless minimum wage staff.  i am glad they are here though - because I needed a hew harness and they had just what I needed.

This is Marble Slab Creamery (They Bought out Maggie Moo's) and for $2.99 your kid under 12 can get ice cream in a cup or cone with unlimited "mix ins".  My kid opted for 99 cents for a waffle cone dipped in chocolate.  Sugar overload.  Meanwhile I tasted the ice cream (Sweet Cream vs. Vanilla vs. Butter Pecan and it was "just OK".  Give me Hagen Daaz or Ben & Jerry's over this any day.
OK, I give 'em another star.  I took my 4 year old there for the $5.00 Tower Tour (15 minutes to go up, look around and come back down).  She WUVED it!

A fairly clean, decently run Subway with all the usual items. Although the dining area was more pleasant to eat in than our usual Subway (at 17 & the Parkway), this one had soggy flatbread.  Otherwise, the male manager was very nice and we enjoyed our sandwiches (minus tha soggy flatbread).

I had a surprisingly decent experience at Pei Wei - and this is the first and only time I'd ever been to one.  It's kinda like the Qdoba of Chinese food.  You place your order and pay at the front counter, then take your number and sit down.  I ordered from a VERY nice young man at the counter.  I had an order of 4 (fried) cream cheese wontons (supposedly they had crab - but they were very light on the crab) and the Viet Namese Chicken rolls (Not the salad wraps - the rice paper rolls).  Good but I've had way better.  Due to the EXCELLENT friendly service - not only from the counter man (who gave me a coupon for my next visit when he heard this was my frst) - but also the sweet young gal who nrought me my order, and the very CLEAN and uncrowded (note it was 11:25 AM on a Thursday) this porbably made my experience better than it could have been.  That said - I will return again to try a "bowl" or entree.  I would not get the Viet rolls again - but I would splurge on the cream-cheesey fried goodness once in a great while.  I also would like to try their Thai style wonton soup.    Not bad - really.  I am pleasantly surprised and will return again to test them.  P.S.  My order total with tax was just under $12 - kinda high for lunch on a workday.  (No beverage!!!!)

Boy do we ever love and value the Arden. Our 7 year old was an usher (part of the FUN - family ushering network) at a performance of "Charlotte's Web".  She learned so much and had a blast.  We all enjoyed the performance. It's good theatre - children's or not.  Go see Charlotte's Web before it's gone. (Even if you don't have kids)  A great production!

A colleague of mine prdered a huge cookie and brownie tray from Panera for an office event and the cookies (HUGE - and about 450 calories a piece) were delicious.  The Chocolate Chipper and Double Chocolate with Walnuts (and white confection pieces) were snapped up in minutes.  I did not try the brownies but they looked great and also disappeared.

Quick and easy - plus they have a drive through. (The morning coffee rush is a bit hectic).  I usually get an iced coffee (I walk in) during the summer. They have everything a basic DD has - coffee, donuts, sandwiches and cold drinks.  No issues from me - but I do not come here a whole lot.

Not as good today - but still a classic. I still prefer Oregon over the Melrose and Penrose diners.  I am grateful to be able to find a few good "old school" diners.  DD had chicken fingers 'n fries (theirs are very fresh and crisp), DH and I had breakfast.

Really good food and great Iced Coffee - pus decent service (but it was really hot in there this last time we went for lunch.  The Chicken over broken rice (or banh) is great and the Chinese broccoli  in garlic sauce was crispy and tender and cooked to perfection.  And you can get flaming rum drinks, too - though we never do.  Love Vietnam for a quick comforting meal.

Should be called the "DiBruno's: market - although there are several other shops.  A Capital Teas, Tabouli, an Asian Place and a great Flower shop.  Only 2 places selling fresh produce.  1 fish market.  Clean and fun to visit. Bring money.  Parking can be tough.

For the airport - it's a decent bet. In general?  It's meh.  If you are stuck in Philly airport you are way better off at ABP than at Famous Familia or that weird little chinese place, or even Chickie's and Pete's.  A safe, if airport-priced choice.
It's such fun here.  And a good place to enjoy a cigar in peace. Terrific, classy service (see Alexandra T.'s review).  Sexy.

Fantastic Food - including Kabobs and Gyros and a terrific lunch special for $7.95.  Very small place and super casual.  Quick, friendly service and delectable sides like Cauliflower & Sabzi!  Yum!!!!

I come here whenever I have a 10 or 15% off coupon that I get in the mail.  If you buy stuff on sale here you can get some nice "gap-ish" quality kids clothes for a decent price.  (Better yet - shop at a Children's place outlet and use those same coupons.)  My daughter who is now 4 wears a size 5 or 6 here.  I think the label sizes run small because at 10 months old she wore and 18 mos. or even a 2T.  The sizes go from 0-3 mos. up to 14-16 - but I can not imagine that any "cool tweens" over 11 who dain to shop here.  It's a KIDS store.  Also when they have end-of-season sales you can get some good deals.  The saleslady here (one of them) was especially nice and event the bored-out-of-her-mind security guard helped me find what I was looking for.  I like to shop here.

Meh.  They look better than they taste.  DD (who is 4 and would give anything with cupcakes 5 stars) and I stopped in to day and split a LARGE $3.00 "Hattie don't play" chocolate cupcake with rich (delish - much better than the dry cake) chocolate frosting.  Unfortunately the cake was a bit dry.  The cupcakes here are a sold 3 star but not as good as Buttercup in NY or dare I say Flying Monkey in RTM.  Glad to see them prosper - maybe next time I'll pick a different flavor? A bit disappointing.

It was OK but not great.  I had a dessert crepe with fresh bananas (about 2 awhole bananas - fresh and great.  But the crepe itself was kinda tasteless.  I think they cut their losses with neither a sweet batter nor a savory batter so that they can use the same batch of batter for both sweet and savory crepes.  Profi's at RTM was better - but also cost more.  I may return.  Not sure. I should also mention that the ONE person they had running the  stand was very, very nice, professional, friendly and helpful.  And he made the crepe effortlessly.  I just wish they'd improve the batter recipe.

I won't be returning to Coco anytime soon. I stopped in at 7:45 AM this morning after passing by many times and seeing the sign advertising over 6 different kinds of soup.  I figured that soup would not be available in the early AM - but the lady said that it was if I really wanted it and what kind would I like?  I settled on a small Chicken & Dumpling soup. After a while she brought out a styrofoam bowl from the kitchen and asked me, "Do you want that heated up"?  What?  Are you kidding me?  "Yes, of course". (I was thinking, what?  I'm gonna eat cold soup?)  Whatever.  Meanwhile the one male cashier was very, very cute. The soup itself was fine - not mind blowing but certainly not worth a rush back.  Service here is just plain odd.  I will not be back.

I'm too old & farty to shop here any more. I think next year they will officially ban me due to my new demographic.  In any case, it's fun to browse for trendy duds here - and though I rarely buy (whew - pricey) - it's fun to just see what new & hot.    Or is that hawt?!

When I moved to Philly after spending 10 years in New York City (1 year in Brooklyn) the diners here were a let-down.  Meanwhile, I am so happy to find the Oregon (I prefer it to the "classic" Melrose).  They have great old-school waitresses full of spunk and bite.  The food is terrific and the Italian Dinners (Chicken Francese, Cacciatore, etc.) are enormous and restaurant quality.)  What a deal.  Salads are fresh and crisp as is the attitude of the patrons.  LOVE this place with or without my 4 year old in tow. Viva the Oregon Diner.

Fantastic theatre in Chester County - with a lovely cafe and gift shop areas. there really isn't a "bad seat" in the (medium sized) house. Certain productions are geared toward families with kids.  They also have a "Teen" theatre camp.  You can even hold events in the Bistro/Barn area they own.  Wonderful staff and volunteers.  We support you!

We came at the end of the day (around 4 PM) on Sunday so the shelves were fairly barren - but my 11 year old and I shared a HUGE Mexican cookie/cake and a churro (delicious).  Lady helping spoke little English but had a bright smile. Inexpensive.  Wish they offered a place to sit and eat,  (Philter - a cafe is next door).  Very welcome treats! CASH ONLY.

Ugh.  Don't get me started on O.G. - and this one in particular is where 2 out of 3 of my DH's brothers had their wedding rehearsal dinners.  Thus, my (then future) FIL wanted US to have our rehearsal dinner there too.  NO WAY!!!  (We wound up going to Bensi's across the street).  Meanwhile - O.G is NOT Italian.  It's faux-talian-american.  And it's full of kids.  I am not a fan of the over cooked, over sauce formula-cooked pastas. It's OK in a pinch but there are so many way better choices.
So expensive and such a snotty vibe. The best part is the boutique upstairs, but basically I was given dirty looks by the sales ladies the entire time i shopped.  Whatever.

At last - I am a Tony Luke's virgin no longer.  And what a way to go.  It was a gorgeous day in November for philly and DH & I went to Tony Luke's but the line was so long that we decided to go acrosss the street to the sports bar.  Afetr a round of fried goodnees - DH had the cheese fries and I had some really outstanding O-rings - we were on to our main attraction.  DH had a cheese steak with Provolone and it was terrific. I enjoyed a garlicky plate of Veal Scallopini that was kickin' in old school.  This was THE $#!T - for real.  Mushrooms, green peppers, onions and tender veal (wish there had been a bit more of that) in a garlicky, olive-oily sauce that reminded me of how my Nonna woulda done it.  Um.  If I'd had an Italian Nonna.  Can't wait to go back and try the Chicken Sandwich with Spinach.  I am sold on Tony Luke's.

Took my mom and my 6 year old here for a perfomrance of "The Flea & the Professor", not only was this great Children's Theater - but it was great theatre in general.  All 3 generations laughed and enjoyed.  Great actors and very good for introducing kids to the love of live performance.  We love it here.  This was our first year as subsricbers and we will subscribe again next year.  We also had awesome seats - there are NO bad seats here - small theater with good sight lines.  We loved every minute.

My ex boyfriend LOVED this tiny gem of a tobacconist.  He is/was a cigar afficianado and this place had some rare cigar that he had been seeking.  I like a puff or 2 in good measure - but am no "knower" of all things cigar - but this was a nice, friendly little shop right in the center of D-Town (wedged in between the Fountain House (aka Starbucks) and Buck County Coffee.  Cigars & Coffee.  Who would have thunk it?

This Panera is clean and well managed.  I had a delicious (Pick 2) lunch special with a small greek salad (no onion, dressing on the side) and French onion soup (a little too salty but still good).  Panera's food can be LOADED with calories so watch what you get - especially the bread .   My lunch combo came with a choice of chips, a baguette or an apple.  I took the apple and felt downright righteous.  Meanwhile the pineaplle upside-down mini bundts were calling my name - but I was good and diregarded that call.  I do like Panera - as chains go - to me it's BETTER than Cosi.  (I don't like Cosi because once the bread cools down it turns to cardboard.)

I am not a cart food person - but every once in a blue moon (especially in spring & summer when a girl's mind turns to... ...fresh fruit) I get fruit salad from this cart or from the one on 17 & JFK.  A small is $3.00, is actually HUGE and they give you a banana with it.  If you want all (or mostly mango) it's $3.50.  They usually sell little bags of grapes or occaisionally cherries for $1 - $2 in season.  Hooray for non-junky fast food.  Hooray for fruit.  Let's hope it's clean. (I'm always leery of this.)

My friend and I went and it was a disaster.  They got the orders totally wrong, and the place was not even busy.  Yes, they are new, yes they are pricey and the turkey burger I had was tasty - but the customer service was very, very bad.  I don't think they will make it.

Meh. They were out of "Republic of Tea" Ginger Peach - so I had the Mango Ceylon (you gotta check out Repulic of Tea's website - good stuff).   They seem to have remodeled a bit and things look brighter and there is less crowding at the front of the store during the lunch "crush".  Also now they give you a buzzer so you can get a table and site while you wait for your mediocre salads, sandwiches and salty soups.  Sorry - but the food is not that great, to me.  Soups are all very salty. Beet salad had great toppings but the base was raw kale and arugula - did not thrill me.  Next time I will see if they will make it with some romaine in there.  Good news!  You can choose an apple instead of chip or a baguette.  (Guess what I got.)  Too caloric for a "healthy" choice fast food. Yet, still, my company gets LOTS and lots of lunches catered from here.
Basic hoagies and sandwiches.  Better than Subway - but nothing orgasmic.  I prefer Primo' any day.  That being said, I am glad to see another moderately priced, FAST lunch option in the area.

The 4 stars is for the burger - I did not try any other items (Fries, mayo or shakes). I got soggy sweet potato fries at L'il Dans - FAIL.  (But that's another review.)  The burger itself was on the rare side - and I had the special with a fried egg (perfectly done - a bit runny but not raw) and cheddare cheese (subbed for swiss), lettuce tomato and scallion mayo.  Perfection!   (And a calorie bomb.)  Can't wait to visit again - but not for at least 4 weeks.  $9 for just the burger.  (That can really add up if you get a $3 soda or $4 fries)

I prefer the Ardmore outpost of BM to this BUSY and revolving door of staff, Center City location.  Meanwhile this overpriced, but decent selection of high end brands, gets me my Caudalie goodies whenever I am shopping in Center City.  Sephora is nearby, so I sually buy only what I absolutely MUST have from BM.  I can't comment on their limited selection of spa services.  Happy they carry (some) Fresh and Morocanoil (the real one) produits.  Bring money - you will need it.

A solid choice in the Comcast Center - but by no means a Holy Grail. Betetr than the sit-down Mexican Post locations.  Meh-x-ican,  I usually play it safe with beans, rice and guacamole. (Or a chicken burrito) Not bad - but not mind blowing. Fairly priced. QUICK service even during the lunch rush.

4.5 stars.  We love it here and are members.  Our 4 year old adores the "Big Dig" exhibit and everyone (even bug-phobic me) likes the butterfly area.  (Wear light weight clothing - it's hot and very humid in there.)  This year the Academy had a free Members night for the members and it was great fun!  Membership pays for itself if you visit more than 3 times.  Bring food/snacks - the Cafe has a limited selection - but better than some. Pizza was dried out & nasty - but they did have yogurt, frui8t and other healthier options.

Went here last night for Lexi's big bash and it was such fun.  We had a choice of 3 beers, a white wine, a Merlot or 2 cocktails.  I had 2 of the Mojitos and they were very sweet and easy to drink.  (I'm sure Sprite was in the mix).  They also had a Sake Sangria which was Orange-Juice colored and full of fresh fruit.  I did not have it but Anjali did, and she seemed to like it.  They also served plates of thinly-sliced crsipy sweet potato chips (yum) with a supposedly-truffled, truffle sour crea.  It was tasty - but I detected little to no truffle - I was like dipping in pure sour cream.  OK - but just OK.  (Fat City!)  A few people ordered some small plates of food and everything looked nice, but I did not try any.  Pearl (now AKOYA) has re-vamped its look to be more of a club/bar and less of a fine dining place.  Many of the menu items remain, but the menu is more streamlined and focuses on muchies with an Asian flair.  Not bad.    Oh - and the bartender was a hottie and VERY attentive to all of us.  (He was workin' it.)

Seriously old and old-school.  In need of a toal property makeover (and not to mention the crappy diner next door which I think is now out of biz.).  Rooms are basic and OLD.   Ook.  Not a top choice - but it's the only choice in this immediate area in Delaware County.  please wash the comforter covers.  They look so bad.  Maybe replace them?

This is my go-to Panera when I am working near here - whenever I am maxed out on the Chipotle and Kebab Café in the same shopping plaza.  The have "Republic of Tea" hot teas - like Ginger Peach and the salads are OK.  Other items (pastas and sandwiches) have too many calories for the taste payoff.  (Might as well get a 1500 calorie burrito bowl at Chipotle versus a "meh" turkey on wheat here.  Spacious interior and less chaotic than Starbucks down the block.  I am still not 100% sold on Panera, but it'll do in a pinch.  Coworkers LOVE it here.  We suffer through bland office catering from Panera quite often. Whatever.

This review is for RAW - inside Boyd's.  Raw - the sushi & sake lunge from 12 & Sansom - opened a 2nd branch inside Boyd's Department store on the mezzanine level.  I just had lunch there today and for $13 it very well may be the only thing I can afford at Boyds!  Delicious yellowtail bento box was a steal at $13.00 and came with yummy salad, miso soup, rice, gyoza, 2 bacon-wrapped shrimp and FABULOUS tuna tartare.  I'll be bag.  And maybe I'll snag that Ferragamo dress or $3000 cashmere knit top I spotted today.  Or those fabulous Black & Gold D & G Stilletos.

I have to give B&N a BIG positive shout-out for supporting my child's school.  once or twice per school year we have a B&N day.  Teachers can make a wishlist of books they need and parents can purchase them.  Also any purchases we make that day - using a code - a portion goes to help the school.  It's a great program so I am really thankful to B&N for this. Even our purchases at the Starbucks Cafe (most of them anyway) count!  Excellent.

Such a cute place for gifts - at the holidays it gets crowded - but Quincy's is great shopping all year-round.  I love to support stores like this - owner-operated local non-chain businesses.  Full of nostalgia and charm. And hostess gifts.

Ok, maybe I am in a bad mood.  I am at a toss up between 2 and 3 stars. My "joey Bag of Donuts" chicken burrito was dry and I just didn't like the food here as much as Baja Fresh, Qdoba or Chipotle.  It sure seems like "Fast Mex Food" is all the rage these days.  I'd come back here - but not in a hurry.  And the guacamole tasted too sour.  (89 cents for a tiny side of it.)

I tried Sabrina's again - this time on a rainy weekday with my mother-in-law because it was close by.  Wish I hadn't bothered.  So "meh", poor service and overpriced. Yes, my MIL loved her ENORMOUS slices of thick french toast (more like french toast cake) with whipped cream, but my dish was just OK.  Anyhow - they are in the nabe - and if you go on a weekday when there is no line, it's fine - but it is so not worth a long waits on weekends for brunch. Tip:  call ahead to get on the list!  It's just not all that for me and I have tried it 4 or 5 times already. And I want to love it, I really do - but I just don't.

Ate at Azie on Main in Villanova (It's around the back of the shopping center next to the STAPLES) as part of a large group - 27 people - in a semi-private room.  We had a set menu which was very good - but I have a feeling the "regular" menu is even better.  Good options for pescetarians.  Nice service.  Gorgeous decor.  Will be back soon.

The manager, Greg was very pleasant and explained things well, but I wound up sitting there for 117 minutes for a 1 hour oil change (actually more because I came in early.)  The place was very busy when I came - but I managed to get an oil change and they replaced a burned out headlight & tail light.  I will return - but I may try Pep Boys next time - although they also had me waiting a long time.
Took my 10 year old and a friend here for small cups after we visited Color Me Mine next door.  Ice cream was just OK.    Not thrilled.

I can't believe that kitchenette has been here for 3 years and I have never noticed it before.  As I die-hard cookery junkie, I have shopped at many similar stores, but the lady who manages kitchenette was so cool and patient. They were having a sale (75% off ) on selected porcelain items, and I snagged a quiche dish for $3.75.  Three seventy five!  What a deal.  I also picked up 4 basic six-ounce ramekins.  (Needed 'em to make flan.)

2 - 3 star sushi (and teppanyaki/hibachi tables in the back) with over-load of sauces (get the sauce on the side) and mediocre fish.  Seemed fresh enough but obviously frozen tamago and others. I actually got sick after I ate it.  This might go to a 1 star review if I can figure out for sure that my gastric distress was from the fish.  Not a holy grail - but for $8.95 ($1 extra for ONE specialy maki) for the 2 maki lunch - with Miso Soup and Salad - it's OK.  I had a yellowtail scallion roll and the "Rose" roll - spicy tuna inside with tuna on top.  Not Great. In my opinion, Sushi Nami down the street is better. And the place was so cold inside.  (Hot green tea helped warm us up.)

3.5 stars is just about right for the food (long lines notwithstanding) I purchased at the Media Italian Festival.  It was a gorgeous day and turnout was high so the pork was nearly gone, but I was able to buy a platter with 2 meatballs and a Chicken Cutlet with broccoli rabe for $8.00.  Tasty for "festival" food. Need better menus and signage to facilitate the line.

Attended a catered event for8-10 people and it was amazing.  A delicious pasta salad with tomatoes, spinach and feta (not too salty).  Green salad wth nuts, cinnamon pears and a Maple-Walnut dressing that was so good you could drink it.  Desserts and more!  Love this place and wish I lived closer.

It's mall sushi - and believe it or not - it's safe and decent. My 5 year old loves the "free examples" (that's what she calls free samples) of the Cali roll.  Last time we got her a whole order of California rolls and asked the guy to cut them into 8 instead of 6 pieces (which he kindly did) and she ate them ALL.  Note:  I have never had any Nigiri here (I'm too scared/food-snobby) but for a cooked maki - no problema!

I can not say enough good things about the brand and the dealership. Maserati of the Main Line, Robert and Rick treated us so very well showing us cars that mere mortals only dream of.  Along with new and pre-owned Maserati they also carry a few Ferrari and other luxury vehicles.  You can design your car from the "ground up" down to every last detail, if you so choose. This is a one-of-a-kind car buying experience.  Wow!

I happen to really like L'Occitane's Shea butter based products and the Verbena fragrance line, so I was/am pleased that the Walnut Street boutique is near my office.  At holiday time they have some good deals - although I was able to snag the hand cream trio CHEAPER at Sephora down the block - slightly different packaging - same great products inside.  Staff are friendly & helpful.

I am dithering on what to rate this UPS store as I had 2 dramatically different experiences on day apart.  The first day was horrible. I actually came back the next day and even though the store was more crowded (the young lady in the back came out front to help after hanging up on a personal phone call), I had a better experience.  Do not come here if you are in a rush.  That said - they do know what they are doing and my packages were shipped without issue - please they stock inexpensive shipping supplies.

Well, my initial love affair with Oregon Diner (aka "the cookie diner" in the words of my 8 year old) has faded a bit.  Lunch was good yesterday - but the cheese ravioli was drowned in "gravy". I extricated the 6 lovely (delcious) cheese-filled pillows onto another plate. Lunch saved.  My dining partner ordered a cheese steak.  He proclaimed it "very good". Looks ok to me but it's not Tony Luke's!  Servers, as always are characters and great fun to watch.  I love it here still - but it is really more of a 3 than a 4 star place. It's "just as you remember" a good diner in Sou-filly to be.

We had a positive experience with the service department.  I called about 2 weeks ago when our dryer broke (no heat) and Tina - who answered the phone explained a few things to me about dryers (no, we did not have a clogged vent or tubing) and then their policy.  It costs 79 for the guy to come out and if there is a fixable problem they apply the 79 to the labor (99 minimum charge) and parts.  It would up costing $169.60 to fix our broken heater (coil was busted) and he had one right on his truck. I wrote a check but could have also used a credit card.  The only complaint?  I was told 9 AM - 1 PM and they came at 12:45 PM (still technically on time, but I waited almost 4 hours).  I wish they could have 2 hour windows - or more repair techs.  Our guy (Rob??) was getting sick and working his a$$ off.  Tina was a doll.  I will call again if we ever need to - but I pray we won't need to often.

It's Target.  This one is fairly nice now that they have re-habbed it slightly and moved stuff around.  We come here, seriously, every one to two weeks and always on a weekend so it can get crowded.  But they have the household cleaners, supplies and cheap kids gear that we need.  So hooray for Target.  Beats the heck outta that ghetto-like Walmart down the road.

Lately, my office crew has wanted to go to Panera so i have now been to this one quite a few times and have my "pick 2" order down to a science.  I am starting to actually like it here now - I always ask for an apple instead of the bread that comes with the meal. If I get a beverage I blow about $12 (close to $13) so I try to just get water. Otherwise my choices are about $10 - $11.  I like to stare at the baked goods in the case but I never get any.

I vacilate between 3 + 4 stars - and one time 2 stars. The first few times and also recently the sushi has been swimmingly fresh and wonderful at moshi-moshi, but about a year ago I had a very awful experience during a crowded lunch-hour.  We sat upstairs which I DO NOT RECOMMEND and were nearly forgotten about and the kitchen (cooked) meals came out all wrong.  Meanwhile - they make an addicitve Toro-Giza handroll and believe it or not the "kids Maki" with Tamago and veggies for $4.50 is a delicious treat.  It's not nearly as good as Shiroi Hana and it sure ain't Morimoto - but it is not nearly as pricey either.  It's a mid priced place with middle-of-the-road sushi.

Awesome selection of PRICEY gear and sections dedicated to yoga, pilates.  (Which I love.)  Also children's wear (limited selection).  They have a free yoga class on Sunday, too.  So neat.  Plus there are big photographs of local fitness professionals (Pilates Teacher, Karen Pecarsky among them).  I'd give it 5 stars - as it's a gorgeous store, but the prices are just Soooooo high.  But if you just have to have that custom $45 yoga mat - go for it.  It's very fun to browse here, I just wish i could afford to do more buying.

You must rush over to Capiro THIS WEEK for the most delicious and unexpected flavor yet - butternut squash.  YES, my goodness YES.  A creamy, butter, slightly squash-y (vegetal) but not too much. Unexpected and delicious.  Oh - and the fresh fig sorbetto was amazing, too.  We are truly blessed and lucky to have Capogiro right here in our own back yard.  Some of the best gelato in the nation and maybe the world (I have had the real deal in Italy - and Capogiro is the real McCoy!)  G-d bless you capogiro. And G-d bless the multiple-piercing-wearing hipster servers who graciously and patiently allow me to sample these exquisite flavors.  PLEASE bring back the mini cone!!!!

Now I think I am reviewing the right place - I saw a movie last night at the "Landmark East" theatre on 2nd Street between Chestnut & Walnut.  It was clean and there were no ticket lines.  Hardly anybody there - which made it nice.  Restrooms were clean - but I bet if it were crowded that it would not have been.  Concession area offered hot & cold beferages, popcorn, candy and snacks - plus you could purchase DVDs to take home.  The staff was friendly.  All in all we had an excellent viewing experience

We ate here after our wedding cake tasting at Night Kitchen Bakery (Yum City!) in Chestnut Hill.  Read that review!   Anyhow, Solaris seemed like a safe enough option tat would appeal to my brither and sister in law who have very simple, unadventurous tastes.  3 of the 4 of us got burgers (big surprise).
