My husband broke down and ordered the $13 Kobe beef burger whioch was very good - but not $13 good.  The regular burgers were fine.  My chicken sandwich was a little dry (the chicken was dry - the sandwich itself had cheese and a sauce on it.).  It was OK - and not mind blowing in any way.  Service was fine.  Decor was fine.  Food was Good but not great.

Stopped in here for breakfast after tootling around the Bourse to find little or nothing open at 10 AM.  It is a buffet (per pound) much like Oh so good.  It was fine.  Just OK.  Nothing stellar.  A good place to grab a quick bite - and right near all the Independence Mall touristy stuff.
It's McPaper. It's Metro It's easy to read  And there's usually a Sudoku Puzzle toward the back.  I read it when I take the R5.

Pretty awful. I have tried it twice - once back in abour 2008 when I worked nearby and got overly doughy steamed dumplings for takeout (filled with a greasy mystery meat).  YUCK.  Aside from the grotty digs and crappy location - next to the XXX rated theatre, I ventured in again.  And I will never do this again.  I played it "safe" with chicken and brocolli. I have had better food from a cart.  Never again!

Having lived in Doylestown from 1977 until 1988 and visiting often ever since (family still ives there) I have seen the hospital grow, grow, GROW into the large complex it is today.  The emergency room is well managed, and the "regular" hospital is run by a caring trained staff.  Great doctors, nurses, P.T.s, the works.  So glad they are building a new parking facility.  They need it!

I was sooooo pleasantly surprised by our group of 5's dinner (yes - try it for dinner - less crowded than the lunch rush) at a huge table (that can seat 7 or 8) in the D-town Panera (fairly new location).  While prices are a bit high for "cafe style" fast food - the soups and breads are tasty (if not caloric) and our 8 year old loved the $11 Shrimp Sandwich. Plus - somebody's gotta wash the real nowls and flatware they serve on (This is not a Saladworks!).  Some items took a long time to come out - but were worth the wait.  We'll be back for sure.
Stopped in here for a "Bagel Thin" sandwich - which wasn't bad. Clean environs and collegial service.  Nice bagel selection including egg & pumpernickel.

Back in "the day" I would occaisionally grab a bite to eat at Houston Hall when I was a grad student at PENN.  (That was, indeed, more than a few years back).  Mostly fast food options - but also a bagel place and a salad place.  Just OK - but convenient when you are on campus.

Duck Deli (so named for the original location in Duck, NC) is a great find for BBQ in Bucks County.  The owner, Chris, is terrific and the Duck Deli catered a "Backyard BBQ Bash" I threw for my husband's surprise 30th birthday in 2007.  The mac 'n cheese, pulled Pork, Beef Brisket and smoked BBQ chicken are terrific. For a lighter idea - get a caesar or house salad topped with 6 grilled shrimp.  (Big ones!)  The iced tea and lemonade freely flow into big ball-jar mugs.  My 3 year old daughter loves it - but always asks if they serve Duck.  No Duck is served at Duck Deli, but we love it just the same.

Holy smokes!  i got the lobster roll ($14.99 for 1/2 roll $16.99 on its own) with a cup of soup and an apple.  Spent just over 420 for lunch.  Yikes.  And no, it's not THAT good. I shoulda known better.  Will NOT order that (seasonal) item again.
Took gorgeous candids of my (then) 6 year old at a yelp event. Wow.

A great place to shop for Japanese groceries and products - as aforementioned.  The Okinomiyaki was kinda heavy and did not thrill me.  My little one loved the shrimp shumai, though.  I also had an avocado onigiri.  It was good - but it's pretty hard to mess that up.  They also have lots of hello kitty-themed toys & trinkets that my little one adores.  A nice find!

Between OK and Iovine's the RTM has your produce needs more than adequately met. I usually check Iovine's first and then head to Ok's for whatever did not appeal over there.  They also have good prices on bananas. Some of the discounted bagged produce you must use it right away (use it or lose it).

Cute place.  I hope they make it. Expensive coffee drinks - along the lines of Starbucks or Burlap and Bean.  Easy to get out (or in but not in (or out) since they are right on 252 and if there is traffic getting in (or out) is bad if you need to make that dreaded "left turn".  Good customer service and I love to support local businesses.

OK.  I have to tell you that I DID NOT GET TO ACTUALLY EAT HERE.  So I can not comment on the food - who friends and colleagues tell me is great. I have also been told that when they screw up, they screw up in a big way.  Well they screwed up today.   I am rating Sabrina's on the abysmal way in which I was treated this morning at 9:40 AM.  Yes - on Saturday AM's the place gets slammed - but I was BY MYSELF - solo - and could have easily been greeted and asked to sit at the counter which had 4 open stools.  Since it was before 10 (don't even think about coming at 11 on a weekend) there were even 2 tables open (where the 2 other parties got seated.)  Nevertheless the host ignored me and proceeded to seat the party before (natch) and after me and NEVER GREETED me.    I pulled a menu off of the pile on the host/hostess stand and read it for a few minutes (sounded good- medium to high prices).  Still nothing.  I just said "screw it" and left.  I hope to actually get a chance to eat here in the future.  I guess singles aren't too welcome here.  Next time I'll bring my adorable 4 year old.  I bet we'll get seated.

I'm a Chipotle fan from back in my Manhattan days - so I was glad to see one open in Warrington.  While I must admit to liking Qdoba a tad more - Chipotle is my go-to place for a Burrito Bol (Naked Burrito) with Chicken, Black Beans and Guacamole.  It's fast and cheap - but watch those calories - I never get cheese and rarely get sour cream so I can justify that guac!  This bracnh of Chipotle is in a stand-alone building (did it used to be the Pizza Hut - I forget).  It has a cool-gray ambience - a bit industrial looking.  We usally get take out, though so we don't really care.  On the Sunday afternoon when we last visited, the place was loaded with families with young children.

No issues for me - but I usually just use the ATM here.  The teller experience is not one I love, so I tend to avoid going inside unless I have to.  That said - my kid participates in TD bank's summer reading program (They give kids $10 for reading 10 books over the summer) and they are so nice to her.

OK, the reason why this place is not a 4 or even a 5 is simple.  The customer service is BAD.  Very, very snooty-snotty sales girls - some of whom would never be able to afford the high-end products IRL.  I adore Fresh and Comptoir Sud Pacifique and Diptyque and alot of the higher-end and HTF barnds that BM sells, but the sales experience is too high pressure for little old moi.  Also, the are no longer offering services the way the used to - like eyelash application or facials.  (You want a good facial?  Try Ursula's about Phace with Elina at 17 & Sansom)  Anyhow, I am glad they exist - but now with Sephora nearby and the internet at my fingertips - I will probably come in to sample and sniff and then buy elsewhere.  Sorry, snooty-ladies.

After watching numerous cups of iced tea, "fairy tea" (a red herbal and berry tisane) and sweets come out of Zen Den, we just had to try it for ourselves.  The clean, new, wood-floored decor complete with comfy seating will be a huge hit - as I'm sure will be the La Colombe coffee.  We though the Lemonade was just "OK" and the sweet tea urn was surrounded by fruit flies which kinda skeeved me out.  So we opted to mix the Lemonade with a bit of the unsweetened black tea and a few ounces of the orangey iced green tea.  Meanwhile, the brownie was just OK - a weird (soft - almost confection-like, fudge?) spreadable consistency.  More like a candy or fudge than a brownie.  Odd.  We'll be back - but won't rush back.  Wonderfully spacious and clean ladies room! Beats the hack outta Charbucks. Good service from the cute young highschool "boys" behind the counter.

Went to a private event at Boyd's last night for Philadelphia Collection 20101 (Philly's version of Fashion Week).  The theme was Bella Italia and they had great food from several vendors including DiBruno Bros., Yogorino, Le Castagne and more. Plus a DJ, live opera singers and models who posed as mannequins wear prada and gucci etc.  They had a Vespa and a Maseratti parkes out front.  It was a blast!  And my 5 year old came too (despite aghast looks from salefolk) and tried on a fabulous pair of purple & black velour Prada shoes. (And some $1300 Manolo's - she's a gal after my own heart.)  I swear I'm gonna buy them for her the minute her feet are big enough.  Too Cute.

For cheap Chinese - this place is great.  Inexpensive, relatively clean and safe. The lunch specials are usually what we get - as it is near out office.  Also try the steamed dumplings (Get the watercress kind - they seem to be home made.).  Service can get slow - as they are usually under staffed (1 waitress and the mam-san Owner/Manager) during a busy lunch time can be a bit harried.  The used to give out free ice cream - but that is over now.  (They made it past the 6 month mark.)  Did I mention the prices are sooooooo low? It ain't Susanna Foo - but for 6.99 for Shrimp & Broccoli with brown rice (not too gloppy either) I'll be back!  Oh - and they WILL deliver.

I used to work at the Mercer Museum - as a summer day camp counselor and arts & crafts supervisor MANY, many years ago.  I don't know if they run a kids sumer program here any mroe - but the one they used to have was great.  Anyhow, the Moravian Pottery & Tile works was built of  steel reinforced concrete by Henry Chapman Mercer to erve as his workshop and still produces lots of gorgeous tiles to this day..  Kids and Adults can both learn from Mercer - either here or at his home, Fontill next door.  You can also get married on the grounds and it's a great place to have a picnic in the summer or fall.

"I agree wholeheartedly . This IS the UK version of TGI Friday's.  And it's pretty Meh.  The fried fish & chips and decent - but predictably greasy and salty.  The food is bland, boring "formula" cooking and the staff are pretty bored with it all."

Once again my (now) 9 year old and I made the annual pilgrimage to Macy's, the Holiday Light Show and Chritmas Village (Dicken's).  She loves it - BUT - now the show is every 2 hours. It's mayhem.  They need to go back to every hour or 30 minutes.  Also - to have your picture taken with Santa is free - but the photos start at $16.99 (plus tax).  OUCH!

Excellent food and service from Mike at the bar and Paul our server. The Salmon Manchmanteles never disappoints me. Echiladas Mixtos were tasty, too - as were the shrimp tacos (app) and Flauta (app). Do not miss the Watermelon Margarita.  ($5 off at happy hour).  Hot churros and Tres Leche Cake were delicious.  Love it here.

I hired Meredith (very affordable and super timely) to take about 2.5 hours worth of candids for my mom's surprise 70th birthday.  Less than 4 days later, I had the disc in hand with over 200 images to choose from/  Great work!  Great pricing! Great Photography.  Thanks, Meredith!

They catered an event for me with cold salads (mozzarella balls, pasta etc.) Very good food and decent prices.  Will use again.  I should clarify - they made the food - but I had to come pick it all up.  Still - a great option.

While I would never buy a dog here (and you can adopt cats here for free.), I am upgrading Monster Pets fish & aquatic department.  We bought a 50-cent feeder fish (goldfish) for our kid - and with proper care and advice, she is thriving in a cute 2.5 gallon take with a few decorative plants.  It's been almost a month - and I hope this little fishie will have a long and healthy life. We go great advice here on first-time goldfish ownership.  Oh - and we buy oodles of Eukeneuba dog frood and Greenie Pill pockets here for our pug.

This is our local Bruster's and it is open YEAR ROUND - though much more crowded in summer.  The gals runnin' the show are friendly and kind to our 9 year old who LOVES the orange & vanilla parfaits (5 scoops of ice cream/sherbet is an obscene amount so she eaits it in 2-3 sittings.)  We like it just fine. Have been back several times now.

Still a solid, inexpensive choice for classic chinese - take out or dine in. For $7.50 - $9.50 you can get a filling lunch special (small charge for brown rice).  I ask for whatever I get to be "light on the sauce" and It's always saucy anyway. I enjoy the Chinese Eggplant with tofu or chicken and sometimes I ask them to add string beans or broccolli for $1 extra.  FAST service. LOW Prices. A solid lunch-time pick.

Super yummy ORTGANIC chocolate treats - and adorable packaging.  Those cute little ladybugs are awesome party favors or gifts.  You can get them alot more places, too, nowadays like RTM and farmer's markets as well as online.  Love the little bumble bees, too.  Yes, they are expensive (but check out other high-end cholatiers - and they are within range) but you get what you pay for here.  GREAT packaging and deliciousness inside.  (The raspberry filling is my fave - I am not a mint lover.)  Keep up the good work J&K's!
Browsed for $200 - $300 Michael Kors Watches which my kid wants. Did not purchase (yet) but the saleslady was very nice and humored us while my kid tried on a myriad of fake rose-gold-toned watches.

Oh lawd!  I just ate the most horrifc lunch at E & C.  A meatloaf sandwich - wherein the meatloaf contained multiple bone fragments.  Sooooooo disgusting,  Fortunately they took it off the bill.  I used to tolerate E & C - I will now NEVER go back on my own accord.  (Alas, some co-workers insist on dragging me here.)  BLECH!

4 stars for the drinks and 3 for the food at the bar (we sat at the bar for the 4 - 6 PM Happy Hour) with Jet.  He made us a delicious hot toddy and Irish coffee on a cold day.  Apps are pricey - even on the happy hour menu. $10 shrimp cocktail came with 6 large, deliciously seasoned shrimp and a vodka cocktail sauce.  Very good.  Can't wait to return. Menu is small but lots of good choices.

I have been to a few corporate events & seminars here - and also eaten at Keating's River Grill (separate review on yelp).  Most recently I attended a meeting on the 2nd floor in a large ballroom.  AV and amenities were just fin and the open bar and appetizers afterward were surprisingly good.  Vegetable crudite (including blanched broccoli - not raw - nice touch), Cheese and crackers,  EXCELLENT mini crab cakes with remoulade (real crab - very little filler - YUM) and deep-fried dumplings (deep fried is noy my fave).  Bartenders and servers were so friendly and pleasant.  I would consider having an event here - maybe even a wedding if you are into a "ballroom" style wedding.  Great views of the river.

Humanely raised, chemical free produce, eggs and meats (lamb, pork and poultry). Available at the Media Farmers Market on Thursdays (and Bryn Mawr on Saturdays).  Love the $4/doz. Brown eggs and $9/lb bacon. Got another lb of bacon in September, too.  LAMB!!!!  Will consider getting a 4 pack of duck breasts next time and definitely a T-giving bird!  LOVE THEM!  Credit Cards for orders over $25.

2 or 3.  We took our 5 y.o. to see Annie here - and while the production was fine - and she loved every minute, our 1st row of the family circle seats were so uncomfortable.  NO LEGROOM (and I am 5 foot 3 - DH is much taller - I can only imagine).  The place is in dire need of cleaning and new carpets/paint.  It is a majestic, old theatre that just looks, well, old.  And a bit shabby.  The air conditioning ducts had stained black onto the walls.  EEW.  Also there are only 2 ladies bathroom stalls in the family circle ladies room - and a HUGE line made this just impractical. KNOW before you go - lots of stairs.  $45 for the cheap seats?  Wow.  Not worth it.

I wanted to love it but I just thought it was "OK".  I had lunch in the dining room (cafeteria style) and had a shrimp Kebab platter.  The kebab itself was great.  The sides I chose - roasted veggies (Meh) and "braised" white beans - kinda like a thick white bean soup with way too much rosemary - would not try again.  Meanwhile, my friend's basil/pesto hummus was very tasty.  Next time I will try something else.

Cute (and brand new - open about 5 months) Korean-run cafe with bubble tea (of course) poppy-seed shakes, Korean-style shave-ice (YUM and perfect in August) and unique Korean style egg waffles (I got a chocolate one - so nice - fresh of the waffle maker).  I hope they do well!

It's another link in the Taste of Philly chain - and it's a solid one.  I had a fresh, hot, pretzel dog from the stand in front og the store at the Chestnut Hill festival.  It was so tasty (and oven fresh) that I went inside to check out the store itself.  So why was my p-dog $2.50 out front but they are only $2.00 in store?  Seemed kinda unfair.  Meanwhile, if you live in Chestnut Hill and need pretzels or pretzel-dogs for your superbowl party or some other event - definitely come here.  When they are fresh - they are pretty terrific!
Pros:  They have wheat grass juice. They have fresh squeezed OJ  Cons:  Most of the smothies contain "sorbet" or sugar containing ingredients No grapefruit juice. Pricey.
It's fine - as stadium/venues go.  Went here to see Toy Story 3 on ice with my little one.

A close female friend and I dined at Stella tonight. The weather was sublime and we sat inside - but right by the LARGE open floor to ceiling windows - so we had the best of both worlds - inside and al fresco.  We BOTH ordered a plate of the special app - a gloriously fresh mozzarella and heirloom tomato (yellow, orange, red, brown and purple) salad.  It was lightly and PERFECTLY dressed with a basil infused oil and a sweet balsamic (decent quality - not the cheap stuff, but not the 17 year old either).  It sang on the palate.  I am hankeing to try the meatball and risotto app - next time.   (And there WILL be a next time.)  Next we split a pizza.  Let me preface this by saying that I am not (shocking, I know) a pizza lover.  I am a pasta lover, but never really "get off" on pizza.    Stella's pizza is very, very good.  (My friend says it's better than Osteria - but the pie she had as Osteria was burnt.)  Thin crust - but not ridiculously thin.  (I dislike "pizza on a cracker")  Thin in the middle and medium rise (with some puffiness) on the edges.  We had #11 - Spinach.  It was a white pie with a healthy hit of garlic, toasted pine nuts (Oh, yeah, baby!!), the ideal amount of fresh, bright green, sauteed spinach, and a few heavy handed spinkles (globs?) of a sundried tomato/oil puree.  Definitely tasty - and worth a try for those of you who like spinach.  One negative?  No substitutions on pie.  They make 'em how they make 'em.  One positive?  GREAT service by our your server (can not remember her name - but she was really nice and attentive.)  Another thing... only gelatos for dessert.  We skipped dessert here and opted to get some home-made cakes at "More than Just Ice Cream".  But I bet their gelato is good.  (However, Capogiro is not too far, ya know...)  Anyhow - Starr strikes again with a good (and not overly decorated - thank goodnees) spot.  Note to the hard-working pie men (and gals):  Please keep the pies crispy on the bottom - nobody likes a soggy pie.  JOB WELL DONE.  Oh - another thing - we really wish you'd take reservations.  Thankfully at 5:30 on a May Sunday we (2 people) did not need one and were seated quickly.  Hooray!

Real-deal authentico Mexican "bodega style" - no atmosphere, tiny space and a bit "grubby" but man, the food is good.  Squash blossom quesadillas and very solid tacos al pastor.  Real Horchata, too.  Lovely service. Inexpensive.  Can't wait to return.

What a disappointment!  I had not been to the CH Mall since the late '80's and boy - considering it is under construction - it sure needs the overhaul.  The food court (supposedly brand new) was so new that it had only 2 stores - and 1 was Orange Julius.  We wound up eating at the "Bistro" which is like a little diner in the middle of the mall.  (They serve pizza, too.)  They had a Build-aBear workshop, Sephora and alot of "average" chain stores.  There is a brand new Crate & Barrel (big) and "The" Container Store on the property.  Kinda sad to see how dead that mall was on a Wednesday night in August.  I hope the construction doesn't KILL their holiday sales.

An old-fashiooned chocolate shop with a luncheonette attached - been in Wilmington since the 1890's!  Period decor and friendly old-school service.  Most of the chocolates are made upstairs on the 3rd floor.  Reasonably priced.  Have NOT tried the luncheonette yet - just the chocolates.
Not as reliable as Bolt Bus - but good in a pinch - and GREAT compared to the priceyness of AMTRAK.    We take Mega whenever we can't get a bolt that fits our needs.

Our group of 4 came here for lunch at 11:45 on what turned into an insanely busy Driday lunch rush.  You gotta come early or the waits are long.  We shared 20 wings (double fried, K-style spricy and soy) and each got entrees.  Note - way to much food.  Next time just the entrees or fewer wings.  The food was great - the Gal-bi (beef) costs $4 extra but for me it is worth it.  We like Giwa too, but Koreana is a winner in my book. I shall return.

Wanted to go to Yia across the street but it was a Monday and they were closed.  So a friend and I went to Desert Rose - and this time the food was much better than I remembered from a few years back.  I had a Chicken Shwarma platter and they gladly substituted cucumber slices for the pita bread.  The cucumber/tomato salad here is terrific and always fresh.  Moroccan Tomato soup was a tad too acidic but the pine nuts were a delicious addition.   Fresh mint tea afterward is always refreshing.  Pleasant service.

Wow - it kinda boggles the mind just how many beers, ales, ciders, lagers, stouts etc. there are.  Gotta love America for dat!    Staff is eclectic and helpful (and mostly male) with a small bar in the back to imbibe and sample while you shop.  (Bring ID - they card EVERYONE).  If you are a beer lover you will enjoy this place.

I am giving this place a good review for the nostalgia factor. Years and years (and years) ago my childhood best friend and I - who are still best friends to this day went to the "Grange Fair" every year.  And what fun it was in those days.  Rides, games and flea-markety stuff to buy (or not) and junky food.  When you are 10 or 12 - it's great fun.

Returned to Paramour - this time for Happy Hour with a picky, disgruntled colleague,  (Not Paramour's fault).  Giselle, the lovely hostess and the nice young male bartender (forgot his name) tried to smooth things over but he (my colleague) was NOT having it. He did not like the "house" wine and when he ordered a different wine, complained that the pour was too little.    Le sigh...  Meanwhile my Vodka & Soda was 1/2 price (for happy hour) and the deviled eggs here are terrific.  I know, who get's jazzed over deviled eggs?  Well I do, at Paramour.  I get all 3 peppadew or 2 peppadew and a bacon.  LOVE Paramours deviled eggs.  Wow.  My apologies to the lovely staff for my grumpy colleague. I won't be bringing him again!

Yum! Scaramuzza'a frozen pasta - available at local deli's and even at Acme. Love it! Competitively priced and cooks up straight from the frozen state.  I have gotten the Linguini, Fettucini and Manicotti.  Good stuff!

A coworker took me here for dinner and I was fully expecting good sushi (and I was not disappointed) but what really made me smile was the incredible Galbi/Kalbi!  Wow - complete with 5 panchan (potatoes, bean sprouts, kimchi, broccoli and cucumber salad).    Some of the best Korean I have had in a long while.  The spicy crunchy tuna rolls are delicious here and they have a FULL BAR. Lovely lady (owner??) served us.  Can't wait to return. Jazz once a month!

The Philly branch of Macy's will ALWAYS be Wanamaker's to me.  The Eagle statue, the Christmas Light show (which our daughter just loves) and the Dicken's Xmas Village are all great reasons to come here.  The rest of the year?  It's your typical over-priced department store.  (Though I must say I found THE perfect bras in their vast lingerie deaprtment.)  I also got a decent shirt/tie for my husband on sale in the Menswear department.  The little girls clothing is cute and if it's on sale, decently priced.  If someone gives me a gift card - I shop here.  Otherwise, not.

We buy liquor here on occaision because it is near the Reading Terminal Market.  This store is small and crowded.  I think the PA liquor laws are really strange and generally nonsensical.  A necessary evil.

OMG!  I just had one of the best lunches I have ever had in a long while. I think whether you rate this place a 4 or a 5 can depend on your viewpoint.  The service on a non-busy lunch shift is quite different than the after-work bar scene or dinner or brunch.  Décor is just lovely and service was fine - the busser was new and clueless, but the female server was terrific.  But for lunch?  Albeit a pricey one ($70 for lunch for 2 - not including drinks or desserts, including tip).  We got 2 entrees (The crab/seafood louis - which is DIVINE) and 2 apps.  The devilled eggs (We got all peppadew - normally you get one of each in a sampler, peppadew, bacon and truffle) and a crab-stuffed piquillo pepper app (2 pieces) which was ABSOLUTELY marvelous.  Not too spicy.  Akin to a crabcake with luscious sauces on the plate.  I.  LOVED. LUNCH.  here.  I'll be back as soon as my wallet can recover.  (I am thinking Bar for Happy hour.)

I am not a fan of Olive Garden and never a fan of Faux-talian, however, this 3 star review for an Olive Garden is like a 4 or 5 star review anywhere else.  For an O.G. - this is as good as it gets. You can get the "Soup, Salad and Breadstick" thing for $8.00 at lunch (no tax - it's DE.) and get in and out in 35 minutes. (Come before 1210 PM or after 1:30 PM)  Do I love it?  No, but the staff (bartender was great) was terrific and the food was, well, edible.  I never eat the breadsticks.  So salty. So carby.  Nope.  Not doin' it.

I am astounded at how good the food was here for a late lunch. The hostess, however, had a very sour disposition - perhaps tempered by thescreaming throngs of 6 year olds assembled for a noisy birthday party.  We asked to sit elsewhere.  This displeased her all the more.  But the 2 star hostess was quickly forgotten when sunny Stephanie arrived to take our drink orders.  The food came quickly and was delicious - everything from the (somewhat high priced) kids meal for the kiddo, to DH's sandwich to MIL's mushroom pizza.  I had a 1/2 order ("small plate" of pasta wit chicken, broccoli andlemon pesto.   It was great.  Honestly!  I can't believe I now like it here. Wow.

Con Murphy's accomodated our fairly large (maybe 50 people??) private event with a semi-open bar (soft drinks and selected beers and wines) and butlered hors d'ouvres.  The ladies were really young and cute and friendly as they offered platters of "goat cheese & Truffles flatbread" and sliders and mini crab cakes.  The (obviously frozen) veggie potstickers were the best of the lot IMHO.  It was a convivial setting with MANY big-screen TVs broadcasting the Phils game.   It's a bar.  It's conveniently located.  It had 2 clean unisex restrooms.  Will I rush right back here?  Nah.  But it's a great option for the nabe.

4 star food but 3 star prices.  We ordered 2 pies (1 Sicilian - plain the other a large Neapolitan with lots of toppings) and 40 wings - 10 hot, 10 BBQ and 20 mild.  The food was piping hot  when we picked it up and the food was tasty - but that cost $62 (with tax) and a free 2 liter soda.  Meanwhile - we'll order again.

OMG - horrible. Stay away.  Disinterested service that does not acknowledge when you walk in. Cheap, but overly fried and greasy food (Lunch combos are all under $6).  I drank my 85 cent diet coke and threw most of my fried (They would not make it for me steamed even though I asked) tofu and broccoli.  Brown rice (they do have it - probably a big mistake) was gluey.

Wow - much better than King of Tandoor.  We had a very inexpensive ($8-$9) lunch today at Saffron.  What a pleasant place.  The saffron colored decor with black accents, the delicious Chicken Tikka Masala, the Mango Lassi - everything was great.  2 very nice tag-team male servers.  They even made me a poori (not on the menu) and my friend had a scrumptious garlic naan.  Fresh and wonderful!  Can't wait to try it at dinner time.

They have renovated and it is super clean, freshly painted (even the restrooms are clean and fresh) and just a GREAT place to either have a party (kids or adults bowling/birthday party) or rent a lane and bowl for a couple of hours.  Very nice!

Maybe I am getting jaded after 7 consecutive flower shows and annual Household memberships in the PHS, but this year's show was not great.  Sorry.  First part was our fault - we went on a Saturday. Fail.  Crowded beyond belief.  2nd part was their fault - lots of wilted exhitbits and fewer "big ticket" displays.  The new Horticort is great though.  We'll go ONE more time next year - but only if I can haul my a$$ in from the 'burbs.
Yay!  D-town got a Primo's!  I like the Nonna's veggie (as a wrap) or the Milno.  The fresh mozzarella is so good on the sandwiches here.  LOVE PRIMO'S.

I am absolutely astounded at how good the food was here for a late lunch with our party of 7.  The hostess, however, had an unfriendly disposition - perhaps tempered by thescreaming throngs of 6 year olds assembled for a noisy birthday party.  We asked to sit elsewhere.  This displeased her all the more.  But the 2 star hostess was quickly forgotten when our sunny female server arrived to take our drink orders.  The food came quickly and was delicious - everything from the (somewhat high priced) kids meal for the kiddo, to DH's sandwich to MIL's mushroom pizza. They also have a full bar - so I had a (well) vodka and cranberry juice.  I had a 1/2 order ("small plate") of pasta with shrimp and a few chunks of lobster in a scampi-esque sauce.   It was great.  Honestly! (I asked for it light on the sauce so it was not swimming in oil.  YAY!)  I can't believe I now like it here. A chain. Who knew that would be possible?

The food tastes fine - and the cafeteria style of "design your own" burritos, tacos and quesadillas is catching on fast -but don't be fooled.  It's still fast food - and it is super-duper HIGH in calories.  A typical burrito has 1100 - 1600 calories.  (Naked will reduce it by 330 - as the PLAIN TORTILLA is 330 whopping calories alone.)  That said - I do enjoy the Naked Chicked Burrito, no cheese, small (70 cal) taco-sized torilla on the side.  It's just too hard for me to "hold the guac" and save 220 calories.  That guac - for fast food guac tastes muy bien to me.  Also "Dan" the manager at this location is very good - he catered a small event for my group and it went well (Naked Burrito Bar and lots of different salsas).  By the way - I think Jack-in-the-box owns Qdoba - I know Chipotle is owned by McDonalds.  FAST FOOD - people. Eat under a health advisory.  Note:  In the summer they make a very tasty mango salsa.  You can get it on ANY burrito if you ask.

Vacilating between 3 & 4 stars. We came here with a party of 6 (2 little kids and 4 adults) and sat outside on the roof deck upstairs (NICE!!!).  The mesh staircase freaked out my kid pretty badly (and me, too!).  Meanwhile our server was so patient and kind.  Brought the kids "mocktails" in martini glasses and extra slices of orange to nibble on.  We all shared a mushroom pizza - very good. Lasagna cupcakes were a cute idea, but poorly executed (dry pasta on the bottom, huge glob of ricotta on top).  Maybe some more sauce?  The best bite for me was the beet salad - a lettuce-free composed plate of red and golden beets, sliced almonds, thinly slice cucumber and a medallion of yummy (and not too goaty) goat cheese.  Sweet and tasty (albeit, perhaps, a bit too sweet on the dressing).  Would re-order for sure.  A fun place for a post-Arden-theatre bite.  Even the cast eats here!

Epic fail. I should have known better after my kinda-sorta-bad experience the first time.  I stopped by to pick up a toasted english muffin. I saw a sign for grits - $1.99.  So I ordered that too.  The lady scooped and scraped the grits from the bottom of the steam-pan and then shouted, "Guys, we're gonna need more grits!". But she had enough for my order. When I ate it back at my office the grits were so salty I literally spit out the first bite and trashed it.  Meanwhile, the english muffin was barely toasted and flabby.  I called them - and they have agreed to refund my $1.99 when I stop in tomorrow - but that will be the last time I come here.  So disappointing.  Many of my colleagues come here every day and love it - but they are now 2 for 2 in the "bad" category with me.

Average VS in the Plymouth meeting mall.  Fortunately it was not at all crowded on the Sunday afternoon in August when my teen daughter and I went to buy her a bra and snag our "free" panties. No issues.  Update:  Sept. 2017 - new Associate Gianna just started and she is very helpful and good. Got our 5 for $28 panties and left.

This is now our go-to Tar-Jay, however over the last 4 years it has gotten dirtier, less organized and the staff just generally seem disinterested.  (Checkers)  In general we find what we need here - but we do not get many groceries here. The shoe department is a HOT mess. The cosmetics department is fine - in fact sometimes better deal on the same stuff at Ulta. (next door there is an Ulta that my 11 year old girlie-girl just LOVES).  So yes, we still shop at Target in Springfield - but no, it's not as good as it was years ago.

I joined Philly Foodworks in the spring on 2019 after taking a few years hiatus from my old CSA.  I love that you can customize the boxes and add meat, dairy and pantry items.  The user interface is not super easy, but the customer service from Dylan and the team is so great that I don't care.  I just email changes to them if I can't get the website to work, but I almost always can.  I get an egg subscription too, and if I need to cancel it one week or three?  Nobody minds.  There is a $28 minimum (easy to meet - organic veggies are not cheap) but everything is fresh and so delicious.  LOVE, LOVE, LOVE!
This is the Starbucks in the Lawrence Park Shopping center and it is fine.  Bathrooms are closed due to Covid and the service can vary based on who is working.  No issues.
It's just OK.  The atmosphere is about 1 star - the food about 4.  Good for delivery to "the office".  A Mandarin Restaurant on 20th is better and Square on Square is even better.

As with most Starr establishments, Parc is style over substance.  Many of the "French Bistro" touches are spot on - like the $10 French Onion Soup - which is EXCELLENT, down to the fixtures in the W.C.  Service was odd.  Great at first when we arrived at 6:15 and once we hit 8 PM it was spotty - we were sometimes ignored (like when the soup arrived with no spoons) and then at times hovered over.  In our party of 3 only one of us ordered a "true" entree - Branzino - which was delicious.  My friend and I decided to share the duck liver mousse (delicious and light - but small amount of mousse and HUGE amount of grain mustard - I mean, who needs THAT much mustard.)  It was also served sans cornichons - a sacrilege - but 3 small french pickles were brought right away (thankfully for no charge) upon request.  The seafood cocktails - shrimp, crab (2 legs for $18 - ouch) and lobster all were effortless to eat.  ($16 for 4 shrimp - eeek!)  My friend and I were still hungry so she got the French onion soup (and I helped!) which quickly killed our appetites.  (Heavy - but sweet and not to salty and delicious.)  Profiteroles for dessert were very good but not orgasmic.  (And I had been eye-ing them all evening.)  So would I return?  Hell, yes!  But will I run right back?  Heck, no!

I had an amazingly good first experience with Sweet Freedom.  I spoke to a very pleasant lady on the phone who put aside 6 vanilla cupcakes for my vegan teen's birthday.  When I came to pick them up they were boxed and ready.   I also wound up getting 6 more cupcakes in assorted flavors, chocolate, salted caramel and triple berry.  My kid loved them and shared with her friends.  Good vegan desserts are a blessing.  Thanks, sweet freedom, for supporting our animal-free diet.

A solid place for take-out - does not seem to be as popular for dine in. Pizza, Garlic knots, Focaccia (fresh) and Salads (big!) were all solid and did not disappoint.  Friendly service.  Restroom was moderately scary.  Needs to be cleaned more often.  They also have a soda fountain like the ones at Wawa where you can make any flavor drink you can imagine.  Good pizza and a huge variety of slices or (better yet) get a whole pie baked fresh.

1 star for food but 4 star service from our 2 female servers and the chic Manager on Duty. We had a private part for 10 on a Sunday for lunch,  My food was inedible but the other folks snarfed theirs down. So salty/oily (Shrimp Scampi) and even though I asked for the pasta to be cooked al dente, I do not think they know the meaning of those words.  Not a fan and never will be. My in-laws family loves it here for whatever reason so every year or two I get dragged along.  This is NOT Italian food.  This is formula cooking administered by college kids.

It really depends what you order and HOW you order it here. My friend and I (a different friend this time) had lunch at Mazzella's today and the food was much improved.  He had the $6.00 special - a grilled Italian hoagie which was basically a pork-fest on a bun, served with a giant pile of (quite tasty) fries.  I had the chicken marsala, which for $14.50 was an enormous portion (I took about half of it back to the office!) and a surprisignly fresh, tasty salad.  Not bad.  Still not AWESOME, but very passable for a quick, mid-priced (Unless you are getting a special or a slice, it's not cheap) lunch.

My colleague brought in cookies and muffins to share with the team from Pure Bread and the Red Velvet/chocolate chip muffin (or, shall I say unfrosted cupcake) was terrific! I had half - but now I want another half!  I am sufficiently sugared-up for the day.

Just a 3 star meal today - but it was Mother's Day - a historically bad day on which to dine out (everybody and their "mother" is out).  Sarah was an excellent server.  Food was heavily salted (bread sticks, steamed broccoli, mashed potatoes - all way too salty).

Still love getting the occasional item from Canter Hill at the Media Farmer's market - they are there every Thursday.  Got a 4-pack of frozen duck breasts ($14 per pound - sometimes on sale for $12 per pound). I only wish they were individually frozen so I could cook one or two at a time.  Great people producing humanely raised meats and poultry.  LOVE!

I have driven past Maria's many times but finally stopped inside and am I ever glad that I did!  The butter cake, strawberry shortcakes (we got a mini size for $4.25 in the refrigerated case) and cookies are all delicious.  The service from the 2 young ladies was great, too.  I would definitely order a birthday or wedding cake from here if I were local to this area.  Yes, it's more expensive than Acme - but way better quality. So good.  Love Maria's!

We are now coming here about every 3 months so that I can have my shakshuka fix. That and the beef short ribs and silky-smooth hummus are faves. The tomato soup with Manchego cheese shaved over the top is worth a try, too, if you like tomato soup.   Don't miss the fresh mint tea, too. Great service the last few times.  Very happy now!

Just OK. Sorry - folks - but I am not 100% sure of the sourcing here (much is farmed, and frozen - as with most fish in the US.)  They do have fair prices and a good selection, but aside from Shrimp - I rarely buy my fin-fare here.  I get salmon from a CSA and other fish from other places.  I would never get my salmon here. It is not from a sustainable source. Sorry to rain on everyone's parade.

Good news!  Media Bean Company now brings their fabulous breads, pies, FOCCACIA PIZZA ($4 a slice and worth every penny) and artesanal baked good to the Media Farmers Market on Sundays from 9 AM - 1 PM.  We just love that pizza - especially the kind with fresh mozzarella, fresh basil (with or without a balsamic drizzle).  My 13 year old gets 2 slices to go from the market and they are usually mostly gone by the time we drive home.  Soooooo delicious - and supports working people with disabilities.  Keep it up, Media Bean Co!

Stopped in famished in a dead-empty summer Sunday. Had a very good lobster bisque and a boring side salad.  A real bar, with decent food.   Friendly service from Liz. I will come back one Wednesday night for Quizzo.

For better or for worse, Philly is MY city.  (No, it is not the 6th Borough of New York City).  The restaurant scene is strong and getting better all the time. Shopping districts are improving. Yes, there is still a huge problem with poverty and street crime.  We have come a long way and we will continue to get better.

Still only 3 stars.  Got a schwarma rice platter for lunch and meat was still dry - albeit fresher than at dinner time.  DO NOT COME HERE AFTER 2 PM.  Female cashier was friendly and kind. Rice was fresher at lunchtime.  $8.00 and change. (no drink).

Absolutely "as good as it gets" for an "adult"  (AKA sex shoppe). The owner was a bit chatty - and I'm really, really private about this kinda stuff - but DH & I had a nice browse through that got us thinking.  Some of the items are kinda pricey - but I am not really a comparison shopper of sex toys.  Need a new Rabbit Pearl? Come here.

I think it says alot that downtown Media now has 2 bubble tea joints and soon will have 2 dim sum spots.  Meanwhile, Kung Fu Tea is brand new (about a month old) and spacious and clean with a ton of sugar-laden tea and coffee/tea and slush and bubble-tea choices.  They also offer rice balls and crepes (Did not try yet).  Speedy service (they call your number so hang on to your recepit), so sit in a booth or on a comfy couch and play a game of Jenga or Uno.  Then, sip and enjoy.  A great spot! Boba Tiki needs to watch out.

Martine's is just OK.  It get's crammed with summer tourists and the food is nothing special (at least for me).  It is a respite from walking around town, though and in winter they have hearty soups.  Pros:  Right on the river, great view Cons:  Tourist Filled (but what isn't in summer in NHPA?), Blah unmemorable food.

You're kidding? Based on grungy digs alone my family (of 3) walked in and out.  This is clearly a take-out only place (a few card tables and zero atmosphere for dining in.)  The sushi case was empty. Empty.  There is no way I would get sushi here. I am reticent to even try the Chinese food.  Maybe it is, "all that". But I was scared to even go there.
Great for take out. Fabulous Gyro sandwiches, platters, kebabbs and afghan delights including fried cauliflower and (oily but good) eggplant.  Spinach is great, too.  Love it here!

Quaker City was my old law firm's go-to company.  We had a voucher system (so that the firm would pay for the cabs) and it worked very well.  Independently I will sometimes call Quaker City when I can't get a car from Philadelphia Coach.  Some of the cars are very nice and well maintained - others less so - and one smelled awful.  It's on a car by car basis - as are most of the cab companies in Philly.  My list of companies I use (and the order I call them:):  1.  Philadelphia Coach (215) 744-7777 2.  Quaker City 3.  Olde City Taxi

Peri at Night Kitchen bakery did our (gorgeous) 3 tiered wedding cake in 2008.  It was beautiful to look at and 2 of the 3 tiers were delicious.  The top tier was white cake with Lemon curd and it was slightly dry, but the middle tier (carrot cake no raisins) and bottom tier (Moist deep chocolate cake with chocolate mousse) were both scrumptious.  The cakes here are made with love and attention to detail.  I recommend them highly.

I can't say enough great things about Dylan, James and the entire Philly Foodworks team.  I am a subscribing member now and I just love this service and the best local, seasonal produce around.  So great!

OK, here's the secret to having a 5 star experience at Amada - go on a slower night (like a Monday during the summer) so that you can be seated comfortably and the noise level won't be too deafening (this is a LOUD, busy place).  Go with a crowd - we had 7 ladies and ordered 2 plates each.  Sounds like not enough?  WRONG!!!  Many of the choices are heavy. (Even at tapas size.)  Standouts amoung the 14 different items we tried?  Gambas (your basic garlic shrimp - done just right), Flatbread with Artichokes (divine), Yellow tomato gazpacho (perfect on a summer night) was garnished with crab salad and avocado ice cream (Yes - a savory icecream pluche).  The crab-stuffed peppers were so incredibly creamy, crabby and tasty we ordered one more plateful.  (So I guess we had 15 dishes among 7 ladies).  The plate of veggies (can't remember the name) was simple and perfect - tomato, pepper, onion and a delectable eggplant dip.  It was accompanied by crispy-thin bread smeared lightly with a chive goat cheese.  HEAVENLY.  Lamb meatballs were too rare (nearly raw)  for most of the groups liking, but the sherry cream sauce and fresh green peas were tasty.  The salad with figs and blue cheese came literally wrapped in Jamon.  Weird and not my bag - but it, too, disappeared.  Meanwhile, they ARE heavy handed with the salt and the (salty) cheeses - so if you KNOW this (you, smart -yelper-who-pre-reads before you go, you!)  Ask for items light on the (salt) (Cheese) (Sauce) etc.  I can't wait to come back here - at an off time - with more than 2 other people.  2 dishes apiece for 7 people came to $280 (including tax 'n tip) including ONE sangria each.  (Well, not I, I had 2 virgin mojitos with a splash of pineapple juice).    Jose, baby,  you live up to your hype.  And I have now been to all 5 Philly Garces joints.  Huzzah!  Oh - and if you don't eat pork or shellfish - you'll have a TOUGH time here.  And if you are vegan - fuggedaboutit!  (Dairy is hidden in things)

My husband and I had a "date night" here on a fairly slow Saturday night. Everything was smooth and easy from the web-based lane reservation process to the clean lanes, to the slick bottoms of the rental shoes.  We bowled 3 games each and had a great time.  Can't wait to take our 8 year old here. No, it's not a chi-chi North Bowl - but this is old school bowling in a clean (even the ladies room was clean!) well-lit environment.  And there is a snack bar - and arcade area.  FUN TIMES!

I really, really want to give them 4 or 5 stars because the concept ROCKS (Think Maoz meets Qdoba) and the guys who run the place are really nice, but - there are a few things that need working out first.  I came to Zaffron for dinner (mistake number 1 on my part - you'll see why) while running a last minute Victoria's Secret coupon redemption run. I rarely eat in the food court unless I have my 6 year old with me (She likes the California Rolls from Sarku - go figure, and Saladworks, and Chik-fil-A on the rare occaision I'll let her get it.)  So I headed over to Spice (the Indian Joint) and saw this place - brand spankin' new (2months old really).    I ordered a Schwarma platter and jazzed it up with lots of cucumbers, tomatoes, chick peas and olives.  Everything has potential - but the meat was DRY (It had been precut - likely at lunchtime - the Schwarma Spit was empty by the time I got there) and some of it was crunchy - and not in a good way.  Also the rice had been siting around a little long - great flavor - but tasted like the remnants of lunch.  Again, this is probably "my bad" and I bet at lunch when the turnover is higher, the food is likely fresher and tastier - but meanwhile - I can;t wait to go back (at 11:30 pre-lunch line crowd) and give them another try.  The 2 dudes ahead of me orderes $2.00 side of falafel (3 balls per side) and that seems just about perfect.    Also I did not try the hummus which looked awesome - and for just $.50 you can add a bunch of mix-ins and toppings, if you care to.  Owners are 3 culinary partners and the one I met tonight was a sweetie.  I intend to try them again and re-yelp - hoefully with more stars.  Keep it FRESH - from first client to last - and you'll have more dinner business.  Also - I noticed they open at 9 AM - I wonder if they'll offer breakfast?  Shakshouka to go?  Price is "Philadelphia Lunch" approriate - $8 - $10 (more if you dare to get a beverage.)

This is pretty much "As good as it gets" for a Dollar Stiore - huge, clean, spacious, well-run store - complete with $.99 balloons (great for parties - order 1-2 days in advnace), convenient hours (even Sunday) and school supplies "on the cheap".  My 9 year old gets goodie for her "goodie bags" for her parties here - and also paper goods for some parties (Party City has more and is a bit higher prices).  My one caveat?  NEVER purchase food/consumables at Dollar Stores.  But for a Dollar Store?  This one is GREAT - and they have a nice big parking lot.

I took my 7 year old daughter here and wound up having "the haircut experience from hell".  My kid had a HUGE tantrum - would not see Kevin - because he's male, so we saw Lauren - a sweet gal with Cobalt blue hair.  My kid was so bad that poor Lauren could not possibly get a good cut on her - and my kid refused to be shampooed. I would like to go back but i'm, frankly, too embarrased to show my face in there.  Lauren - you're a trooper for putting up with these shenanigans!  Meanwhile the salon has Avenda and MoroccanOil products.  Odd stations with a shampoo bowl in each little "cubby" (a bit claustrophobic and dated looking with enormous green Belevdere styling chairs circa 1983.  Like I said - I'll probably be back - but I'll leave the "little angel" at home.  $16 for a kids cut.  I gave the poor stylist a $10. My kid looked like a shorn sheep. (Bangs were nice and straight and short, though.)  It was my kids fault - not the stylist.

Got a simple take out order of Chicken with Broccoli (light sauce), brown rice, steamed pork dumplings (so tasty) and classic Moo Shu Pork.   Everything was terrific.  Very impressed as my expectations were low - I usually don't like Chinese - too greasy and many have "gloppy" sauces.  This did not.    Wow.  I will be back - and maybe dine in next time so I can try their Peking Duck - if a place does Moo Shu well (good pancakes, hoi sin) they MIGHT just do the duck well.  THANK YOU!

I agree with Dave H.  Bucks County is sorely lacking in the Thai Department.  (And how I loves me a good Thai meal - especially that Tom Kha Gai!)  Meanwhile - Siam Cuisine does a very nice job in holding me over for West Coast Thai.  Prices are moderate, service is good and food is tatsy (if predictable.).  Even had a nice DUCK breast dish a while back.  My parent's are old-school and to them Italian is adventurous - so I can't get them to go there too much - but I did manage to get them to go with me once years ago and I my mom liked the Chicken Basil Curry.  I will definitely be back.

Oh how I want to love this place - the owners are terrific and big supporters of my kid's school.  The staff is friendly enough but...  1.  They close too early (I came at 8 and they were sweeping up) 2.  The food itself is just OK (Sure, this ain't Zahav - and the prices are cheaper but my hummus platter was Drowning in an Olive Oil slick.) 3.  Service was extremely slow (friendly, but slow) so don't come here in a rush.  Place was nearly empty, too - so why so slow??  Next time I will get no Olive Oil and tahini on the side. Grilled eggplant was burnt tasting (too charred). A plus?  The chopped tomato and cucumber salad served as a side was FRESH and tasty.  I adore this type of cuisine - and the pita bread here is light, fluffy and fresh (5 star baked on premises) but the other food just wasn't "all that".  Next time I will get pita and salad and skip the greasy hummus plate.

Nope.   Fail.   They carry the Eukeneuba my pooch prefers but at nearly $3 per bag more. Even with a 15% off coupon I still paid more that at Delchester Feed.  I have one more coupon - this one is for $5 off a bag - and if they honor it i will use it, get my Eukeneuba and not return.  Overpriced!

It took me 4 years to return to Bellini Grill, and I must say that at the Beginning of our evening I had my faith restored, briefly.  A good friend and I enjoyed our meal here but the super-high notes that started our evening gradually sunk lower and lower.  Firstly, the restaurant was very slow - maybe 3 or 4 tables - when we arrived at 6 or 6:15 PM on a Friday.  We were greeted and our coats were taken.  I immediately noticed that the place looks much differently (and better!) than it did 4 years ago.  Most notable were the painted murals on the ceiling and walls - complete with a "Caesar-like" portrait of the owner on the wall.  One of the specials that night was a shrimp appetizer ($14.95 - ouch!) that fortunately, seemed to justify the high price.  It was outstanding.  I ordered the Caprese Salad with much trepidation.  Winter tomatoes usually disappoint.  Luckily, this Caprese was Excellent - and lightly drizzled with an olive-oil/balsamic/pesto that was bread-dippin' worthy.  The special fishes that night were Branzino and Sole - so just for kicks I asked - and (as expected) the price was super-high - $41!  I could not order it.  Both of us ordered veal dishes which both had flaws - but luckily - delicious thinly-pounded tender veal.  My dish came with 2 tiny lumps of succulent crabmeat.  (So after giving one to my friend - I basically got one bite of crabmeat.  Oh well.)  My dish was also drowning in a heavy butter and lemon sauce - that almost seemed like "Knorr" Hollandaise from a packet.  I nearly ordered the dish "Light on the sauce" and now, I wish I had.  My friend's Veal Saltimboca was great.  By now, the place was hoppin' - so our service began to suffer.  At $8 - $10 each (and $9 for a single cannoli) we skipped dessert.  I really, really wanted a latte - but they were $5.25 (yikes) - so we both ordered decaf coffees.  FAIL!  My coffee had coffee grounds all over the rim of the mug.  The coffee itself was not hot - and tasted awful.  My friend had to ask for cream multiple times (I had wanted milk, and she cream - but they brought only milk.) At $2.50 percup/mug - we were glad to not be charged for coffee we could not drink.  Note:  This place is a BYO - which I had forgotten, and seems odd given the name (Bellini) is a cocktail.  Also Note:  They added a 20% "Service Charge/Gratuity" without us asking.  In this case, I would have left maybe 18% given the service decline at the end of the evening.  That kind pissed us off.   When all is said and done, I would return to Bellini - but I would order dishes lightly sauced and ask more questions before ordering.  I also would NEVER order coffee nor dessert here.  (At my local Italian bakery I can get a small cannoli for $1.75, large for $3.00 - but I am very lucky to live right near one.)

Blue Mercury is a chain and a pricey one at that - but this is where I get my Caudalie and Fresh fix. Today I literally spent 2 minutes in the store - got my 6.7 ounce $24 bottle of Caudalie Eau de Raisin (a must have - read my reviews on makeupalley.com).  But not before spritzing myself with Jo Malone's classic orange blossom fragrance.  I. Love. Cosmetics.  Blue Mercury is a good place to pick up hair, skin and cosmetic products from higher-end brands.

@Christopher - they had a Belgian called Delirium Tremmens tonight. Interesting brews for sure here. (8.5% alc.)  I had avoided coming here for years. Really. Years.  I had such bad experiences with the Uno (then called Pizzeria Uno) in the early '90's that I just never wanted to deal.  So tongiht our party of 7 dined for aboout $100 - very reasonable (But few of us ordered alcohol - and no apps, no desserts).  My 6 year old loves it here and - get this - gobbled up all of the steamed broccoli.  The side order of steamed broc is $2.99 and worth every penny.  I got one for me and one for her (along with our pasta dishes.  Wow.  My faith has been restored in Uno - and Steven our young server was very friendly and had a great attitude - and the hostess Lori (sp??) addressed me by name - twice.  Oh - and ironically nobody ordered pizza.  And we all enjoyed or pastas, burgers and chicken dishes. Great for kids and families.   Such a pleasant surprise.

Had a great and moderately priced (no longer cheap!) large lunch here (we took a bunch home).  Great service and tasty basic diner food.  Excellent soup.  I love diners!  Huge menu - eat breakfast whenever you like. Nicer than the Melrose (IMO).  Food at Oregon Diner is a little bit better (also MHO).

Noisy, Crowded and way way way overpriced. My lunch today was $33 ($66 for 2 - we split it) no alcohol, no dessert.  The Shrimp salad (delish) was $18.50 and we shared a tuna tartare $10.50 She had a beet salad and a $5 Coffee.  How this adds up to $66 is beyond me.  Anyhow I will NOT be back anytime soon. Wonderful food and people watching but just too $$rich$$ for my blood.  Left hungry and broke.  .

Dayum!  I wish I had read my old reviews.  I got the schwarma - again pre-cut meat (at lunch - 11:50 AM) and bone-dry and COLD.  So I had a salad with cold, dry meat on top and threw away most of the meat.  Just icky.  I added some sauces and toppings but was told hummus is $.79 extra.  What???  And the have no baba ghannoush.  There are so many fast-casual Med spots (CaVa, Naya, Naf Naf) that I will not be returning to Zaffron.  Just skip this place and eat elsewhere in the Liberty Place Food Court. There is a reason their line is shorter than the others.  Not happy. Not happy at all.

Better than Granite Run (now defunct), Better than the $h!tty Gallery in Philly, but not as nice as K of P.  It's a MALL!  This one has a Target and an Ulta as well.  The era of the "80's mall-mecca is darned near over.  Disney Store, Claire's, Build-A-Bear, Children's Place - all stuff our 8 year old appreciates.  It's fine - and I am glad it's here (I live in Target). No issues from me.  Updated 2018 - Granite Run Mall has been demolished to build a new shopping/dining area.  Springfield Mall is hanging on for a few more years.  Target and Ulta (and possibly Macy's) are keeping things alive.
this is our go-to Wawa WITH Gas - and it is always busy but you can get in & out fast.  no issues.

This place - as many, many others have said is a hidden gem with really, truly good and inexpensive Mexican food.  The Huaracche (I got mine with Al Pastor) was $7.50 and enormous.  Home-made horchata and a variety of aqua fresca.  Plus you can shop for REAL Mexican goods and groceries.  Our server Jeanette (sp??) was a doll.  Can't wait to return. It almost makes Norristown bearable.

My 11 year old will occasionally want to come here - and they are open all year -round (but of course, busier in summer).  Prices are a little high - but ice cream, parfaits and other treats are very good and service is just swell.  One day a week (Thursday? I forget) there is a deal if you BYOB (Bring Your Own Banana) for a cheaper banana split.  I thought this was a scream - but we have never done it.  Imagine... BYO Banana!!!  Cracks me up.  Also if your small child is under a certain height they get a free kiddie cone.

Sorry - but they not only followed me and my 12 year old around the store as if we were going to steal things, they then tried to overcharge my kid when she purchsed two $1 each "crystal" hair pins.  For the birds.  Nope.

They screw up orders here alot so be specific and be careful to check your order before you leave (if you are doing take out).  That said, they always fix it if they mess up but time is money and I need to go, go, GO!  We ordered a few items for 2 diners (to go) and it was accidentally entered as dine-in so we had to wait  (additionally) while they packed it. My kid is a vegan so there are always specifics like "no cheese" and switching of the bread.  Another time they got a few items flat out wrong.  Again, check, check, check your order.  Front desk clerks/cashiers - please be diligent in your order entry. Again - this is fast food run by teens so do not expect "the Ritz".  Moderately clean restrooms.  Dining room was fine.  (Although we rarely dine in - we are to-go people.)  One of the disgruntled ex-Chick-Fil-A people works here now. Please smile - you look so much better if you smile.

I used to eat at the Full Moon many moons ago - so boy was I glad to find that it's still Egg-cellent after all these many moons!  Yesterday my huband, 6 year old and 2 cousins met for a noon-time brunch at the Full Moon (they also serve dinner - once a month on the Full Moon).  I had a decadent crab, tomato & spinach topped eggs benedict - one of the best I've ever eaten.  Service was great - the place is small and they don't take reservations - so come early or be prepared for a bit of a wait.  (We lucked out and were seated right away.)  Nice waitstaff, great food in a moon-decored casual atmosphere.  Now, if only I could explain to my 6 year old not to moon people.

OK, I am going to be generous and give Carousel Flowers (the NEW Carousel Flowers) 3 stars.  If it were the old owner, Frank Grau - I would give him 1 or even ZERO Stars.)  Years & Years ago - as a young tween/teen I worked for Frank Grau's Carousel Flowers and he was a complete jerk to me.  It got so bad I had to have my dad come with me when I quit (I was probably 13 years old).  Before that I had worked at a different florist (a few of them, actually) in Doylestown and had a great experience.  My goal back then was to become a floriculturist.  In any case, it was a learning experience - and it is amazing that even after 2 location changes, Carousel Flowers is still there.

Much improved!  (That renovation period was the pits) A new clean food court with decent sushi, crepes, DQ/Orange Julius, A&W Rootbeer (aka fried food nightmare) and Taco Hell.  My littel one loves Build-a-Bear workshop, and I usually can find what I need at Kitchen Kapers.  (Love it!)  There is also a Maggiano's, a Seasons 52, Bahama Breeze (meh!) and a BIG crate & Barrell in the parking lot of the mall.  And - NORDSTROMS!

Just Salad is Just OK.  It wasn't bad and it wasn't mind-blowing. It was a bit pricier than Saladworks but also had a few more "yuppie type" ingredients.  That said, the "California" salad I ordered (kinda like a Cobb without bacon) was romaine, chicken, tomatoes, avocado and egg whites.  The lady serving it had quite a 'tude.  Not friendly service at all.  Meanwhile I enjoined the Maple Cider (read sweet as sugar) vinaigrette. The teeny blue plastic fork was a joke.  In the mean time I prefer other salad chains better and will not be rushing back here - however 2 of my coworkers love it so I bet - I just bet we'll be back.  Not a holy grail, but not an epic fail.  Just Salad. Just OK.
Heather is well qualified as an aesthetician and explains things very well. Try the Hydrofacial - it is pricey but visible results! She is a caring, kind and patient practitioner.  Excellent!
A full service Wawa with clean restrooms and a gas station.  Can get crowded but service is always quick and friendly with all the staples that every Wawa has.  I come here about 4-6 times per year.

Sabrina's - you have redeemed yourself.  (or maybe I've just figured out when to come and what to order??)  I dined solo (and was greeted and served promptly and properly) tonight and enjoyed a 1/2 sandwich, soup and salad ($1.00 extra for salad instead of fries).  The plate also had a home-made slaw of cabbage, carrot and sweetened, dried cranberries.  A nice plate!  Also enjoyed my (you betcha!) Arnold Palmer.  Iskra was a doll and I am now much more optimistic about Sabrina's. When they get it right, they really get it right (and when they screw up - the screw up bigtime.)  Here's my take - DO NOT GO at brunch/breakfast time.  Come here for dinner. And try the stuffed (dessert posing as breakfast) french toast.

Every time I am dragged to Uno I am amazed that it is as good as it is.  My dad and I came here during COVID (masks on) and sat in the empty bar area and a bar-booth.  We both had burgers.  BIG (8 oz) juicy, perfectly cooked and topped with whatever you wish (I had Cheddar, tomato and lettuce).  I was able to get steamed broccoli instead of fries.  Yay!  Honestly? It was really good.  For a chain.  The key is NOT getting pizza, I think.

This is a review of the spa area only - not the medical stuff and not the hair salon area. The locker rooms needed attention - showers were lined with little pieces of soap from other guests.  (Eew) And there was NO conditioner (I came at about 6 PM). Used robes and slippers littered the restroom area.  That aside - my actual massage was a REAL lomi lomi by Vicki who is a gifted healer. I had only had one Lomi Lomi ever before and that was on Maui years and years ago.  Vicki's came close.  For $130 - not sure I would do this, but for the special price of $99 (plus a dear friend got me a gift card) - I was all-in.  The brine room is way overhyped- basically it's a lounge with annoying and ever-changing LED colored lights.  The salt crystals are nice.  They also have a real Rassul (mud) room and a Steamed Hay treatment (not my thing).  For an everyday massage - I would not waste the money here - it is soooooo expensive, but for aspecial treat - or a party with friends (that Brine room can seat 6 people easily) it's fine.  They also throw in a complimentary foot soak (lavender or peppermint in a copper bowl of water.  Whoo-hoo!  This place is a little gimmicky - but if the therapists are good (which they seem to be) - I'll go with it.  Overhyped, overpriced and gimmicky - but deep down - a good spa. And if you get a chance for a lomi lomi (Vicki is the only practitioner who does 'em) or a Lotus - try it out.  P.S.  You MUST tip in cash - so bring plenty.

It's more like 3.5 stars - but I am giving them four to be generous.  The dark, slightly in need of a make-over Morracan digs are a great place to crash on a cusion or low couch with a crowd on a Friday or Saturday night when the hot mint tea flows, the belly dancers shake their thang and the hookah comes out of retirement.  My 3 year old was enthralled by the belly dancer.  Food is a set meal - with just about the best Bastilla (rabbit or chicken) around for miles.  Lamb was tender and flavorful.  Not a holy grail - but for Bucks County - where else ya gonna go for the "real deal" Moroccan cuisine?  Plus - they are family owned and have been around for gotta be well over 20 years.

OMG!!! It's awful.  Maybe I just hit 'em on a bad day/time -as it was on a weekend at about 4 PM - kinda between the lunch & dinner crowds.  Place was empty - so service was quick.  I ordered 1 item - a steak taco.  Then I noticed the fruit flies.  Swarms of 'em - near the "hot sauce" bar area.  Ugh.  Appetite destroyed.  I paid for my taco and took it to go - and ate it next door at the Dunkin' Donuts while my 4 year old stared at the donuts and decided which one she wanted.  Taco?  Inedible - and the vision of those flies was dancing thru my head.  Chucked the taco.  Don't think I'll be back.

Oy, vey!  It's Finneys.  How many underaged drinks did I get here? (Way, way back in the day?)  How many of my high shcool friends got completely and utterly $h@!-faced here?  How many busts occured here?  How many joints were snuck in the bathroom (or out back?)  How many ancient buzzed or dunken memories have been through these hallowed doors?  This place was one of the ONLY liquor-licensed bars in D-town for YEARS (before D-town became yuppieville and a certified tourist destination - BWAH-HA-HA).  When I was growing up here we had Finney's and the Farm House - and the Amber Inn (which was called something else - I can't remember) and a few other seedy bars.  Finney's is, indeed, as Erin R. writes a "frat party" atmosphere - and also your basic townie bar.  But it kept us good and liquored up all thru Jr. High and High School and for that I am grateful.  (Mom, are you reading this???)
We come here for tax-free Home Despot. Lighting supplies, household repairs, tools, etc. We had our interior paint mixed here, as well.  We'll be back.  It's a neccessary evil.

I have a love/hate relationship with DB (David's Bridal.). While I elected in the end NOT to get my bridal gown through them, my bridesmaids both got decent (cheap - but hell, they'll NEVER wear them again - let's face it) bridesmaids dresses there.  The customer service can run the gamut from "fend for yourself, bitch" to "your humble servant".  It depends on who you get and WHAT DAY AND TIME (i.e. do not TRY to get good service on a weekend in "bridal/prom" season).  Meanwhile - you can buy color swatches here for $1 a piece and go have a dress made in whatever color your bride has forced upon you.  I had my girls wear a cobalt/royal blue shade called "Royal Velvet".  They were allowed to pick any dress they wanted as long as it met 2 criteria:  1.  Had to be floor length 2.  Had to be Royal VElvet.  Surprisingly enough both gals selected strapless styles - and they are NOT small women.  They both needed fitting and the alterations were done correectly the first time.  A-men.  Thank god the weddig planning is over.  P.S.  Do NOT give them your email address, like I did, or your will be on Every frikkin' bridal/newlywed email spam list around for months and months.  My wedding was in June 2008 and I still get emails from DB related businesses.
A nice place to see a flick.  Fairly clean and quiet. No problems here.

I had a lovely solo dining experience at El Rey on a scorching hot Wednesday Night.  My servers Justin and Isaiah were both terrific and very knowledgeable about food and the menu items.  Since I dined alone I had only one item from the menu (and I can't wait to return to try more).  I had the short rib torta and it was BIG (Huge, and messy - definitely NOT a date night food.), but more importantly it was Excellente!  The braised beef shortrib was tender, yet charred (they do this at the end for presentation) and tasted so flavorful and succulent with just the right amout of fat to taste great but not too fatty.  The sauce - made of guajillo (sp??) peppers and tomato, really tasted like tomato sauce to me - but what do I know?  The best part?  A FRESH - I mean uber-fresh - baked roll - almost like a mexican "fat" baquette with a crunchy crust and a white, airy inside.  (Yes, I know trop carbs, but who cares when the Bread is shipped in from Parc!!!)  They even re-did the back bar as a swanky faux speak-easy.  Yes, it's pricey - but I bet if you order the right things you can have a 4 star night easily at El Rey.  Oh - and even though the place is blaringly-loud - it's still less noisy than Distrito - but I gotta say - Distrito's food still ROCKS my world.  I shall return.  Next time with friends!

Came here for a license renewal (photo required - so could not do online) and luckily I picked a good time as it was not too crowded and I only had to wait for a few minutes.    No issues - which is great to report.  Way better than the DMV in Center City or worse - NYC where I used to live.

My family & I have been eating at Chambers for years (a big shout out to Matt and the gals!), but it is rare that we venture over to "the other side" as we are not big drinkers.  We did, however dine on the other side when we went for Mother's Day Brunch at Chambers.  The enter place (both sides) were packed and the food was terrific.  TOS offers a fully stocked bar and a lively scene - especially on Friday or Saturday nights.  We sure do love Chambers, and Matt & the gang are the BEST!

Finally we a got a chance to eat inside the restaurant and the food is every bit as terrific inside as it was on those balmy summer nights.  We started with the super-fresh (just made) $8 guacamole and chips.  (Plus their 4 house made salsas.  Our 10 year old loves the salsa Roja and I like the Chipotle one.  El kiddo had the surf & turf fajitas which she loved and I had a special - small steak and chicken enchilada.  Husband had pork ribs al pastor (delish!).  Kudos to Greg (who was not there that night) Nina and Sidney (Sydney?) for terrific friendly service - even with problem with their POS.  We love you!

Still the best bang for the buck THAI food in the entire city. Salmon Curry Tom Kha that ROCKS.  Love it!!! And still lovin' it years later and after trying lots of Thai places in Philly. (And elsewhere)

I like Jos. A. Bank when they are having sales (which is nearly always). Ran in here quickly to buy my man some duds.  Excellent service.  Makes for good gifts.  Update:  I bought a bunch of stuff here in February 2015 for a Valentine's gift for my husband.  I needed to return 2 items and they accepted them back (unopened with receipt) with no issues.  Easy Peasy!  GREAT SERVICE.

Oh wow!!!! Went here for a private event 4 course lunch yesterday and it was phenomenal.  The pastry chef did a baking demonstration for our group and the owner is a class act!  We started with the incredible humus on fresh baked bread. 4 types of delectable veggie salads: Carrots, beets & walnuts, red peppers & tabbouleh.  All were yummy.  Next the haloumi (fried) cheese with fig compote arrived along with crispy fried cauliflower & an heirloom tomato & sable salad.  For the entree we had either grilled eggplant (infused with pomegranite) or salmon.  Both were super tasty.  The desserts included a home-made cashew baklava with white chocolate pannagotta and fresh peaches.  Also a labneh semi-freddo (I did not care for it's tang) garnished with cucumbers and fresh diced summer melons.  The garnish tasted better than the dessert (to me).  FABulous service and a great, great meal.  G-d, I love it here.

The next best thing to a trip to Cape Cod - I tried the Taste of Maine which is a 1/2 roll each of shrimp, lobster and crab for $20 - including a drink (I got a pellegrino) and a bag of Cape Cod chips (I got BBQ and saved them for later).  Good sized rolls and the crab one was really excellent. I also loved the lobster one. Not too much mayo and the roll was toasted and lightly buttered (a classic split-top) just as it should be.  Can't wait to go back. (I went at 11:40 right before the line started to form.  Smart move!

Affectionately known as Charbucks or Fourbucks - we have adopted the slogan of:  "Friends don't let friends drink starbucks."  Save money by brewing at home with Peregrine Coffee (the BEST) or go to La Colombe or Caffeination.

Just got all my knives done (the ones that needed it) by Neil at the Media Farmer's Market.  He  is there once per month and worth every penny.  He does Scissors and Lawnmower blades, too.  LOVE HIM and we value his work!

This restaurant rivals any fine dining place you'd expect on NYC's Upper East side.  Small space, crammed with tables, deafeningly loud and pricey.  The food, however is very well prepared and they use top-quality ingredients.  The signature app. - thinly sliced smoked salmon wrapped around a panko-crusted poached egg topped with a razor-thin crispy potato "chip", microgreens in a tangy vanaigrette and a bitt of maldon salt.  WOW.  (And for $14 it better be!).  DH had the pork belly with came with a delicious jus and a golden raisin puree (which on paper grosses me out - but actually tasted ok.) and topped with a quarter-sized "slice" of mustard gelee (eew. sorry - gelee is also not a big hit for me.)  DH also had the trout entree which was perfection on a plate - sided with creamy pureed cauliflower.  I opted for foie gras app in lieu of an entree - which made me feel like I needed gall bladder surgery.  Wow - so fattening - I literally only ate half. (It was a scoop of foie with a "liquid center" of cherries.)  The brioche toast to spread it on was heavenly as well.  After all that fat we just couldn't handle dessert - but the table behind us had fresh begneits which looked amazing.  We brought our own wine and the bill was still nearly $100 (and I had 2 apps - no entree).  Wow that's kinda steep for a BYO.  Service was top-notch - especially Jackie our server who catered to our every whim.  A few things make it so I just can't give them 5 stars - namely the price for what you get.  They have Manhattan prices in Coshohocken. Imagine! Meanwhile the place was packed, and the decor and service are great - if you can handle the crowded digs and the noise.  I would definitely go back, but I would not RUSH back.   It is worth ONE trip out from Center City to see if you like it. After that - judge for yourself.  Oh - and they cater - but man am I scared to imagine that bill.

OK, I'm gonna be nice and give them 2 stars - as usually McDonald's by it's very nature is a one star chain for me.   I don't do fast food.  I just don't - but if you need a clean(ish) restroom - and the new McCafe coffee - the New Britain (old school) mcD's has been around for-eh-ver.  I think it may be about the same vintage as the Doylestown location.  The people working here are pleasant, though and that is worth alot.  Mostly CB West folks, some young adults - some not-so-young (during the day shift).  I won't be in often, but hey - it's there.
Just got back from a lovely Sunday 2 hour session of blueberry and peach picking.  From March - December there is something to do that's great at Linvilla.

Just stopped in for a quick bowl of vermicelli with spring rolls and sliced beef. On a cold night - this place (still in dire need of a makeover) serves a great, warming meal for under $10.  Love it here!

I am dithering back & forth between 3 & 4 (yes, really - 4 stars) stars.  I am giving it 3 stars because it's mall susho - but I gotta say for mall sushi - it is pretty damned good.  I had an American Dream roll, which is basically a shrimp tempura roll, draped in avocado & fresh salmon.  The salmon was fresh and tasty, and the roll was garnished with an abundance of masago and 2 sauces, unagi (eel) sauce and spicy mayo.  In future I will ask for the sauces on the side - or just for less sauce - it was a little too gloppy for my taste.  I wish I had noticed they have brown rice - or I woulda had that for sure.  I would definitely choose Yanagi over other food court options.

Truly Delightful prepared and Packaged foods. Not so much delightfulness?  The place could use a good cleaning and the parking situation is a bit crazy.  (I wound up at the McDonald's nearby - no spots in the back nor the front.)  wish they had fresh produce too.  Stocked up on some of the BEST stuffed grape-leaves i have EVER had.  plus eggplant salad (a little oily) and delicious meat pies and bakalava.  Don't miss the Lahmahjoon!!!!  LOVE THIS and wishing them many more years of success.
