Dining Under the Stars (Wednesday night in the summer) can be a big ole mess - super crowded, long waits for a table, long waits to order, long waits to get food.  Surprisingly - this was NOT the case and we. lucked. out.  Greg and his amazing team at Dos Gringos honored our 6:45 PM reservation (all 3 people in our party were present) and sat us right when we arrived at 6:30 PM (WOW!).  The wait staff was uber-busy so we waiting a while - but not very long for menus, chops/salsa (so good) and that fabulous $10 guac.  Yup.  Guacamole is $10 here.  But we love it.  Vegetable enchiladas and surf & turf fajitas are family faves.  We keep coming back (even after Hildago opened - which we also enjoy). See you next time!

I have been taking my (now) almost 11 year old pug hear for about 2-3 years (after I moved back from NYC).  Even though we live in Philly now and commute up to DAMC to take him - it is worth it.  We have seen Drs. Benson (GREAT) and Gray (OK - not as nice as Benson, but still a good vet.)    Saturday appointments are limited and the placed gets mobbed - so be timely and call in advance to help us all out.  The administation of the practice is OK - but not superb (I got spoiled by my FABulous - and fabulously expensive - vet in NYC).  They are very willing to ship meds and supllies to me in Philly which is a huge help.  All is all, I recommend them - but I did get spoiled while in NYC - where my precious puggy was treated for the first 8 years of his life.

Yep.  It sure does live up to the hype.  Decor:  classy - nice flooring and cool light fixtures Service:  GREAT!  Hostess was pretty and not too icy, Chef was welcoming, servers wore cute Hebrew-emblazonned Coca Cola Tees.  Food:  Sublime!  The 4 types of hummus (we tried 2 - the one with a glob of Chick peas in the center and the Buttery one served warm which was just heavenly)  DOn't miss the salad sampler - so yummy.  8 types of cold veggie salads.  The Sabra chicken and the lamb skewers were tender and terrific.  Perfectly prepared.  The jeweled rice that accompanied the lamb was a treat.  The "old school" and "new school" phyllo desserts were terrific, too.  We did spend a bundle through - $290 (incl. tip) for 4 adults and a 3 year old who just picked off our plates.

As with many Starr joints, - it is style over substance to (a-hem) justify a higher price.  Continental is a solid choice for brunch - and OK for lunch or dinner.  We enjoyed the super fresh Vietnamese-type "Summer Roll" - but at $8.50 it should not be filled with surimi (imitation crab).  It was also very light and I could have eaten 2 of them myself.    For $9.50 the udon and wonton soup came with 3 wontons and a few slivers of scallion.  NOT worth the high price, but tasty.  Edamame was $6.50.  OUCH!!!!!    Server, Katie, was gorgeous and attentive.  Hot (and likely gay) barkeep had beautiful tattoos on Saturn on his arm.  A fun place - but bring MONEY.
Another excellent night at Dos Gringos with 5 star servce from Nina, Billie, Jess & of course, Greg.    Our 9 year old devoured the "surf & turf" fajita platter.

My (now) husband and his guys (and the fathers) all got stuck getting there tuxedo rentals at MW.  I mean, what choices do you have (read:  Venteresca's in Doylestown kicks MW's a$$, but anyhow) if you have any guys who live outside of your local area, do them all a favor a get MW tuxes.  The groom's Tux is "free" if the wedding party is 4 or more.  (They all have to pay for and return their tuxes before the groom gets credited for his.)  Customer service really varies - and is completely  sales associate dependant.  et a good associate, you'll have a better experience.  They STILL managed to f**k up part our order on wedding day.  One guy had no shirt and one guy's shirt was the wrong size.  The store manager saved the day (literally) by shlepping the correct shirts to the Inn where we got married.  Thank God that's over!  P.S.  Don't give them your email address, unless you want to be on every frikking mailing list wedding-related or not, known to man.

We came here with a party of 5 for a late lunch and on a tight time-frame. Unfortunately, we were seated in a booth (the place was not busy so we should have asked for a table - and will do so if we ever return).  That booth was so uncomfortable especially for our 8 year old. "Smushy", she said.  In any case, our server Bryan (Brian?) was very accomodating. The food was just OK - lunch menu items - we mostly all had sandwiches (burger, filet on foccacia and Prime rib pieces with onions on a kaiser roll).  Kiddo had (again) the "Mac-a-roo" but this time did not like the cheese sauce (too rich and thick this time.)  Oh, well.  I was never a big fan of Outback - but we had such a great experience the last time we came, we thought we'd give it another go.  Tips:  Come during NON peak hours, Sit at a TABLE not a booth - especially for parties of 5 or 6.

Such a cute store - and a great place to pamper your pooch.  I have an 11 year old male pug and he is just a love.  I get his "treaties" here.  (Glucosamine/Chondroitin to help with his arthritis.  Expensive - but nice, top-quality merchandise.  Woof!  You have my bark of approval!

I had great fun browsing amongst the All-Clad, raclette Machine, Fondue Sets, Lemon Misters and Ice Cube Molds at Kitchen Kapers.   When buyng kitchen gear I prefer multi-taskers to items used for only one limited purpose - but Kitchen Kapers has items I never knew I needed!  Great for gifts and barware, too.  Friendly and knowledageble staff.  Fun to browse.  The $400 Breville toaster oven was a hoot.  I will stick with my $79 job from tar-jay.

Bonner's rennovated the back dining room and our group was treated like royalty for a private event.  Food was still pretty "meh" - but Dan (the man) is a great and generous host and Liz  runs the show, pretty much.  Bonner's is a standard, solid Irish pub with good drinks and lots of good times. It's a PECO hangout for many, for sure!

We went here for brunch and it was surprisingly AWESOME. Having eaten lunch several time s and having drinks at the Continental Midtown over the years - I was iffy about coming here - but we needed FOOD and it called to us.  I had an eggs Florentine (egges Benedict with spinach instead of meat.) and my husband got the Breakfast quesadilla.  Both were good and brunch was served with a melon mint sorbetto as a palate cleanser.  Decor is Starr-ized and funky (although someone told me that Starr is not involved with the Continental on Market - only the Continental midtown - not sure if this is true.)  Olive themed light fixtures and olive drab restrooms with gorgeous stainless steel light fixtures on the mirror.  Servers were young, good-looking and surprisingly attentive.  The only disappointment wis the potatoe casserole.  It was just their regular deep-fried potato slices with cheese, peepers & onions melted over the top.  It really shoulda said "cheese fries".  Prices weren't too bad.  Brunch for 2 - no alcohol was $25! (But I missed having a Champagne-o-rama - my Continental Fave.)  Drink menu is THE SAME as the Cont. midtown.  We may actually come back here!

Not a fan.  Sorry.  With Qdoba nearby and really GOOD places like Xochitl and Tequila's, I guess I am forever spoiled.  Even my former experience with San Francisco tacquerias puts Hot Tamales to shame.  I had a burrito with spinach, mushrooms and supposedly turkey - but it seemed almost exactly the same as the ground beef my friend ordered.  Weird.  And bland.  And just not that tasty.  It's not that the food is dangerous or anything - it's just not that good. It is cheap, however.  And crowded at lunch time (I thnk they are closed at dinner time.)  Whatever.  Not really worth the energy.

The juice bar gets 5 stars - the procude 4.  Sook Hee, the owner is a doll and offers a myriad of fresh fruit, veggies and gourmet snack items.  The juice bar which has FRESH wheatgrass juice is a godsend for me.  This is the real deal - and I will support them.  We needs a REAL JUICE BAR (Basic 4 in RTM is ok, but this is even better.)

An unbelievably excellent meal and service at Dos Gringos Mexican Kitchen. Those short-ribs were meltingly tender, and the veggie enchiladas and tostones al pastor are Da Bomb! Shout outs to Danielle and your new expediter/busser. Terrific. A +! Wonderful birthday celebration.  Greg treats us like old friends.  Much love.

I have stopped in at Burlap & Bean twice now - once in the afternoon for an iced coffee which was very good and once in the morning for an iced latte which was so strong and bitter I could only drink about half of it and threw the other half out.  The place is very nice, clean and spacious and I will definitely come back to hear some music in the evenings, but I am gun-shy of thei espresso drinks now, which is a shame, as I love a good latte/iced latte etc.  Could be a 4 star place but that latte really tasted bad.  Service was friendly.

Went here for a desperation dinner - and needed something the 7 year old would like.  (She suggested it).   The good:  The black & white milkshake ($4.05) was freshly made and big enough for the 3 of us to each have a good bit of. - really big enough for 2 to share.  The chicken sandwiches were fried - but freshly fried.  Very pleasant service - an older lady took the orders, a younger gal cooked and served and a teen guy spun milkshakes and got us fountain drinks.  The bad:  Waffle fries are just OK.  Onion rings are tasteless and above a 1/2 step about BK quality.  I wanted the real deal - and this ain't it.  The ugly:  NASTY horrid bathroom.  Used - again - out of a 7 year old's desperation.  We'll be back - in the spring/summer when the weather is nicer.  A junk food paradise.  There is NOTHING remotely healthy on the menu.  Not even an iceberg side salad.

It's OK.  Just OK.  I grabbed a quick low-fat banana berry muffin ($2.00 including tax) and the lady heated it up in the microwave for me.  With so many other goodies in RTM - this might be OK if you need BREAD - but for sammies or treats I'd go elsewhere (Like Flying Monkey for treats or Olympia Gyro).  But I guess that's not an apples to apples comparisson.  It may be intangible, but I was never thrilled with le Bus.  Very 1989.

This is a GREAT place to buy beef.  (For chicken I like Harry Ochs - also on the Market).  The steaks are gorgeous - and you certainly pay for that care & expertise.  The butcher will custom cut and package the meat for you (which is great for our small family.)  I love to shop at RTM and Giunta's is a welcome addition (or mainstay -  should say!).  Nice selection of ground beef, pork & veal, too.  Lovely looking veal chops - but alas, I could not afford them that day.

Just OK.  Not great.  The nail services are OK.  A few of the many floors could use a makeover.  Looks a little dated.  I bet it's been around a LONG time.  Nice selection of retail and jewelry/accessories.  CUTE stuff.  Nice owners.

It's here - and that's a BIG plus.  I just bought a 1/2 gallon of tropicana OJ there - i was in a pinch and HAD to have it - and it was $4.49.  OUCH!  I also got a 12 oz. bottle of V-8 for $1.99 - Double OUCH!  Korean-run and nice staff, but wow - so pricey.  They also have a hot food bar that looks so unappetizing to me.  Glad they are here - wish they were cleaner and cheaper.

Years ago I would have given Herb's 5 stars.  I remember shopping in their original location on the corner of Main & Wets Streets.  Now they are just a few doors down Main where the old Fagin & Fagin grocery store (now THAT's a blast from the past) used to be.  Herb's is a D-town instituion and a great go-to spot for crafters who don't feel like driving out to AC Moore or Michaels.  They have all sorts of crating supplies, balsa wood, glue, floral arranging supllies, DIY kits - you name it.  When I was 8-11 this place was like wonderland.  Glad they're still around.

Let me make it clear that I am reviweing the restaurant in the BAR AREA at the Sofitel - but it is the same menu and same kitchen as Chez Colette.  Service here has always been great for us - we come for lunch and I usually get the Salmon over butternut squash risotto - which is a rich, delicious meal.  My friend usually will get a burger that is served with an enormous cone of thinly cut greasy fries.  (Yes - they are a little BKish.)  But the food was not crap when we went.  It was really good - and I had freshly squeezed OJ.  Eat in the bar - for the comfy couches and big tables and people watching.  The main restaurant (which I have never sat in) is usually dead empty.

Delicious coffee drinks and a plethora of syrups (Butterscotch latte anyone?) if you are into diabetes in a cup.  Funky-eclectic male baristas.    Decent prices and a fun-in-the-sunny window seating area.  Love.

My mother in law loves this place and has given Douglas Jewelers a ton of business over the past few years.  She bought me a 10 K white gold and Garnet pendant - and while it is lovely - i KNOW it was overpriced.  She also convinced my husband to buy me a piece of Blue Topaz Jewelry here that was $800 and worth about 3.  I made him return it.  They have lovely items - but for quality vs. value I prefer to shop at Caroll's jewelers.  The "deals" at douglas are not deals at all.

Kingyo has summer appetizer specials for $3.00  Yes - that's right $3.00 - for sizling AgeTofu with mushrooms (enoki & shitake)  or 4 crispy Ebi (Shrimp) shumai.  Kingyo is rapidly becoming my go-to spot for a sushi fix when I am in that area.  Ben and Yama are very nice to me and to my 5 year old - who loves the steamed shumai.  Try the Tuna Citrus salad - served in a whole orange - or the spicy tuna tartar.  I also like the tuna tataki over a bed of fresh greens - very diet-friendly.  I have had all kinds of maki and te-maki here - very fresh - and the best of all?  Home-made tamago (none of that frozen garbage.).  Yes it costs a bit more than Vic's or Jay's - but the preparations are more classic and pure.  I like that from time to time.  Kingyo is much friendlier to me than Genji ever was.  Hooray! Dinner for 2 last night with one cocktail ($9) was $70 including tax 'n tip.

Greg and his staff treat our party of 3 like royalty during our "Dining Under The Stars"  (aka chaos out in the heat).  Possibly "Duning out in the Mist" due to the light rain and heavy cloud cover.  Still, the place was hoppin' and the food was poppin'.  Our 9 year old get a chicken quesadilla and rice & beans which she loved.  She also plowed through the guacamole abd the mild red salsa.  I love the specia that night - Crab (real lump crabmeat) and goat cheese enchiladas.  The pale green avo-jalapeno crema was terrific over top of it.  Rich and decadent.  So close to 5 stars - why not?  Hubby did not care for the braised beef enchiladas - he said the shortribs last time were better.  I did not try his dish but it looked flippin' fantasstic to me.  Love this place - and love to Greg and his hard working staff (front and back)!

Now they have all 4 ramen options in a vegetarian broth with great veggies! Also for Summer 2013 there is a great cold ramen salad ($11.00). HOORAY FOR VEG-Friendly options.  I love it here - but it is sooooo salty - but today the lady said if I tell her they can make them less salty.  This time I got the Vegetarian Miso (regular size is plenty big for me - but they also have a large size) and a side of tender Toriniku Pork (I like it better than the Cha su).  I skip the egg and extra noodles (no need for me - but if you like poached eggs they offer it as an add-on.)  So happy they are here! This is one place where I like takeout better than eat in - as they pack the broth and noodles/goodies separately and I love that!!! And they accept LevelUp.

We had an absolutely 5 star experience today - because we got there at 8:55 AM (it opens at 9 AM) and were literally the first people in line.  My 6 year old brought her sketch pad and we sat (and sat) and she sketched the bell from front and back while the throngs walked around us.  The security guards were terrific with us - and we even took a picture with one.    GREAT fun today!  Better than usual.
A great place for birdwatching, and of course, wildflower tours for adults and kids.  This is a great treasure in Bucks County.  GORGEOUS.  Must go here.

We loved coming to (there are more than one) all the Lamberti's over the years.  My best friend (of MANY years) and her late father loved it here so much that she had her (small, informal, hippy-filled) wedding here.  The chicken marsala and salmon were excellent, and the family style penne marinara and spinach made it a great evening.  The roasted peppers and mozzarella are sooooo good here.  It is a very casual place - not what I would pick for a wedding - but maybe for a rehearsal dinner or shower.

Convenient location on the corner of Rittenhouse Square with 3 ATMs.  I just wish that ALL of the TD ATMs could do ALL of the functions.  (Like deposiuts, purchase stamps).  They are often out of stamps.  Before, when TD was Commerce you could do every function from every ATM.  This new system is NOT GOOD.

Just got back from the CHAOS that is Linvilla during halloween season. We enjoyed a fabulous hayride and bonfire - complete with long sticks and marshmallows for toasting and small cups of home-pressed Linvilla apple cider.  I also bought (naughty me) a half-dozen apple cider donuts which were still warm and disappeared quickly.  YUM!  It would be 5 stas but for the commercialism that is rampant and grows larger every year (they have 2 enormous parking areas and they are both always packed.)  Want to really enjoy Linvilla - come when it's not Hallowwen and get the same great treats, seasonal rpdocue and less people/kids/lines/chaos.

Great products. Fair prices. Weird hit or miss service at this location.  I disapgree with eric f. and I BET he gets treated well because he's a guy.  Anyhow - I stock up on my lip balm #1 and get the heck out.

Still only 3 stars.  Stopped in alone and the bar was hopping - but the dining room was deserted.  Server was pleasant but often disappeared just when I needed her.  Delicous bread (baguette) and butter garnished with garlic chive blossoms.  Cute Amuse.    Best thing?  Salad of rainbow chard and too-salty duck confit with a poached egg.  Leat favorite?  Mushroom vol-au-vent.  Too earthy for me.  $38.50 for dinner for just me - NO BEVERAGE NO DESSERT.  Ouch.

Lydia R. sums it up.  The manicurist is the best part - (Carol??) she is a gem and a great technician - but my polish chipped 6 hours later. (Which seems odd seeing that she used CND products.  That said - I returned a few weeks later to see Carol for a mini facial (30 minutes, Dermalogica Products).  The hairdresser, Elle, did just an OK job on my blowout. She did not listen to what I wanted.  Manager/Receptionist Jamie was very pleasant and friendly.  One suggestion:  Please have a water cooler or water available.  I was told I could fill up my own water bottle in the bathroom.  Not too classy for an otherwise classy salon.  Decor is beautiful but B2 has some kinks to work out. 4 star manicure, 4 star facial, 2 star blowout.

Decor is very nice and food is passable. I had a Salmon Lover lunch special ($15) and it came with an iceberg salad and good miso soup.  Salmon was fresh but rice for the maki was a little gummy. I also tried the Lotus In Roll - and that was much better - with fresh yellowtail - but I forgot to ask for "sauce on the side" and it was smothered in wasabi mayo.  (Too much for my tastes - next time I gotta remember "sauce on the side")  Not Nobu - but very good considering the area.  I will be back for sure. Chinese dishes and Chicken Teriyaki lunch special looked good - might try a Faux-Thai dish (Pad Thai) next time.    Note:  I also tried the Sesame Shrimp - and it was very good (albeit deep-fried).

I finally took the plunge and accompanied a close friend of mine to BP last night.  She had been there oodles of times - but it was my first.  I had the most amazing Salade Lyonnaise and home-made cavatelli. Her fish (Brnazino) had bones in it which accounts for knocking a star off.  Service was terrific - attentive yet unassuming.  Decor is fab. A great selection of wines - although we did not partake.  We really enjoyed our evening capped off by a delectable plate of assorted cookies (that pattissiere knows what they are doing!) and fresh brewed Jasmine Green tea that was fragrant and wonderful.  I can't wait to go back.

Still don't accept credit cards - but they do have take out - that is well packed (broth and goodies in separate bowls). I also love the little piece of nori that comes when you get Shoyu.  You can also add bean sprouts and/or bok choy for a small upcharge.  I tried the Shio this time - and liked it better than the Shoyu.  Both are salt-laden, though. And I also enjoy the Miso - but that may be from the drizzle of black garlic "nom nom" sauce on top.  Next time will try the (limited time offer) Pork Cheeks or the Soft-Shell crab buns!  (pricey stuff - but I bet it's great.)  The bad part?  With all the extra goodies (no need for extra noodles in my opinion, unless you are a big eater and famished) I usually spend about $10 on ramen.  YIKES.

My (then) 10 year old took 8 classes (2 packages of 4 classes each) before she decided that Archery was not "her thing" but in the mean time, GG and her daughter were great instructors and she got to be pretty good and indoor and outdoor target shooting.  My kid even joins JOAD for a bit.  Grounds are beautiful.  I liked our experience here.

Had a much better experience - this time for dinner - and the grilled beef summer rolls ($6.50) were so tasty and fresh.  Pho was average - but worked.  Broken rice platters are a good value. Friendly service and a fun experience.

Our membership has paid for itself this year (We 've been members for many years but, thankfully, we don;t need to call often.)  We got a severe flat tire (literally, we were "screwed" as a metal screw pretty much popped the driver's side rear tire and tube) and called AAA at 1:10 PM.  They guarantee service within an hour and Ricardo Blanco from New Castle, DE arrived in 36 minutes.  G-d bless him.  He changed our tire (using our existing spare) and inflated the spare properly.  We are so grateful.  Everyone should join AAA - for real!

When they said "small plates" they weren't kidding. Lilliputian is the word my friend used to describe our $2.00 cups of tea and $5 cappuccino.  Deleicious food - but so small. Sushi rolls are "normal" size - and the $5 spicy tuna roll at happy hour (Usually $9) is a good deal - but you have to sit at the bar or in the bar area.  Mike from Detroit was our cheerful server/bartender and he was terrific.  I enjoyed the Louella roll (Lots of yellowtail) most of all - but the tuna nachos - had 5 (five) nachos on the plate.  Really?  For $10 there wer five pieces?  That's$2 per chip.  Seriously???  I would never bring my husband here or any "big eater". No way.  This is a menu comprised of apps and you can very easily leave here feeling hungry with a much lighter wallet.

3.5 stars max for average food. I was very disappointed in that I had been to Avero a while back for a private event and the food for that was terrific.  Came here last night for Happy Hour - which was great for the $4 drink specials (vodka drinks or beer or a few house wines) and 1/2 price pizzas/flatbreads.  I ordered a chicken picatta entree and it was just LOADED with capers - even after I had asked for "light on the capers".  I can not imagine what the "normal" amount of capers would have been?  Anyhow it made the dish exceedingly salty/vinegary.  The drinks were fine and service was fine, too (not crowded at 4:45 PM on a Wednesday).  Not sure I'll be rushing back here.

I am NOT a fan of chains - and truly not a fan of Outback (in fact, I stay away from most of the steaks there), but today our party of 5 - including my parents who LOVE Outback had a great Sunday lunch.  Part of what made it so great was that the place was EMPTY at 12 noon on a Sunday. Thus, we had attentive service and no waiting to be seated.  Bliss.  I enjoyed a 1/2 rack (4) of ribs and my 7 year old ate 2 of them.  Plus a kids meal of "mac-a-roo" - and steamed broccoli.  The kid ate like a champ.  Do I love the food here?  Not really.  Is it 5 stars?  No way. But we got a decent 4 star meal out of a 3 star place. Good for kids (mine at least.)  Go at an off-peak time for this formula-cooking meat fest.  P.S.  - for $5 they serve up an enormous and very good key lime pie on a graham cracker crust.

Came back one more time - and this time there was a special exhibit on Sugar and Candy Making (how ships brough the sugar to America) by the Berley Brothers (Shane Confectionery/Franklin Fountain).  My kid - who by then was 8 -now she's 9 - loved it and she really likes this museum. Don't miss the ship-building shop where they will cheerfully answer your questions and the master craftsmen will stop their work to talk to you.  What great (and talented) guys!  We also thoroughly hit up the gift shop on this trip and there are lots of over-priced toys and knick knacks that appeal to kids so beware if you have children - they will want one of everything.\  A fun museum - and if they keep roating the exhibits we'll be back for a 3rd go.  P.S.  The tattooing exhibit is lots of fun as well.
Here again but this time had EXCELLENT service from an u-named male employee who showed us where to get everything we needed.  No problems this visit.

Stopped in for a free (coupon) beverage at an odd hour (5:15 PM) and got in and out relatively quickly, however it took over 45 seconds (seems like longer than it is) to be acknowledged by the single overworked staffer.  I chose an iced macchiatto. (I bet I spelled that wrong.)  No issues - and for free?  That was fine. Oh - and they have a drive thru here.

A great and majestic venue for hosting a corporate event or large party - easily accomodates 300 for cocktails/stations.  You must use their caterers, though - decent food and excellent, friendly servers.  Coat room available. Spacious. Ammenities.  Consider this for your next event!
closed!!!!!

Otto's dumpy brauhaus has been around for years & years & years - as long as I can remember.  I went twice over the years and both were pretty bad - but I am not a "wurst" gal.  You can drink yourself silly with the NUMEROUS beers on tap and in bottles.  (Alas, I am not a beer gal either) You can watch the game, ogle the dusty old busts of deer on the walls or count the multi-colored beer steins hanging on the walls.  It's just not that great.  The food is mediocre at best and some of the servers (who've worked there for eons) just really don't care any more.  If you LIKE German food - then go, otherwise I'd skip it.

I attended a large (260 mostly women) function all day today at the Meadowland's Country Club.  While valet parking is (and was) available, we parked in the large lot and walked over.  The building outside is stone and beautiful as are the (golf coursey) grounds.  The facilities are very lovely although a bit dated looking.  For instance, I would not have my wedding here but a Bar/Bat Mitvah or corporate function would be fine.  It's just not "slick" enough (in my humble opinion) for a wedding.  The food and service were very good.  While continental breakfast and lunch were both provided, breakfast was not big deal  (Literally juices, coffe & danish - that was IT.)  Buffet style lunch service was tasty and nicely presented.  The eggs florentine (served for 260) was a bit cold, but tasted wonderful.  Homemade tune & egg salads were tasty and the green salad bar had numerous tasty toppings.  All fresh.  All great.  A giant fresh fruit display walong with delectable (and some still warm) homemade cookies and (not warm) brownies.  A nice place to host an affair.  Also - Membership is reduced from $1500 to $1000 due to the recession (a house membership does NOT include pool access, and you have to spend $125 a month on food from Dec - Mar).  Since we live in Center City I doubt we would ever join here - but I sure would consider having an event here - if they'd let a non member do that.

Olive Garden - ah yes - Faux-talian. Went here for a nice lunch (this is as good as an OG can get IMO) with 2 friends. One had the "tour of Italy", the other had the stuffed Chicken Marsala which looked entirely too cheesey for me to attempt eating.  I played it safe and ordered the shrimp scampi app over pasta instead of crositini.  The portion was HUGE and that was more than enough.  Salty breadstcks and overly dressed iceberg salad came free (as it always does at OG.  Not a holy grail - but a "safe' choice when you are in the area.

Called for an inquiry - and plan to use them to re-key our new home in Media.  Woody was very helpful and informative.  A service call is $85 plus the cost of whatever you are having done.  They have 24 hour emergency service, too.

Odd service (from hostesses - not server - she was great) and excellent "fresh" food for a pricey but delicious lunch.  Crab Cake Wedge salad was terrific as was a simple side of roasted red beets with sliced almonds.  Sweet & Crunchy and so easy to scarf down.  A fizzy glass of sparkling raspberry lemonade was refreshing and light.  Love it here.  Wish I could afford to come more often.
Meh. Decent staff helping us or trying to sell us a new phone.  Not gonna buy here, I don't think.  A decent selection of high priced phones.

Try the Toriniku (pork cheek) special - or get a side order of it. If you are a pork fan this is BETTER than the pork belly.  Still fatty, yes, but very tender.  Super flavorful.  All the broth here is very salty to me, but still a tasty winter treat. Tip:  add Bok Choy and Bean Sprouts!
Very clean, well-run Starbucks.  Parking lot around back. No issues.
I can usually find some decent pants and socks at NY&Co.  Good prices and they usually send e coupons in th email.  The one in K of P is nicer, as i loathe the Gallery.

Not sure if this is the SAME produce cart neat Penn's dental School - but if it is - I love it.  Used to get fruits and veggies here all the time when I went to Penn.  Tip:  you MUST wash everything well.  They always have apples, bananas and organges, but very often they have more exotic fruits like mangoes and fresh berries - at GREAT prices.  Select carefully, weash thoroughly and ENJOY!

We had a very nice and extremely reasonable meal of wings on "Wing Wednesdays"  (60 cents per wing - and we ordered 16 of them).  The wings are better than the  pizza and come in 3 varieties - Traditional Bone-in, Bone-in Breaded and Boneless. (We got traditional with Honey BBQ sauce (a little too much sauce) and Blue Cheese (or ranch).  The wings are smaller and not as good as Hooters - but they were so cheap!  NO CELERY - that is very bad.  Meanwhile, our server Jackie was a doll and treated us well.  For $18.50 for dinner for two - including tax & tip it was a junk-food fest.  Stay away from the greasy Pizza Hut Pizza - but do consider "Wing Wednesday" - oh and BYOC - Bring your own celery.  PLEASE GET SOME CELERY STICKS!

I hope they'll make it but I fear they will not. Only one size smoothie and it is $7 - so i get my 10 year old and a friend to split it.  Wish they had a kids size for about $4 or $4.50.  Friendly service and great ideas and products but it is almost always empty and I wonder how they'll make it? I fear the end may be near.
A nice flower shop - right in New Hope.  They have done a few items for our family over the years, but we usually used Doylestown Florists - because they were closer.

I can't say enough good things about Lori & Victoria at North Bowl - also John and Erin and everyone who helped make my 6 year old's birthday party with 14 5 & 6 year olds a smashing success.  The food was good - plain pizzas from rustica, veggies 'n dip, the famous tots, chicken fingers.  The bowling was great!  And the single shot on Absolut Vanille hit the spot.  Got a party to plan?  I highly recommend you consider North Bowl.

Stopped in for a non-coffee beverage and wound up with a winner - the Watermelon (non-alc.) mojito (sans simple syrup and it's still very sweet).  4 stars for the great beverage - 2 stars for the icy reception from the (female) barrista.  Again - this place is just OK.
One of the only places in D-town to get a car washed.  Has changed names and owners a few times.  Not bad.  Not awesome either.  It's fine by me!

Took my 7 year old to Golosa as part of Dining with Friends - her school's program.  We are so glad Golosa participated.  The red velvet cake and hot 56% chocolate with "shaken cream" on top were divine.    DD loved the red velvet cake so much we got a slice to go for tomorrow. She also got a blood orange chocolate (truffle?) for $2.00.  We also tasted 4 different cookies ($4.00) and we liked the corn meal and cocoa sable the best.  An elegant, pricey, caloric, indulgence. Worth it!  Love it here.  Cash only.

Ok, my best friend calls this place Icky Vicky's - because if you are a big gal - this is NOT the place for you.  Victoria's secret is a place to buy "every day" underwear.  It is mall-quality, mass produced bras, panties, sleepwear, loungewear and now - really poor quality fragrances and cosmetics that bilk thousands of teens and young 20-somethings out of millions each year - and their mama's too!  If it sounds as though I am being harsh - well...  ...I Kinda am.  anyhow, I get my typical five for $25 plain cotton string bikinis there and whenever I get a "free panty" coupon in the mail I run right over.  I am definitely not a a Power Shopper at VS - I much prefer high end lovelies like La Perla or Agent Provacateur for the specialty goods.  But for an everyday comfy cotton undie?  VS is my go-to spot.  Just don't ask for help from the teen-aged, undereducated, underpaid staff (although they'll probably offer to help you).  Come here during off hours when there are no lines to check out.

Nope.  We're sticking with Da Shin.  This place is good for certain items - but on the whole very greasy.  And you can't dine in (card table, eew. Just, no!) so for delivery yes to Jing Fong, for dine in?  Da Shin.
Just OK.  Meh is the perfect word to describe the S&HF.  Been around a long time though so SOMEBODY must be going there.  Years & Years ago it was a meh pizzeria.  This location is cursed.

Now on my 2nd visit - I am on my way to becoming a lobstah mobstah.  This time I got 1 lobster roll and a side ($6) of Jonah Crab claws. The taste of summer in New England.  Can't wait to take my 8 year old here - she'll love it.  She's a lobster roll fan big-time.  So awesome!!!!

Jeff is about as good as you can find in Philly (far better than Hahnemann! Kinder than HUP).  My father went here for an outpatient procedure and it was handled well. Administratively (as with most large hospitals) it's kind of a nightmare.  Allow ample time - your 8 AM (or 9 AM) appointment - when you show up at 7:30 AM may not start until past 10 AM!!!  Lots of hurry-up-and-wait.

I vacillate between 3 & 4 stars because there are, indeed, numerous kinks (mostly service related) that need ironing out.  I came to Amuse with a group of 13 women, and we sat at the large high-top communal table in the bar area.  Service was scattered from the get go - they only brought out 3 menus, we asked for more.  They did not give us water until we asked.  Many of us had no cutlery nor napkins.  Again, we asked.  Sasha - one of our servers, was lovely - but stretched too thin to accommodate all of us, who ordered (partially separate checks) bar items, bar menu items and dinner menu items.  Items and courses sometimes came right away and other orders were lost in the shuffle and never arrived.  Meanwhile, my partner (on the same check) and I shared the $3 Parisienne Gnocchi (Paris is not known for Gnocchi, by the way), the $5 Mac & Cheese (both from the BAR menu) and a $7 side of sauteed brussels sprouts.  All were delicious - but the gnocchi was SWIMMING in butter and I would not order it again.  The brussels sprouts were the high point for me.  Others at the table had the Quinoa/Ratatouille dinner entree - and the Quinoa was way, way undercooked.  It was crunchy.  Fortunately the ratatouille was excellent.  Decor is sleek & gorgeous (I mean, the place is brand new.) and the food is NOT "Mariott-era" hotel fare.  I am pleasantly surprised and plan to return - but I will allow ample time and expect erratic and weird service.

Even better than the original Shane's! The fabulous guys who run the Franklin Fountain have re-opened (and gussied up) Shane's.  It's a REAL  old-time confectionary shop - replete with barley sugar (toy) candies (made in molds), chocolate creations and "penny candy" (that starts at $4 for a generous small).  My daughter (age 7) proclaimed the large plump, multi-colored and distinctly multi-flavored gummy bears, "The best I've ever eaten in my entire life!".  We are so gleefully happy that Shan'es is back - and better than ever.  See you at Valentine's Day! And Easter!  And whenever I get a hankering for Necco Chcoclate Wafers...  Thank goodness for the new & improved Shane's!

We still go here - and my kid is now a teenager.  She got braces here (invisalign Teen), retainer afterward and gets cleanings twice a year (assuming no cavities.).  We love Ashley (hygiene) and Dr. Alex.  Linda and Maryellen (??) at the front desk are great, too.  However - we can't give them five stars because their hours are sooooo limited.  No Friday afternoons.  One Saturday per month.  No late evenings - maybe one day per week they might stay past 6.  For a working parent, it is not convenient.  But now that ortho is over, we can make it work for 2 cleanings per year.

Super happy with Dr. Alex (pediatric) and Linda (Pediatric office Manager). Also I go to RTD for adult dental cleanings downstairs.  Dr. Liberman (sp??) is great, too.  Our only complaint?  very limited (sometime none) Satruday or evening hours.  Kids need appointments after 3 PM and after 6 PM many days.  It is very hard to get my kid the coveted 5 PM cleaning and I book it months in advance.  (And then, life happens.)  Wish they had more weekend and evening hours.  (Maybe open at noon one day a week and work until 8 PM?) Yes, staff hates that - but patients love it!

Love it here. Great staff and everything you need for a party or cocktail hour at home. Frozen hors d'ouvres, Cheeses like Chevre, Cheddar and Stilton, Crackers, Fresh OJ, Pomegranate seeds to garnish.  WONDERFUL.

I had been taking Amtrak (way expensive) every 2 weeks up and back to NYC, but now that my dad told me about Bolt bus - ihave used it twice.  The first time was awesome - but the second time our 8:30 AM bus did not arrive until 9 AM -needless to say we arrived about 35 minutes late to NY.  Like others below - how the heck to they make money?  For me and 2 other to go up and back to NYC was under $60.00.  The tickets ranged from $7 to $13 one way.  I did not get the $1 fare yet.  Also - there is a 50 cent surcharge for each transaction - so kep that in mind when you book.  I am kinda hoping this stays a secret because the busses are getting more & more crowded each time we go.  I also agree that the seats are very stiff and not comfy - but the busses are new and CLEAN (not like Chinatown hell, I mean, bus).  I did not use the wifi - but others did.  There are plenty of outlets (pugs) and also sometimes they'll play a movie.  MUCH cheaper than Amtrak.  During the winter (icy roads) I may be forced back to Amtrak.

DSW is usually a good place for us to find shoes (Women's Men's and shoes for my enormous 11 year old who wears a ladies size 10).    This location was no exeption - we scored big with 2 pairs of ladies size 10 heels - one open toed and one strappy sandal.  No issues here - and be sure to check out the clearance area all the way in the back corner - you never know!

This is my go-to Tar-jay and it is nicer than the one in Philly (on Colombus Blvd) for sure.  I can get vaious and sundry supplies, kids stuff and household goods.  The bad part?  I a always seem to drop no less than $80 and usually over $100 every time I come here - which is about every other weekend.  They have a (slow as molasses) starbucks on the lower level and restroom on both levels.
It's nice but not a holy grail.  They offer soups and a few sandwiches - I kinda wish they had more lunch options as I am not much for coffee drinks.  Very clean and brand new.

Burlap and Bean is a nice alternative to that "other" ubiquitous coffee chain.  Prices are a bit high and the coffee is a bit too bitter for me - but my kid just LOVES it here and eats the waffles.  Plus on Wednesday nights they do an "open mic" - and some crazy old folks were singing the last time we came in.  A homey-vibe - very chill and laid back.  Do not come here during the morning rush and expect to be in and out quickly.  People here take there time.  If you want quick - head to Charbucks or Dunkin (feh).  If you want to relax with a beverage and a snack - this is the spot.  Wish they stayed open later on Saturdays - they close at 3 PM.

OMG!!!! Do not let my secret out.  $2.00 Tom Ka Gai can not be beat (the most addictive Thai Coconut Soup - with chicke or shrimp - for $2.50 - or just vegetarian.)  I love the pad thai and curries, too.  CASH ONLY and you don't need much - for around $6.00 you can get a full delicious Thai meal.  (Bring some home tonight - the eat-in ambience leaves something to be desired.  YUM!!!!!!

As usual, I agree with Steven B. word for word. We were flying Southwest and in dire need of sustenance - and NOT fast food if at all possible.  My husband has a decidedly 2 star beef fajita salad - but my Enchiladas were actuallly good!  So pleased.  So surprised.  This will be where we drop our $40 on crappy airport food from now on.  Not so crappy.
Two words.  Tomato Pie.  All you need to know.

Being in the spa biz it PAINS me to pay retail - but for certain items that I must have NOW (and can't or won't wait for shipping online or ebay) I get at Douglas.  They even carry Bond fragrances.  (Love 'em.)  Also my 3 year old is a girly-girl and runs straight to the CHanel display to play with lipstick whenever we are there.  She adores Coco Pink.

This Maggiano's is not nearly as nice as the one in the Cherry Hill mall, but my parents and little girl and I go there sometimes when we want to sit down, however, the food is so much better at the Reading Terminal Market - which is just a block away.  Pasta dishes are a good value at lunch - but I ask them to go lightly on the sauce(s) - the garlic load is pretty intense.  An OK place for a "family meal" - no, it's not earth-shattering - and it can feel a bit "cafeteria-like" as it gets loud and the acoustics are pretty awful.   Also the ladies room could use a spruce-up.

I nicknamed this place Bun Cali - because i much prefer to get the bun here - tho the Pho is good, too.  My little daughter likes the Sugar Cane shrimp.  CHEAP, fast and a good Viet-fix when you need one. Decor is very basic and could use a clean-up.

I still go to Francis - since 2006 - and occasionally I stray. I have "cheated" on him at high-end places and lower-end places. I always come home to Francis - and twice I have had him rescue me from botched color jobs from other salons.  Francis is still the BEST old-school mid-priced  place for a cut and color. I love Frances as a person and respect him as a stylist. Over the years we have become good friends as well.  I have ALWAYS been pleased with my color here. Love it!
Dunkin Donuts at Philly airport - a safe choice which does not have over-inflated "gotcha" prices.  America may run on Dunkin, but I walk. Slowly.  I guess I got the decaf.

How do they do it?  And they've been doin' it for years?  The country place serves good down-home/bar type food and is sooooooo cheap.  Great drinks - and yes, sometimes the crowd is bikers and other times "church ;adies" so you never know what you're gonna get.  I miss it.  I live in Philly now and am too far away to go to COuntry Place - but I have fond memories.

I really, really needed a new manual can opener (we rarely open cans except maybe for our dog) and did not want an el-cheapo from Acme or Giant, so off I trekked to KK.  They had about 7 varieties from $13 - $25.  I settled on a $17.99 (about 19 with tax) model that is alot like my trusted (AS SEEN ON TV) "Safe-T-Can" that crimps the edges.    I was also tempted by a $60 nonstick pan, but I resisted.  Love to shop for kitchen gear. Love to cook.  Very nice store.

Mediocrity.  Came here when I was in a huge rush and Hip City Veg (next door) was bustling and Nom Nom ramen had a long line.  Spent about $6 on a latte and a stale bagel with veggie "light" cream cheese, tomato and cucumber.  Bitter overpriced latte.    BLAH.  Waste of calories.  Not goin' back.

We went to this "rustic sports bar" on a lovely summer day with family - not realizing that it is a chain.  The food was surprisingly good - Potstickers (though frozen, very tasty) and Cobb Salad (nice FRESH romaine) among them.  The outdoor seating is fun - but we opted ti sit indoors in the a/c.  Service by Sarah our server was great and friendly.  If we are in Medford lakes again we would return for lunch - but I bet dinner and happy hour are crowded and noisy.  Lunch is nice & quiet.

Better update the address - Foster's has not been on Union Street for YEARS - they moved to the shopping Plaza where Kmart is (and there used to be a SuperFresh there until 2009) on 611 near 313.  Anyhow, Fosters is our go-to place for balloons and party supplies, as well as all sorts of toys and bikes for kids.  They are NOT cheap.  It is NOT Toys-R-Hell, and the service is great and you pay for that.  I love Fosters - a Doylestown institution for many, many years.  And they have helped me make my kid's 1st & 2nd birthday parties so special (the dollar store in the same shopping plaza has cheaper balloons, but they don't last as long and they'renot open on Sundays.)  I trust that Foster's will get my balloon order right - and I am thankful for that!

We LOVE this place and always will. The Berley Brothers rock!  Excellent gummy bears (seriously - the best my 11 year old has ever tried) and great chocolate treats.  Packaging, music, decor and experience is second to none. LOVE IT HERE!

I found out about this place through Clare H. - a fellow yelper and friend.  She loves it here - I thought it was 3 or 4 stars for food and the decor is certainly not bad - but not terrific either.  Service was great.  OK - maybe I will cave and give them 5 stars?  I enjoyed my $14 lunch special of shortribs with brown rice - but the 3 grape tomatoes (and cucumbers) that came as a garnish were rotten inside.  Blargh!  Meanwhile the summer rolls & noodle soups here are far better than the place in Paoli that I frequent. (Er - used to frequent?)  So I will be pleased to come out here again.  Next time I gotta get some noodles!
I get all my cooking knives sharpened every year from Neil at the Media Farmers Market. he is a pro and can also handle scissors, Axes and even pinking shears!  Fantastic service! Fairly priced.

Still taking my elderly pug here - after all these years. Place is mobbed on Saturdays - but they are always friendly (staff and reception) and willing to taker th $100 - $200 I routinely drop every time I walk thru the door.  Excellent vet care - and we will continue to schlep our dog here from Philly until he they day he dies.

A five star experience with Greg & the gang (the entire crew was top notch and working hard).  Even Greg's parents were sitting next to us at the bar and enjoying their BYO Eggplant.  Jess was terrific, too!  Our 10 year old, once again, devoured her plate of surf & turf fajitas.  She loves this dish.  DH had the Seared Tuna special - and I had a bite, too.  Delish!  My enchilada was superior and the salsa verde just makes the dish.  They even had PERNIL on the menu.  Real PERNIL!  So impressive.  The service was just terrific and we were made to feel like family. Thus - a 5 star dining experience all the way around - even on a super crowded Saturday night.  We're coming back in 2 weeks - but this time we made a reservation using their new, cool app.  THANK YOU!!!!!! (And thank you to Greg's parents for the gift of Greg.)

The salads (especially in summer) and ceviches here are amazinglt fresh and flavorful.  I really ejoy it here, especially earlier in the evening before it gets too noisy and corwded.  LOVE the food at El Rey.

A fun place to browse for (and sometimes buy) costume jewelry and accessories.  My 9 year old can't get enough of the place.  Tables are coordinated by color family which is fun.  They also carry a limited selection of clothing and shoes -but the JEWELRY and hair accessories make this akin to a grown-up's Claire's.  Sparkly & Fun and not too hard on the wallet. Great for proms, weddings, color coordinating an outfit, interview stuff.  It's all FAKE (Costume) but it's all FUN!

So far we are very pleased with the Pediatric part of this practice (downstairs). We are sending our 8 year old here for cleanings and some restorative work.  Will report fully when the work has been done.  Bad news?  No more Saturday Appointments.

We stayed here in the mid nineties and it was mediocre then.  I can't imagine how it must have declined since - so my generous 3 stars should really only be 2.  Rooms were passable - and concierge service was nearly non-existent back then when we stayed here.  (We were visiting friends who went to Penn.)  Location was the main reason we stayed here.

5 star service for the bar staff (Matt and Allyssa) and our fabulous, attentive server, Valarie.  The atmosphere and vibe were perfect on a busy Friday evening.  Cocktails for Happy Hour (4 - 6:30 PM) are a great value at $8.  For $13.25 - not so much.  I had a Cucumber Gin/White Cranberry concoction and it was refreshing and enjoyable.  The food was just OK. The highlight for me were the $4.75 brussels sprouts - I got them sans bacon and they were perfectly roasted and wonderful.    The salad I chose was where things fell short.  I ordered the heirloom tomato and mozzarella salad (a dish I have had at many places, prepared in many different ways).  The "herb crust" on the mozz just ruined it.  (And I could tell is was good, quality mozz underneath.)  Also the tomatoes.  The small, mulit-colored tomoatoes were fine - but the thickly sliced green tomato (the "meat" of the dish") was over ripe and mushy.  Ick.  My friend got (what I was thinking of getting and should have gotten) the veggie sampler for $15.50.  Next time (if it is still available) I will get that.  The black bean taco and roasted tofu looked great.  So 3 star food and 5 star service/decor equals about 4 stars. Pretty darned good for a chain.

I concur with Carrie E and the many other 5 stars seen here.  WOWZA!  I just had my very first meal (lunch) at La Croix - and it will not be my last. Service is top-notch.  The server called me by name (Ms. F.) numerous times during the meal.  Attentive without being over-breaing and just perfect.  My dining companion started with the onion soup - which looked marvelous, and I had a delectable tuna tartare.  The swimmingly-fresh fish was cubed and tossed with a wonderful blend of herbs and red peppers (bell peppers), It was artfully plated with tiny cubes of fried diced potatoes.  For entrees my friend had a deliicous - if a bit salty for my taste - dish of baked ham & cheese risotto - so comforting on a winter day.  I had an Or-Gas-Mic and perfectly medium rare, sliced DUCK BREAST (Don't miss this) served with halved ripened blackberries and house-made gnocchi that were heaven on a plate.  Desserts were petit amuse-bouche style including profiteroles, chai creme brulee (miniature) and a sublim Opera torte (complete with the classic gold leaf garnish.)  I was having flashbacks to my honeymoon cruise in Europe.  What a TERRIFIC place.  Much like Arnold Scwartzenager - I'll be baaaack!  I gotta try that brunch.

Bill Haney who runs A & B Cleaning and Dana (and his team) have been cleaning our home for 2 months and so far, so good. They bring their own equipment (vacuum cleaner and all supplies) and charge a very reasonable rate.  We are lucky to have found them!  Update: It's 2014 and we still use A & B cleaners. Very pleased!

Brandywine Catering provides food services for "Dressage at Devon" and many other events. 3 stars is generous - as our food was both overpriced and underwhelming.  My 9 year old had a $10 pulled pork sandwich (came with an inedible side of vinergary 4 bean salad which no kid will ever eat - and no substitutions were available).  I had a $15 hunk of stone-cold (COLD) dried out baked ziti and a side salad.  (Salad was nice).  For $25 we ate sub par food amongst the blue-bloods for which this sum is no big whoop.  Meanwhile - we are glad there was something to eat other than "fair food" and fried things.  I just wish they could keep the hot foods hot. And add some seasoning.

I have never been to John's restaurant, Pizza & Pasta - but they are a godsend to those of us who work at the Amtrak Mechanical Yard.  John brings us goodies like spinach &  ricotta pizza, salads and penne with chicken & broccolli 3 days a week.  The crispy chicken salad with hard boiled egg and Ken's Honey Mustard Dressing was great!  Lettuce (albeit iceberg) was crispy, fresh and rust-free.  Pasta dishes are a little too heavy on the garlic and oil for my tastes  - even when I ask for them "light" on the sauce.  I also tried a cheesesteak roll (Pizza dough wrapped around cheesesteak meat and American cheese).  If you call in your order in advance, they will make you whatever you like.  The other day I had a REAL Veal Parm with spaghetti and delicious (garlicky) garlic bread plus a can of soda for $8.50!!!  Today I had eggplant parm platter (no cheese) and it was PERFECTION - John had just gotten cases of farm-fresh eggplants.  We really appreciate having a nice hot meal nearby!  And they bring it right to our workplace! Thanks to Pizza & Pasta for their efficient catering.  I can't wait to try more items.  They bring the food right to our door!  God bless 'em!

4-5 stars for sure.  I am a huge proponent of greenmarkets and farmers markets and headhouse is no exception.  LOVE IT!  We got some terrific summer fruits here last summer and I can't wait to come bacak agin in May & June to snag some fresh berries.  Oh - and the fresh tomatoes in season are SLAMMIN'! Bring some cash.

No issues with this outpost of Giant on Route 3 right near 352. Got a few snacks at about 8 pm on a Saturday night and there were no crowds and no lines.  I bet it wasn't like that a few hours earlier, though.

This Mickey-D's has been on Sugan road for years and years.  I rarely stop in (I don;t "do" fast food) unless dragged in by a friend or relative.  But - they have clean (relatively) bathrooms and that has saved us on occaision.

Our family is a big Dos Gringos fan, but they really need to figure out a few things. We had a large group (12 people) and they could not seat us all together.  We made due a few feet apart.  Also the new male server is a little abrasive.  It's "his way or the highway".  I kinda miss the nice ladies at lunch time - but I guess they no longer work the dinner shift.  Also - do NOT come here for Dining Under the Stars (aka Chaos out in the Heat).  Service is way, way slow - and we know they are doing their best - but it's not working.  Demand is too high for supply.  Ran out of chips, ran out of mild salsa (made more).    In the mean time, the pitchers of Mango and Lemon/Lime margarita mix are terrific and after a few shots of tequila none of us cared.  Food was excellent - Chicken Enchiladas, Veggie Enchiladas, Fish Tacos and of course the AMAZING surf & turf fajitas.  One more small gripe:  We were changed a $2.95 sharing charge, but the platter was not split for us.  Basically we were charged for the server to give us 2 bread plates.  Wha?????  I don't mind paying a small sharing charge if it means the platter will, indeed, be split to share.  Ours wasn't.  Sorry to come off harshly - we still love you guys - but there are some areas for improvement.  Lunch?  Come here. Dinner (not on a Wednesday)?  Come here. Catering?  Come here. Large Group?  Don't come here. Dining out in the Chaos?  Do NOT come here.

I agree 100% with Ryan C.  I fall more toward the "chocosnob" in that to me, Godiva is not all that great.  The Eurpoean companies are superior for the most part.  But it beat's Hershey's!  My 5 year old loves the chocolate dipped strawberries - but at $5 a pop we are better off going to RTM or Little Italy for $2 berries.  They also now have a club where you can get 1 free piece (not a strawberry) from the chocolate case each month.  No purchase neccessary.  How sweet!

Twelve Baskets Cupcakes has set up a stand (again) at the Media Farmers Market on Thursday afternoons selling their pricey ($3.50 a pop) but gorgeous and most importantly moist & tasty cupcakes.  Packaging is very fancy.  The Lemongrass Blueberry intrigued - but since I was buying for the kiddo - she opted for Chocolate.  She loved it.  Many thanks. Support your local markets!

Yvonne - who usually works evenings at the main register - is a lovely lady. Both she and another sales associate helped me in the cosmetics department.  Even though i usually shop at the Walgreen's in Aston, I come to Paoli from time to time as it is on my way home from work.  The cosmetics lady was very helpful and I was able to get a name-brand gel manicure kit (including LED lamp) for $30 with coupons and deals.  Very pleased.

Meh.  Just like the ones in NYC - over priced but quck and convient with food that looks better than it tastes.  And $3.50 for a small bowl of lettuce (add ingredients to make a salad) is robbery!  And my egg bagel was flavorless and slightly stale.  Won't be back.

Just got 7 knives sharpened at the Media Farmer's Market (it's on Sunday mornings now from 9 AM - 1 PM) by Rich.  He did a great job however because he was so busy my knives (4th order in the line) that I dropped off at 11:15 AM were not finished until about 1:20 PM.  Since the market closes at 1, poor Rich was stuck there for who knows how long finishing up everybody's knife orders.  Tip:  Neil's only comes to Media on the last Sunday of each month, so get there EARLY.  The also sharpen garden tools and axes, scissors, too!  We need this valuable service.

Our company often has happy hours here. Drinks are fine - food is just average. It's bar food - wings, shipach/artichoke dip, hummus and pita, potato skins etc.  Meanwhile service was OK - not great and not bad - and we got great seats at a corner of the bar.  My "Ruby Red" was made with REAL grapefruit juice (I saw the bartender squeezing it), Cointreau and Grapefruit-flavored vodka.  Very summer-y and refreshing.  We also had a corporate lunch for 8 here - and the food was good - but not great.  Soups are very salty (Crab bisque) and salads, while BIG (the small was enormous) are mostly lettuce with a few of the "premium" ingreditents (Salmon and asparagus had 2 spears of asparagus, Beet Salad had one slice of Red beet (cut in half) and One slice of golden beet (cut in half).  While the beets were delicious - I would have appreciated more of them.  Crab cake ($6.95 additional) was good. Grilled fish entree was the best of the lot (fluke?) with jasmine rice and green beans.  I will be back with corporate events but given my own preferences I would not likely dine here on my own acccord.  Drinks?  Fine. Lunch/Dinner?  Maybe go elsewhere. (Oh - but where???)

Summer after summer, means softball games and post-game Gallucio's for Pizza (still greasy), Wings (The BBQ ones are great) and Beer.  Very attentive service - especially for a bar.  Wonderful to sit out back and chill. They treat our 7 year old well, too - and bring her fettucine with butter.

Wish it were a little more affordable because my now 13 year old LOVES to buy accessories and loves the shopping experience here.  Like "Claire's for grown ups"?  Maybe?  OK, maybe not.  But the separated by color displays are just. so. attractive to a tween or teen. Sparkly stuff.  Fun.  A great place to dispose of disposable income. Avoid if you don't have that!

My 9 year old asked me to say this first...  "They have very cold bathrooms".  The ladies rooms was FREEZING. Luckily the rest of the dining room was warm. Service was unobtrusive and fine.  Decor is very lovely.  Food?  Not so fresh.  I had a hamachi sushi lunch special ($17) and the 4 pieces of nigiri 2 tasted off.  9 year old's shu mai (8 pieces) and california roll were fine - maybe even 4 star.  Our friend's Drunken noodles were not terribly spicy but very tasty.  If I ever return I will order cook dishes and not get sushi again here. Which is a shame because I love good sushi.  Note:  We returned a few weeeks later (for business lunch) and I had tofu pad Thai (lunch special $11 with a green salad) and it was fine.  Good but not mindblowing.  Full bar.

What would we do on a rainy day without IKEA?  Our 4 year old can play here and eat a cheap lunch.  We don't really buy much furniture here.  I feel glad to have graduated from the post-collegiate disposable furniture era of my life, but we do come here.  Often.  At least monthly - to entertain our kid.  Last time we bought a cute "Fishie" bath mat for 4.99.  Oh and as of 10/1/08 - no more plastic bags - so bring your own! (Or buy one for 55 cents.)

Now that's we are local-yokels, Linvilla is all the more pleasant. We now live about 5 minutes away - so we go during off times - like March (when all the veggies are 50% 0ff) and get our fresh apple cider donuts (skip the pies - they are not made there - but they are BAKED there), and feed the chickens, goats and an ostrich or two.  Great playground for my 7 year old. We might even have her birthday party here.  It is madness in October, though. Just madness.

I adore much this place.  Everything from the decor and service once inside (the receptionists rudely demand that EVERYONE in your party be present before being seated - and they don't reserve for small groups.  BLAH!!!!).  The waiters are so entertaining - and even balance drinks and tray of drinks on their heads.  (Maybe one of the pre-requisites to employment there is to have a flat head?)  Anyhow, the food is really great - especially the Molcajete dishes and Guacamole.  The appetizers are great too and for lunch try the (affordable) enchildas.  Expensive - but so worth it - for true haute-Mexican cuisine.  This ain't no Qdoba and I am glad of that.  Oh - and the tequila selection and CLASSIC Margaritas are perfectly balanced, fresh and re-freshing.  LOVE 'EM!!!

Well, my husband & I finally tried this place - we've driven by a bunch of times but never went.  And we would consider returning (although Shiroi Hana is more convenient for us - and lately I've been really into Vic's.)  The place was nearly empty at 5:30 on a Friday.  The hostess asked if we had a reservation and we told her that we did not.  She made a negative face so I asked her if that was a problem (The place was empty except for one male couple lingering - and they were there before we got there AND after we left.).  She said no and seated us.  I stopped by the sushi bar to bow to the chef and take a peek at the fish.  Looked good.  Chef recommended the Red Snapper and O-Toro.    We started with an order ($3.00) of Pork Wasabi Shumai.  - 2 large shumai.  Tasty and very wasabi-ish.  My husband ordered a bowl of udon (very tasty dashi broth) a spicy tuna roll which he loved, and a negi-hamachi roll which was just OK.  I got a special roll (Jay roll?) with rice "pops" on it - good but I did not care for the spicye-level of the tuna filling.  It was too hot for me.  (And I had asked for it mild.)  I bet if you are a spicy lover you'd like the rolls here.  Tuna was fresh - but not the yellowtail.  Also my $6.00 piece of O-Toro was gristley and GROSS.  What a shame.  Toro should be a mouth-gasm and this was not.  The best sushi I got was the Inari stuffed with chopped tuna (spicy tuna - this time WAS made mild) and garnished with chunks of avocado and a few pine nuts.  The pine nuts really made it so special.  I would DEFINITELY get that again.  For dessert we had the green-tea icecrem filled mochi which was very good.  Oh - and they do NOT make their own tamago - it's frozen - so we did not order any.
Just OK as starbucks go. Decent service - but I have yet to make a connection with a specific barrista.  Bathrooms are locked (you need to ask for a key) and filthy nonetheless.  Good location.

Yikes - I can't breathe. The overwhelming fog of patchouli hit me like a wall the moment I walked in.  I tried to get past it - that and the chanting music in the background. (I thought they were singing "Trim the edges, Trim the edges" until I realized it was Sanskrit or something).  Anyhow, I loved the merchandise but I can't deal with the intense allergic coughing fit I have upon entry.  Need some sage smudge sticks?  This is your place!

This is a review for the Charbucks next to the Wyndham Garden Inn on Route 100 in Exton,  This Starbucks is walk-able from there and literally saved me throughout the weekend of a conference where I was forced to stay at the Wymdham.  I came here for breakfast - got some decent coffee and a breakfast sandwich which beat the heck out of the pre-packaged "Grab & Go" garbage that the hotel was offering.  I alsostopped in around 3 PM during a break in the conference and got a much-needed Macchiatto (sp??).  Thank you, FOURBucks.
Food quality and service - 4 stars, dining room (sooooo hot in here) 2 stars.  Get it to go!

Unlike Rachel, I was/am not thrilled with the D-town produce outlet.  yes - the prices are low - but often the fruit  (berries & grapes especially) is what I call, "eat now or forever hold your peace". Meaning it is about 16 hours away from becoming rotten.  Be very careful not to over buy here or you will end up throwing away alot of over-ripe produce.  Crowded on weekends and "after work" dead the rest of the week - check them out on a Tuesday or Wednesday AM when it's dead-empty.

I used to come here when it was Genji - and frankly due to the economy (I am in brokeville these days) and a slightly icy experience when I last visited Genji (over a year ago) I was reticent to try Kin Gyo.  Well, boy am I ever glad I stopped in tonight for a solo sushi bar dinner. Yama, the chef/owner was accomodating and cordial.  I savored a delectable negi-hamachi hand roll, a salmon lover's roll (very good but a bit steep at $13.50), a succulent solitary piece of (of all things) foie gras nigiri (Yum and fat-city), 2 HOUSE_MAD tamago sashimi (excellent).  The only negative?  The ikura sushi piece was not quite as "poppin' fresh" as i would have liked.  Meanwhile - Yama makes his OWN inari (what a rarity that can be in the sushi world).  And at $7.00 a pop, I think I will wait till next time to try the Chu-toro (which I actually prefer to the fattier and pricier O-toro).  My faith has been restored.  I disagree with Victoria - the fish was all fresh (save for the ikura which was fresh but not "peak").  Service was very nice,and i can't wait to return.  Dinner for one (just me - no beverages) was $45 including tip.
This place is GREAT for lunch.  Thai, Cheesesteaks, fresh veggies, deli, sushi.  We had very tasty (and spicy) Thai from Jeenwong yesterday.  Nice!  Can't wait to return.

This place is a true hidden treasure.  I am almost afraid to review it, lest I can no longer get an appointment due to the mad rush that will ensue  At first, when you walk by the small red-letters "Francis" are nearly un-noticeable.  Francis Salon is next door to Primo Hoagies in a row-home on the first floor.  It is a small place with 2-4 "chairs" and a single shampoo sink in the back.  Francis, himself is a maestro - a master colorist with Clairol (yes, ladies - this is old-school Clairol which is impeccably applied.)  His assistant ggives a great shampoo and massage (now don't get dirty thoughts in your head.  it's not THAT kind of massage.)  Francis sells NO PRODUCTS - but simply charges $40 for a cut $75 for a cut and single process color or $105 for a cut and a few highlights.  WHAT A DEAL and waht a life long f friendship/hairdresser relationship has ensued.  My little daughter had her very first h/c here and I had Francis do my pre-wedding color and cut.   I love Francis - the man and the salon.  A-men!!!

I attended a breakfast meeting for 24 people (although only 19 showed up) with a sumptuous salad bar buffet (complete with 1/2 sour pickles and egg, tuna & chicken salads - all of which tasted great).  They also had egg omelettes to order - I had an egg white LEO (Lox, Eggs & Onions) wioth choppoed tomatoes added.  The chef, Bill and all the staff (butlered juices and coffee servers) were so kind and lovely.  Wonderful food & service. A great place to host events large or small.

A large location complete with cat, dog, fish and small mammal supplies. They also have doggie training classes. Maria - our instructor - is great.  She owns a huge rottweiler and knows how dogs behave.
Just awful. The restrooms were filthy and nearly un-usable.  Food was dreck.  Not goin' back.
A good source for spices and dried herbs.  Not as much fun as Penzey's - but good prices on most things.

The ladies in here are always so kind to me - and my 8 year old if she's ever with me. They always ask me about her if I go in without her to get her monthly treat.  I get the "free piece" - you can get 1 free piece of chocolate from the case each month - not including certain large items and no chocolate-dipped fruit.  My little one loves the Chocolate Lava Cake and Red Velvet Cake truffles. One summer they had a pineapple truffle and she went crazy for that one, too.  She also likes the dipped berries - but those are not free.  Thanks, Godiva - for making my 8 year old spin around in circles for 20 -30 minutes on her sugar/chocolate-induced high.
Convenient Wawa heading up 252 - coffee/smokes/snacks - check/check/check. And you can get a hoagie.  Wawa is the quintessential PA convenience store.

A friends and I both had Kalbi ($13) lunch boxes here.  Panchan was OK - not great. (Bean spouts were good, fish cake is not my thing and pickled cukes were ok.)  Kalbi itself was tasty.  Salad was iceberg and raw white onions in a mayo-ish dressing.  For $13, I'd rather get sushi at Vic or a bowl at Tampopo (which is also mediocre.)  I miss a really GOOD kalbi or bulgoki.  This place is OK - not bad but not great. It is on par with what Miran was.

I have been coming here/working here/living near here since the late 70's so my how PV has grown.  Now there is a festival just about every weekend in the summertime - and the place is crawling with displaced NYers.  But, it is still charming and you MUST go here at least twice in your life - once during the Strawberry ot Teddy Bear Festival and once on a MID WEEK day in the morning - when it's dead as a doornail and you can actually shop in peace.  Don't miss Penn's Purchase nearby and Granpa Hicks, Total Animal, and Accents & Images Gallery.

I stumbled upon Persian Grill on my way to a 7:00 meeting in the 'burbs.  I walked in at 6 PM on a Tuesday and the place was DEAD - in fact I thought it was closed from the parking lot - but went inside anyway.  No hostess, no wait staff, EMPTY diningroom - except for an elderly couple slowly eating in a front booth.  The rice platters they were eating looked good so I hung around.  Finally a lovely lady came out and seated me and I told her that I was on a tight time frame.  She said it would be no problem.  Then she disappeared for a long while and then came back and took my order.  The food - and I love Persian/Iranian food - was just Ok - yes the rice was 5 star stellar - but I paid $30 for a plate of rice and overcooked chicken (in a delicious sauce, though) thighs (Fesenjoon).  The chicken was so dried out and hard.  Yick.  Meanwhile the rice (and the crispy/burnt rice on top) was great. I also enjoyed the Shirazi (cucmber/tomato/onion salad) but it was drowning in lemon juice and way too oniony.  I wanted to LOVE it here - and many people do, but the slow service, high prices, awful chicken and DATED ancient decor downgrade it for me. And $30 for basically rice and onion salad (no drinks, no dessert).  Other diners got baklava (not sure if they ordered it) but I never got any.  Needs a service and decor makeover.  STAT. I will come back once more to try the lamb chops - but I won't be rushing back.

I am a sucker so I bought a Groupon - but silly me - I didn;t read the not-so-fine print and the groupon was for DINNER ONLY.  Thank goodness they honored it at lunch but you had to order off the dinner menu (no cheapie lunch specials for the groupon.).  That was fine by me. I started my meal with an OK version of Tom Kha Gai (Thai Chicken Coconut Soup).  This is my favorite soup ever so I have to say this version was very nice - not too sweet and not overly rich with too much coconut milk.  4 stars.  An iceberg salad (gloppy ginger dressing on the side) came next.  Meh.  Fine.  There was ONE cherry tomato and ONE cucmber slice buried at the bottom. Whatever.  Next I got a specialty sushi roll (I can;t remember which one - I think it was the Lotus Inn Roll) that was just OK.  The sushi fish here is just OK.  Not bad and not great.  I also got an order of sake (salmon) sashimi ($6.50 for 3 thin slices) which I never should have gotten.  Meh.  For $14.95 I expect more than an alaskan roll with a few slivers of Escolar on top.  Escolar is NOT white tuna.  Albacore is white tuna. Thank goodness I remembered to get the sauce on the side.  Fish was good - but not superb.    But whatdya expect? Meanwhile the party of 6 next to were raving about their chicken & brocolli and shrimp chow mein.  Maybe I oughta stick to cooked foods here. Or the Salmon Lovers Lunch ($14.95) which I have gotten a few times.  Atmoshpere is relaxing.

Beats the heck outta Starbucks.  Plus it's a local institution - IF you can find a table on a busy summer day.  Nice big cones of ice cream and lots of coffee to drink in store or purchase (whole bean or ground) for take home.  In the '80's and '90's (yeah - I'm dating myself again) I even knew some of the kids who worked there.  these kids now prob'ly have kids of their own.  A cute spot - and great after a movie at "The County".

Ellen - the lunch-time bartender (who also served our lovely lunch) is terrific and has been here for years.  I enjoyed the new "spa" menu - and had the $21 3 course lunch - a delightful tomato soup with ginger and lime, a small portion of artic char (like salmon) over beans and oven roasted tomatoes (super juicy and cooked perfectly) and a lo-cal mokha meringue with fruit compote.  (OK - not awesome).  A pleasure to dine in the BAR AREA.  Nice and quiet.

I love Sook Hee's!  Even moreso now than when they first opened. Sook Hee herself is a sweetheart and the juices and fresh salads are a must when I need a healthy pick-me-up in the Comcast Center.  I just got a fresh small salad for $3.99 and it was delicious.
Oh no!  They are closed?  I hear the Franklin Fountain people bought them. I hope they re-open soon.  They were great last spring for Easter Bunnies!

I love trader joes - and this one is smack dab in the middle of down-town Media.  (With parking - yay!)  Same stuff as at my beloved Phillybranch - but pomegranate seeds were $4.99 in Media - just $3.99 in Center City.  Odd.  Great frozen meals, too.  LOVE!!!!
Good, greasy, basic pizza - a little expensive for what it is. Plus they sell gelato, subs & salads.

A friend and I finally got a chance to try Nom Nom (the name kills me!), and it made me lament for the five dollar bowls of ramen from Larme Dosanko back in NYC "back in the day".  Wow for ramen this is pricey stuff.  $8.00 for the regular bowl (I got Shoyu, friend got Kari).  We both got the poached egg (I was "meh" about it - will skip it next time) and extra noodles (WOW!  Should not have done it - but got to take some home.) The extra noodles are $1.85 ish and worth it.  We also shared an order of pork buns which rival those at Chifa.  VERY good!  Wish they'd do a non-pork bun (Tofu??).  Oh - and they NOW OFFER TAKE OUT.  PLEASE start taking credit cards!!!  PLEASE!!!!

The frozen custard is quite good.  I am not a water ice eater - but I love the custard at Rita's.  News flash! Their "Gelatti" is NOT Gelatto.  It is a bastardization combo of water ice and custard.  Whatever.  It tastes good.  Bring on the coffee flavored frozen custard, please.

Note:  I have never stayed here - this review is based on the great job Sofitel did catering our Corporate Holiday party in 2006.  Gorgeous ballrooms, great services, fantastic food.  (We had stations - multiple stattions - with delicious food.)  Even getting a cab home was organized and well executed.  GREAT JOB SOFITEL.  Review of bar food by Chez Colette at Sofitel:  Let me make it clear that I am reviweing the restaurant in the BAR AREA at the Sofitel - but it is the same menu and same kitchen as Chez Colette.  Service here has always been great for us - we come for lunch and I usually get the Salmon over butternut squash risotto - which is a rich, delicious meal.  My friend usually will get a burger that is served with an enormous cone of thinly cut greasy fries.  (Yes - they are a little BKish.)  The food was really good - and I had freshly squeezed OJ.  Eat in the bar - for the comfy couches and big tables and people watching.  The main restaurant (which I have never sat in) is usually dead empty.

Now that I have explored lots of deli options in PHilly and South Jersey - I goot say - for corned beef?  Hershel's is absolutely 5 star in my book.  I often will get a 1/4 or 1/2 lb of sliced corned beef to go along with my fruits & veggies from Iovine's or Fair Food Farmstand.  A few decadent slices are all I can handle.  This is GOOD stuff!

Consistently terrific - Mama's also offers tuna, stuffed grape leaves and a variety of salads and veggies in addition to the fried eggplant, latkes and falafel.  Tahini and hummus are always a treat here.  LOVE it at Mama's - and for $9.50 including tax I can eat like a queen!

We went to tequila's last night for Tres de Mayo (instead of dealing with the Cinco de Mayo crowds).  Margaritas were not nearly as heavenly as in the past.  Too sweet and "lemonadey" this time.  Oh well.  Meanwhile, the food was good - but not 5 star.  My dish (at least to me) was the best - a special of Langostino, split and grilled and sauced with a yummy tequila, garlic and pepper sauce.  Flavorful - but not too hot & spicey.  Tequila's makes one of the BEST Caesar salads EVER,  It can run heavy on the dressing, so i always ask for it lightly dressed and last night's was up to par and delicious.  Our female server (her name escapes me) was lovely and attentive.  The BEST 5 star part of the meal was the Tres Leche cake (which the 3 of us split - we were stuffed).  The worst - which made me downgrade from 5 to 4 stars - was the queso fundito.  Just tooo heavy and greasy.  A big crock of melted cheese.
