(I didn't order it - I never would have in a million years.)  Bring back the FRESH lime margaritas and I'll quickly re-up you to 5 stars.  Tequila's is a great restaurant.  I recommend it to out of town guests often.  Oh - and please start taking reservations.  (Right now they'll only reserve for parties of 6 or more.)

OK, maybe I am biased - because not only am I a patient, but I used to work for Dr. Snyder waaaaaaaay back when.  She is always at the forefront of cosmetic and restorative dental procedures.  She just does damned good denistry.  The office environment is clean, state-of-the-art and at the same time, warm & welcoming.  Her staff is helpful and friendly.  I have since moved away - bt anytime I am in Doylestown and need a cleaning - I go see Dr. Snyder and her hygienist.  It's a terrific practice that I endorse most highly.

This is a review for the Bacco (new location) in the Doylestown shopping Center.  I fully agree with Cheri C.  The food is excellent and the poritons are enormous.  But it took foreever to:  1.  be greeted 2.  be seated (we wound up seating ourselves) 3.  get menus 4.  have someone wait on us 5.  get our food (cooked to order so that was OK) 6.  get our bill  It was like pulling teeth getting service - and the place was not busy.  Our party of 4 ordered Pasta fagiole soup (huge bowl for $3.95), linguini with (REAL) clams - so good, Chicken parm (served with a delicious side of mezza-rigatti pasta in a crushed tomato sauce), and I had the Chicken florentine.  It was terrific.  We'd like to go back but only if we have lots of time to wait around (for the servers) and thus I would never bring my little kid here.
What a welcome green space in Center City. Fitler square has a cute little fountain, shady trees and lots of cute coffee bars and places to explore nearby.  Love this area.
Took my 6 year old here last night and we sat on the high-stools and blissfully munched on Sicilian and veggie slices.  GREAT oizza and very friendly service.  LOVE IT!

This places ROCKS!!!  (And I don't really like falafel - there's is great.).  I usually get a fresh-baked whole wheat pita and a few slices of the most YUMMY friend eggplant.  The hummus is smooth and flavorful - not overpowering. I hate tahini - so none of thast por moi, but bring on those valuable veggies.  Crisp and fresh always.  And hot young men are often manning the counter.  A-men to that!  The side bar with olives and delctable fried (a bit oily) cauliflower [and I am not normally a fan of the 'flwoer] is wonderful, too,.  Great latkes. Great pita Spectacular Sandwiches - and don't miss that eggplant.  This is middle-eastern/kosher paradise for vegans, veggies & carnevores alike.

You really haven't lived until you've had brunch and dinner (they are different experiences) at Commander's.  Bananas Foster is a MUST try here.  The service is white-glove and attentive.  The classic dining rooms (even post-Katrina) recall a bygone era.  It's worth the money and time to come here.  FOR REAL.

Marathon - you have redeemed yourself.  After years of boycotting Marathon (a close friend used to date one of the owners who treated her badly) I lifted said ban and attended a group function at this location - and honestly, truly - everything was A-OK!  Our group of about 60 people had a set meal.  As we arrive each place had a lovely salad (pre-set) with tomato, cucumber, lettuce and roasted beets.  Servers passed bowls of feta on the side.  Dressing was a sweet "buttermilk" style and was served along side.  Each person got a roll and butter.  The main meal was the same for everyone (unless you were vegetarian) - grilled salmon served in a square bowl atop a mound of farfalle with tomato/veggie sauce.  It honestly was really tasty.  Dessert platters of fruit and cookies/brownies/bars were passed afterward with coffee.  A cash bar was available.  Service was very good considering the crowd size.  I have now officially lifted my ban on Marathon.

Oh, the NBI - for me 3 stars is being very generous.  Mostly because my high school best friends younger sister used to LOVE this place.  We never did.  Standard pub grub and beer after beer.  OK When you're a teenager (Oh wait, they can't serve underagers any more - my bad!) but I've outgrown this place.  Its a basic bar.

I have used A & B cleaning services for over 4 years now and they are terrific.  We have had some specific re-training issues that needed to be addressed about 3 year sin when our original team of 2 ladies switched but now we are back on track and everything is "Spic and Span".  I love working with Bill and the team and A & B cleaners. We trust them in our home.

It's a dive bar, it's cheap - and  it can be fun. I attended a large company party there - and we had blast - and some folks got good and blasted themselves.  Dan is a charmer - and Liz, our server was terrific. Food was just Meh, (Extremely salty green beans (frozen), overcooked rice, and average meatballs.  But dive bars just ain't my thang.  P.S.  They are remodelling soon so it may improve things,

We have visited the Pig Placement Network's booth at A-Day at Delaware Valley College for 2 years in a row and can't wait to attend the annual PiggyPalooza benefit at Ross Mill Farm this June 22.  Ross Mill Farm (outside of D-town in Rushland, PA) serves as an educational facility, foster care and sanctuary for pet potbellied pigs.    The pigs are so smart, friendly and cute.  Our 8 year old fell in love instantly.  We are big fans of the valuable work they do here - and making sure that ignorant people don't adopt pigs only to give them up after a few months.  An excellent resource.

A friend of mine got us 2 free passes otherwise, I quite honestly never woulda thunk to come here.  Today I took my 6 year old daughter here and we arrived at 3 PM (They close at 5).  We will definitely come back one more time - soon - to see the rest.  We straight away headed to the submarine (creepy & cramped) and ship that are docked nearby.  This took about 35 minutes.  Then we started in on the exhibits - and did not get all the way through.  We spent a long time in the boat shop.  I had no idea they actually build, replicate and restore boats for museums all over the east coast.  While we were there, one of the head builders stopped sanding long enough to tell us about a design they are working on for the Seaport Museum at Mystic, CT.  Neat-o!!!  The lights were dimmed at 4:45 - so we headed to the gift shop.  Whew - narrowly escaped that one.  We'll be back soon.  I enjoyed this a heck of alot more than I thought I would - on the surface it seems like a real snooze fest.  But with the 6 year old in tow - it was much better.  Oh and it was great to come on a random Monday in April than say - July 4th when tourist central swoops in.

I may be dating myself - but I went here when I was in college at Penn in the mid nineties.  Cav's is still kicking (and they also have the "River Deck".  It's your basic bar.  Bar food.  Bar Music.  Frat-boy (and college-gals) crowd.  Meat-marketing and bozzing of the basest nature.  Decent wings as I recall.   I preferred Smokey Joe's.

Overpriced for sure - I mean, I spent nearly $20 (including tip) for a lemonade/ice green tea and a tomato-brie-proscuitoo omelette.  Sheesh.  Meanwhile the service was terrific (2 very nice gals) and I got to feel like a true "Lady Who Lunches" (Or rather breakfasts??) on a Friday at 9 AM.  Breads are stellar - and they serve a myriad of tasty confitures (apricot!!) and chocolate spreads (Noir, Noisette) to go with them.  Next time I will get a croissant to go and save $12.

It really IS ALL THAT. Yes, it's small & loud - so if you come on a weekend call in advance and STILL be prepared to wait.  Chef RED did his thing tonight.  As did Steve, our server. In fact, all the staff were "on point".  The sweet lady who gave us the marvelous bread (infused olive oil with a blob of lemon ricotta in the center) and kept our water glasses full is a doll. The hostesses even helped to clear plates.  Everyone pitched in and ran their asses off!  A great team.  We noticed and we love ya!  One warning - this meal is a diet-breaker.  Nothing we had was "light 'n healthy".  They should have an MD onsite to perform emergency angioplasties.  I had heard of Modo Mio for a long while - but when I tasted the Mozarella en Carroza at the "Taste of Philadelphia" event in July, I knew I had to come here.  Our party of 4 had the 4 course menu and everyone LOVED everything they had.  The house-made pappardelle with brussels sprouts, the bistecca, the skate wing - all of it.  Chef RED even sent out a platter with 6 glorious desserts on it.  Standouts were the flourless chocolate cake, tiramisu (theirs is light and wonderful), pumpkin bread pudding and home-made crusts, cookies, cremes and panna cottas of all sorts.  A near orgasmic experience at Modo Mio tonight. Only one complaint, at 8:50 PM (We had a 6:45 reservation and were seated closer to 7 PM), they made us leave to seat the next table.  Politely.  Overtly.  But I only had like 2 sips of that wonderful coffee I wanted to enjoy.  Ah well - next time we will come on a weeknight.  WOW!!!!  Can't wait to come back. Can't wait to try Paesano.  (You do own that, right??)

Conveniently located right in Center City - but pricey and a limited selection on items my 8 year old artiste actually uses.  Great in a pinch - and get the student card for a discount (which makes it worth it).  We shop here, Pearl (now closed), Uterecht, AC Moore, Michaels, JoAnnes Fabrics and lots of other places for crafting supplies, canvas, paints and brushes.  We even get the kiddo her own French Easel (but not from here!) - so she can apply to Studio Incamminati when she's ready.

Had a memorable meal with top-notch service from Ella at Casta Diva tonight. My good friend and I both had the beet salad to start (so delicious and fresh).  She had the salmon with crispy skin and red wine sauce.  (A generous piece - or "portion")  I enjoyed the salmon tartare stuffed cannaloni app as an entree.  La Colombe coffee and our own BYO wines sealed the deal.  A great night with stellar food.  The only downer?  Cash only.  Wish I'd known that before we went.
Love KK and this branch is friendlier than the Paoli location. Picked up some Republic of Tea.  Parking sucks - meters are broken.  LOVE.

I went here with 2 girlfriends.  We all split 1 salad (so yummy) 1 appetizer and 1 pasta entree (which was huge) and bought dessert.  Honestly - it was more than enough.  The home-made stuffed pastas are very good.  They also offer "couchlike" outdoor seating (which we did not choose - we sat inside).  They also make pizzas - which we did not order - but they all looked delicious.  We'll be baaaack!

Doesn't do a damned thing for me.  But it is CHEAP and you can get sammies, burgers and FRIED pub grub here for a quick lunch or a beer after work.  Maybe I am too snooty-snotty for this, but I am not a fan.

I am not a big DD fan - but the coffee is fine.  I don't eat the donuts (which are not freshly baked - and usually taste stale to me) and NEVER eat the 400 PLUS calorie breakfast grease-wiches.  It's a good place to get a Vanilla Iced Decaf or a quick cup of joe when it's cold out.  But that's all.

All vegetables (not fruit) are 50% off from Jan 1 - March 31 every year!!! It is a terrific deal and we now buy 95% of our veggies at Linvilla (includes tomatoes which technically are not a veggie).  Love the winter veggie sale!  Also in 2016 apples (many varieties) are 69 cent per lb!  Stock up!!!!!

It was a cold rainy November night when I stumbled into Pho Cali - and believe it or not I actually ordered Pho!  I ordered the "rare steak" pho for $6.50 - and it was great - but the steak (very thinly sliced and tender) was not rare.  I guess the steaming hot broth cooked it through by the time it got to me.  The Pho came with a plate of traditional garnishes - fresh white bean sprouts, slices of green jalapeno, fresh lime,  Delicious!  And for $6.50  Digs could use a makeover.

Surprisingly the service we had here (dine in) was good. DD - our 8 year old - had a certificate for a free personal pizza for being a good reader in school, so we indulged her and she got a cute (tiny) pie with black olives.  She was fine.  I tried a pasta dish. Drowning in a tasteless greasy sauce.  Fail.  It's not happening again. Sorry.  If you like pizza hut pizza - this location is relatively well-run and has a dine-in area that is pleasant.  Order the (grease-laden) pan pizza, bring the kiddies and DINE IN - for fresher tasting pies.  Big flat-screen TVs broadcast "the game". I guess we really, truly live in the 'burbs now.  Yawn...

Love Park would be great save for the numerous homeless and addicts that congregate there.  My little daughter loves the fountain and to run around it and the LOVE statue.  The water in the fountain is seriously gross.  (Probably from said homeless people bething and peeing in it.)  Wish Philly could address these types of problems better. There seem to be more homeless and addicts here than even in NYC. (At least here they are more visible and aggressive.)

FABULOUS FIND - i can't believe I never came here before. Nick, the owner - is a sweetie and he has 2 cute dogs and a cuter 2 year old.  To top it off in amongst the vintage vinyl and new-er CDs he found me a rare 4 disk set of the Complete Bob Marley (with and after the Wailers).  I snapped that right up.  Can't wait to come back.  Bravo!!!

Not bad for a chain.  My 3 year old daughter likes to watch the "pizza man" make pizza - so she, of course, loves it here.  It's better than Olive Garden - but not as good as Bensi's - in the "Scheme of mock-Italian chains".  It is also less noisy in atmosphere and decor than the obnoxious Buca di Beppo.  I'd go here if it was nearby - but would NOT go out of my way to eat here. At least it's not too expensive.

I, too, have a love/hate relationship with Amtrak - seeing as I take it every 2 weeks like clockwork - it is a necessary evil in my life.  First of all the prices.  They're high.  Acela is a complete rip off saving you maybe only 20 minutes of time from Philly to NYC - and that is only if the trains are on time.  Don't bother.  Also you can skip upgrading to Business class - what a freakin' joke.  It's the same seats - just the front car.  BFD!!!  OK, now the schedules - IF they are running on time with no delays they would be adequate.  But you can forget about holidays - when crowded trains are OVERSOLD and running late.  Thanksgiving weekend is a NIGHTMARE,  Basically between T-giving and January 6 the weekends are all a colossal mess.  Bring your own food - many trains no longer have the cafe car.

Hesrchel's meets with my approval:  Dr. Browns?  Check Extra lean corned beef?  Check REAL Rye bread?  Check  Service with a smile?  Double check.  What nice young men.  If I gotta have a jewish deli style corned beef sandwich - I come here! Save me a Diet Dr. Brown's cream soda!
It's fine.  Decent coffee and tea drinks, a reasonably clean restroom, and plenty of seating to work for a while or just relax.  Great location near the "Gayborhood" and Jefferson.

5 stars for food and value - 2 or 3 for decor. When I moved here from NYC about 3 years ago - one of my favorite restaurants in NYC - Afghani or otherwise was Pamir.  So 2 or 3 New Years Eve's ago we went to Kabul - and what'd'ya know?  The owner is the cousin of the man who owned Pamir (which, alas, has since closed in NYC.).  The menus are nearly identical and oh, how I love the fried pumpkin turnovers (Buranee Kadu).  In fact, anything with pumpkin is a yummy choice here.  The service is good - very friendly but they can seem aloof - so if you WANT more water/sauce/napkins - you need to be pro-active (some may see this as a bad thing.).  It was also a great place to have an un-crowded experience.  The place is rarely crowded.  (Possibly because it is a bit old and grungy looking.)  Don't let the crummy decor dissueade you - TRY THE FOOD - terrifc Chalau (stews) and Pallaus (Pilafs/Rice dishes).  I love Afghan food and I love the food at Kabul. And it is a GREAT value for very little money.  Maybe they'll re-decorate some day?  (Not likely.  *sigh*)

Stopped into El Rey this time during happy hour - and man, WHAT A DEAL.  I got 2 of the $1 tacos - one chicken and one fish (the fish taco was perfect!!!  Cabbage, lime-cilantro-crema and fresh fish).  I also had a $4 house margarita.  If you are around early in the evening and need a tasty snack - you can't beat the $1 tacos at El Rey!  They are small - but 2 or 3 or 4 of them together are plenty.  Good service, too.  I am still lovin' it here!

I have been here 3-4 times over the past 2 years.  I have lunch here whenever I go to our Malvern Ofice.  I usually get a Chinese or Thai lunch special - as they are a bargain at 7-8 bucks each, but I am always tempted by the sushi menu.    Alas, I only had sushi once.  It was good as I recall but not mind blowingly so.  I really enjoyed the Pineapple Thai Fried Rice.  Mango Shrimp was good - but a little too goppy and there was ketchup involved in the copious amounts of "sweet & sour" sauce.  I'd pass on it next time.  Choice of Soup or spring roll at lunch was also nice - with a crisp and only a tad too greasy spring roll.  I'll be back the next time I travel to Malvernia.  Oh - the parking lot in this "strip mall" is always JAMMED at lunch hour - so be forewarned.

Since my initial review I have been blessed, lucky and fortunate enough to dine for breakfast, 2 lunches and one life-changing dinner at LaCroix.  Last night my husband and a good friend and I shared in a wonderful meal, with top-notch service by Woody & many others.  After a round of delicious fresh-fruit laden cocktails (blood orange, blackberries, basil, lemon) we sat at a lovely table overlooking a snow-covered Rittenhouse square.  (We could see doggies playing in the snow!)  After an amuse-bouche of squab, fois-gras and horseradish foam, we had some appetizers.  My friend has the LaCroix Salad, and I enjoyed the Lamb carpaccio.  Another amuse of yellowtail was brought, followed by a lovely, simple beef consomme with a few pieces of udon, mushrooms and a single raw oyster that was gently cooked by the broth.  The main course was truly the star of the show.  DH enjoyed perfectly cooked shortribs accompanied by ricotta filled pierogie (yum!), our friends had a simple chicken and I again indulged in a lovely duck sous-vide.    Oh - and the desserts were marvelous.  Piecrust ice cream!  Chocolate tart!    Every bite was perfection.  A dreamy evening!

I had not gone back to pot belly as I did not like it - but we had a corporate luncheon catered from there today and a few things seem to have improved:  1.  The chopped salad with cranberries and walnuts was not too bad (I'd get it without onions in future).  2.  The meatball sandwiches arrived hot and the sandwich boxes (Box 'o sammies) were cute and well organized with a variety of sandwiches.  If I ever go to potbelly again I'm getting the meatball sub.  3.  The dark chocolate chip cookies seemed to be freshly-baked - albeit a bit greasy (butter or margaine?) - they were DELISH.  Much improved.

Went here for a very nice linner (that's half way between lunch and dinner) at about 4 PM on a rainy Sunday.  Since the lunch specials end at 3 PM, we ordered off the regular menu.  DH had a spokie pizza which he enjoyed and I got the dinner portion (enormous - took 2/3 of it home!) of chicken picatta, no capers.  Very good. Quite good for a chain. Really.  Excellent service as well (the place was dead from it being 4 PM on a rainy Sunday).

I jokingly call this place "Oh So Mediocre" but  it really is pretty good. It's the typical pay per pound hot & cold food bar.  The earlier you come - during the weekday lunch hour - the fresher and less "picked-over" the food is.  You can get salads, pasta, chicken, sushi (pre cut rolls) and chinese foods.  Not bad for a quick take out.

Delivery one night - our first time ever and it won;t be the last - but - we have never set foot in the place.  I suspect takeout is their forte.  Mei Fun is delish - and not greasy.  Spare ribs are a saucy greasy mess.  Dumplings are old-school doughy with pork  - el kiddo loved them, grown ups less so.  So far we just might convert from Da Shin to Jing Fong.  We miss old owners of Da Shin.

If you live in Philly or are visiting you HAVE to visit the liberty bell.  But once is probably enough.  To me this is the "new" liberty bell site - as I visited it in a different place as a kid.  This "new" site is much nicer and allows for better line/crowd control.

This review is for the Doylestown Starbucks in the historic Fountain House - that for years & years was a bank.  As you may know - if you read my reviews - I am not a big Fourbucks (aka Charbucks) fan, but this location - smack-dab in the middle of town - is a keeper.  The multiple room layout makes for a good spot to cozy up with a (burnt tasting overpirced)  coffee drink.  My little daughter likes the iced green tea lemonade.  A nice location with decent service for a Starbucks.  About as good as a Starbucks can get.  (Oh and boy, can it get crowded with yuppies!).

On a very hot Thursday Evening at 5:45 PM, 30 women decended on Modo Mio.   Sicilian fare was on the family style menu, and once we were seated, freshly sliced bread (two types) and caponata (eggplant, onions and pine nuts in olive oil) was brought to us.  Monsu is BYOB, so we brought many bottles of wine - red, white and otherwise.  Appetizers were brought by our terrific wait staff, including mussels in a spicy tomato, oregano and white wine broth. Next, came octopus (Polpo) salad with green olives and crunchy wild fennel.  Piping hot, crispy "arrancia" - Sicilian Rice Balls, quickly disappeared. They were filled with luscious saffron rice, gooey mozzarella cheese and savory mushrooms. For the vegetarians of the group a crisp bruschetta with a bright green fava and mint puree appeared, topped with a variety of heirloom tomatoes. The balsamic drizzled on the plate was finger-lickin' good!  Next, we were treated to several pasta primi (first courses). Plates of pillowy-soft ricotta gnocchi were sauced in a bright lemony-tomato cream, studded with chunks of sweet crabmeat.  A spicy (some thought too spicy) rigatoni with tuna as well as house-made taglietelle with a variety of roasted mushrooms and baby artichokes were quickly devoured.   Believe it or not - there was more!!  Next plates of Bisteck - a fried beef steak topped with fried egg, prosciutto and provolone in a savory sauce arrived.  A bit too salty for my taste, but certainly enjoyable. They run heavy on the salt here - so keep that in mind and if your are sensitive to sodium TELL THEM before you order.  For the non-meat eaters, there was Mackerel served over faro salad with roasted red peppers and (more) fennel.  Next came heaping bowls of fall-off-the-bone-tender pork osso bucco (folks ate all of it including the marrow).  An innovative accompaniment to the osso bucco were sweet chestnut pancakes.  Really super!  Our vegetarian friends enjoyed a smokey, freshly baked eggplant parmesan.  Delightful!  Finally, small dessert trays were passed among the tables.  A sweet vanilla panna cotta was topped with a rich strawberry/balsamic mix.  Gooey, rich, flourless chocolate "brownie" cake was enrobed in a thick salted caramel sauce.  A lemon bar, drizzled with raspberry sauce was topped with crunchy coconut shreds.  (By now many of us were too full to eat dessert - but somehow we managed!)  Kudos to Marguerite and Tyree - two of the 5 or 6 servers who helped our lively group.  They kept the water glasses filled and the plates cleared efficiently.  Such outstanding service!  5 star service - and nearly 5 star food - a few dishes were found by some to be overly salted or spicy - but in a group of 30 tastes can vary widely.  I can't wait to go back - and I will surely try the new Delco spot.

We've stopped in this Whole Foods numerous times on our way from Philly to Bucks.  We love Whole Foods (aka whole paycheck) and this one is no exception.  Great baked goods, cheeses, olives, meats, and especially produce.  Fun to shop here - and you can get some great ingredients.  Good pre-packaged sushi, too. Yummy prepared foods.

AVOID during festivals (Strawberry Fest, July 4th weekend, Teddy bears Picnic).  A tourist-packed cluster-f&@k.  Jully 4th weekend was an absolute zoo.  They need someone INSIDE the parking lot to direct people after the fireworks.  It took 40 minutes to exit the parking lot.  Unacceptable.

OK, I am upgrading them to 4 stars now. My husband, daughter & I have come here many times now after every softball game (win or lose).  DD is 5 and she loves the (greasy - blot it off with napkins first) pizza. I love the fettucine - perfectly cooked - aldente but somehow light tasting.  We also play the electronic bowling game in the corner of the bar.  Yes, the place is a bit "divey" but they sometimes have live music - and the back patio can be very nice if it's not too hot 'n humid at night.  The 4th star is now added for nostalgia.  We are making memories.
Fantastic service!  Changed our locks on-the-spot. Woody is great and the guys are so helpful here.  Will definitely call if we need them in the future.

A dreadful branch of Rite-Aid. A neccessary evil.  Clueless cashiers - and never enough of them, thus lines form.  They do have many convenience items, however, so for that - it's OK.  But this one is truly MEH.

BYO Tequila and be sure to have some of the FABulous guac. The steak and meat dishes are pricey - but delicious. Twice we had the Carne Asada and it was perfectly cooked.  The sauce is very rich, though.  Also try the delcious Beet & Goat cheese salad.  All the goodies are hidden under a mound of micro-green goodness.  2 juicy, fried plantain chunks accompanied the plate.  This upsacel Neuvo-Latino/Mex is a BYO and they make the margarita mix for you.  NO CREDIT CARDS and kinda snooty service.  Tables are small and closely spaced.    Our waiter was cute - but rushesd us along and we felt it.

Absolute Mediocrity - but very reasonably priced. Also note - the $4.99 Lunch special is for the regular Chicken teriyaki (not the teppanyaki/hibachi grill).  If you want Hibachi it starts at $6.99 (Veggies only) and goes up from there.  I came with a work group of 4 and the place was quiet on a Summer Friday at 12 noon. Another group of 3 was at the other end of our table.    I had the $8.95 Shrimp teriyaki lunch and it was fine.  They did the onion volcano and the "chuck the shrimp at the customer" thing and my 10 year old would have loved it.  VERY cheap bill - $65 for 4 people.  Simple, edible food.  Sushi looked OK - but the gal who ordered sushi only got an avocado roll.  I likely would not order nigiri or sashimi here.  Super Americanized from the gloppy mayo on the iceberg salad (I forgot to ask for dressing on the side) to having to ASK for chopsticks.  I am in no hurry to rush back - but that said, my colleagues have lunch here every other Friday.  WHATEVER.

Went to A-Day (Agriculture Day) again this year. Our little one is now 8 years old and still loves A-Day (although she has now declared that she si too old for pony ride because she "is in 4H and knows how to ride a horse by herself".  Still had a blast drinking a chocolate milshake and jumping on the bouncy-type rides for kids. Note - $10 to park in the field - so we walked.  Mom & Dad browsed the boutiques and stands, including Vik's Picks - for a jar of delicious home-made pickled beets.  Only ONE person selling local honey this year and it was cost prohibitive.  Bring back the bees!!!!  Als of note - over 4 different booths about dogs, dog rescue and pet adoption.  Including the Pig Placement Network (also at A Day last year with their "kiss a pig" donation fundraiser) which finds homes for pet potbelly pigs.  My kid fell in LOVE with those cute 8 week old oinkers.  Sheep shearing, Bovine and Equine exhibits and frisbee catching rescue dogs. Gorgeous weather helped.  WHAT FUN!
OMG.  Shrimp Scampi over Linguini - came with 6 big shrimp, just the right amount (but alot) of garlic & oil - not too oily/buttery.  Carby BLISS in a foil pan.  I love ya, John!

This is not a great place to shop - but sometimes when I need kids clothes in a pinch, it is a convenient place to go.  You really have to search and dig (and I mean really dig) thru the rumpled, disorganized merchandise.  Toddler sizes mixed in w/ babies - oh and there's a size 12 "big girl".  What's that doing there?  Who knows.  Don't ask the staff - their not around - only at the under-manned chechouts.  Not a fave - but as I said -in a pinch I can get kiddie stuff here.

Please note that they did our wedding from the main HQ in Willow Grove.  They did our wedding flowers and came in at just under our budget of $1,000.  Amy was terrific and the flowers were upscale and just what we wanted.  They were excellent in their communications via email and phone.  We paid for our wedding in 3 installments, in advance.  Most of our flowers involved Bluebird roses, blue hydrangea and different colored irises (light & dark blue and purple).  The colors were vibrant and the arangements, bouquets and boutenieres (all but one - which contained white freesia) survived our 96 degree wedding day.  The flowers on the cake were gorgeous, too, as were the 10 six inch bubble-bowl centerpieces.  We love Kremps.

I hate to give 1 star reviews unless a place truly sucks - and this place... OMG it's awful.  I walked in (I was meaning to go to another place nearby but they were closed) and it was so unbearably hot in there - no A/C in July and all the refrigerators and freezer units give off additional heat)  I had to walk right back out. (After taking a good look around.  Ugh.)  Not goin' back either.

I really wanted to LOVE Tir Na Nog and be "pleasantly surprised" by the tricked-out pseudo-Irish-stylized pub grub - but here's what really happened...  I went to Tir Na Nog last night as part of a private dinner party - there were about 14 of us.  We had a semi-open bar for 45 minutes - and beer on tap and house red or white wine.  I had the Pinot Grigio which I did not enjoy.  However, the barkeep (a lovely young lady) and hostess were attentive and very, very hospitable keeping everyone's glasses full.  I shoulda had a pint of Harp or Bass.  Oh well.  Next time.  Then we were ushered into a private dining area.  A choice of soup or Salad (this was - in my opinion) the best part of the meal.  The house salad was EXCELLENT - 4 stars easily - perfectly dressed fresh greens, lots of cukes & carrots and 2 perfect cherry tomatoes.  Accomanied by a basket of fresh warm bread.  I succumbed to the Irish Soda Bread with creamy butter.  Sooooo good!  A friend had the potato parmesan soup which looked awesome (and fattening as hell) and she just LOOOVED it.  But the entree failed me.  We had 4 choices - a burger (looked great), grilled salmon (looked OK - not earth shattering), a big greasy plate of delicious fish and chips (I tasted a friend's fish - which was begging for malt vinegar - a bottle quickly appeared.) - and my entree - the roast chicken.  Or should I say the dessicated chicken?    This chicken was so dry and over cooked it was just not enjoyable.  UGH.  OK - Star off for that.  Dessert redeemed TNN - with a luscious banana split - with warm caramelized banana halves.  We had a lovely time and I will return (and maybe even give 'em 4 stars next time) but no WAY would I order the roast chicken EVER again.  Oh - you should also know that prior to our dinner - a colleague and I sat on the outdoor patio (we had arrive early) and were given water in FILTHY dirty glasses.  The server hastily replaced them - but it skeeved me out quite a bit.  Glassware in general is not well washed here.

It's not as good as I'd hoped nor as bad as I'd feared. Potbelly is a fast-food sandwichs chain with decent prices and an EXTREMELY limited menu.  I had a Chicken Salad salad that was passable.  I had them add artichoke hearts and remove the dried cranberries. Though I am not thrilled I prefer it to Quizno's and Subway.  Line moved quickly and servers were well trained and fairly friendly.  (But THAT's because they are new.) I am certain that quality will diminish over time, as most fast food places (and manicure joints) do.

Right near our new house - and no lines (even on a Sunday morning). I got the exterior wash plus interior vaccum.  For $12 this was fine - and I even bought a book of 5 washes so I can come back a bunch more times.  So far, so good.  Very pleasant experience for a car wash!  Update:  I also sprang for the $99 ($105 with tax) interior detail and they did an AMAZING job.  It looks like I have a brand-new car.  LOVE IT HERE!

3.5 stars, really, but I feel generous and we had fun last night so I am giving the Limelight in Doylestown 4 stars.  The four of us stopped into the limelight - which is basically a piano bar & restaurant.  The food is Italian influenced American and all of us had veal dishes.  The iceberg lettuce salads were blah and overly dressed in a vinegary-balsamic vinaigrette.  This was made up for by the delicious Veal (or chicken) Irene - with crabmeat and pencil-thin asparagus.   My mom had a veal picatta which she enjoyed.  DH had veal parm whic he said tasted freezer burnt.  We intend to return again to give them another shot (service was good, by the way - friendly and attentive without being pushy) but if things don't go well that'll be it.  Seems like it'd be a fun bar to go hang out in, though.  Happy Hour (4-6 PM Mon - Thurs) offers $2 beers and $5 house wine.

Cutesy-diner-cum-coffee-shop.  We went on a Friday night and I had the panko-crusted mahi-mahi (Fish o' the day) and DH had the "blue plate" special.  Food was above-average and surprisingly good. Service (by cute high-school/college guys) was friendly and the under-age eye candy made me feel slightly strange.  Ask about the "Lucky Buns" for dessert.  Alas, my buns are far too large on their own - so no "Lucky Buns" for me. I'll  stick to the mahi-mahi with lovely brown & wild rice and veggies.  (FRESH green & wax beans and baby carrots.)  YUM!

Gallucio's is THE SPOT where my husband's law firm's (and many other Wilmington Lawyers) softball team meets after games.  They have an outdoor patio in the summer and a LARGE bar area.  The specialties (for us anyhow) are wings, pizza and beer. The wings are decent - not too hot - but you can ask for hot ones. The pizza is a GREASY, GREASY mess - think 3-4 napkins of blot per slice.  However, once you get passed the cheese, the sauce and crust are actually very tasty.  My 4 year old came with us one night after a game (she loves to watch her daddy play softball) and devoured 1.5 slices.  She didn't like the wings though.  In general - this is a BAR and not a kids place - so DD felt very special to be here and admired the tiny fountain on the back patio.  We had fun - and post-game - we'll be back.  Lori our server was friendly, timely and courteous.  Not a holy grail - but a decent place to gather for post-game grub.

Had a decent - and quickly served - lunch at Marathon and the place was (and always is) packed at 12:15 on a weekday.  Long line for a table!  My friend ordered her usual - the Smoked Chicken Quesadilla (next time I am trying this!) and I got a vegetable cappelini.  Would have been 4 star but my cappelini was loaded with some odd creamy sauce.  I wish I had known this so I could have had it omitted.  Tasted good - but a diet disaster.  (Kinda like a parmesan mayo - weird).  We come back from time to time but there are much better places (like Matyson and Vic Sushi Bar) for a better quality of food for lunch.  Good for expense account types.  Prices are a bit too high for the "Meh" quality.

We made a reservation that afternoon for "dining Under the Stars"  (aka chaos Out in the Heat) and were pleasantly surprised by only a 15 minute wait (others waited up to 25 minutes) for our table for 3.  Greg - one of the owners - treated us so very well - as did all the servers and bussers - especially Sarah.    Our 8 year old enjoyed the guacamole, rice & beans and chicken quesadilla kids meal.  The best bite of the night?  My husbands app - a shortrib quesedilla made with queso fresco and diced pear and onion.  Scrumptious!  I enjoyed my shortrib entree - and DH had enchiladas.  Very filling - we took some home.  No issues here at all - and much better food than the Cantina on State.  We can' wait to come back on a non-Wednesday - I bet it's even better!  Many thanks to all at Dos Gringos - they were workin' it - for a lovely evening.
Been there, done that.  This place has been around for decades. Cheesy gag gifts but also some decent condoms.  Tourist trap.

A cutesy pink & purple paradise for tweens (and younger) to get prettied up (tarted up?) and parade around on a mock runway for a birthday extravaganza.  The one in Cherry Hill is even bigger.  They have a full service salon for girls (including hair, nails - pedicure thrones, make your own lip gloss, the works) and TONS of overpriced sparkley merch for eager 8 year old fingers to grasp at.  Hold on to your wallet, kids!  (PARENTS, too)  Parties for 8 kids START at $250.

It's a Wawa - and it's there when we need it.  My DH must have his revered Marlboro lights.  Like most Wawa's - it has alot of coffee and flavored creamers.  We are glad it's here.  Alot of Wawa's are closing due to this weird economy we are in.

My little 4 year old adored Linvilla (Lynn-ville) because there are animals here and our "home orchard" (Solebury Orchard - which ROCKS by the way) does not have animals.  This is a great place for a class field trip -especially around Halloween with the Hayrides and pumpkin & Apple picking and cider making.  A great place.

As always - Louis B.'s review is spot-on!  This old-school Sears is bright, airy and packed with merchandise - but just try paying for it - we can NEVER find a cashier.  It's one of the "Anchor" stores of the now failing Grabbit 'n Run (Granite Run) Mall. A good source for clothes and shoes for my kiddo and to try on Land's end garb or return it if I make a Land's End catalog boo-boo.

OMG - so expensive.  We were shopping for a sofa and loveseat.  Sofas alone (in microfiber) started at $1400.  You get a choice of fabrics and armrest designs.  Nice sales-lady.  Lovely store - just too high for a "family room" - better for a formal living room.

Fantastic take-out food last weekend from Chin's. Note:  Now they are CLOSED MONDAYS.  Try the chicken and broccoli and Shrimp with snow peas. 10 ingredient (House special) fried rice is NOT greasy and full of goodies. Meaty. big spare-ribs and classic (doughy but tasty) steamed meat dumplings.  The only game in D-town!

I usually stop at this Wawa - on a busy stretch of Baltimore Pike - for gas.  That said, it is easy to get in and out here as long as you are "going that way".  I do not usually get food/coffee here.  Convenient for gas.
Everything is fried. Yeah, they have grillwd chicken, but served with fries.  Just ok. Not cheap, either. Limited seating.

We had terrific service on a slow Monday afternoon at 4:30 PM. Yes, my friend and I are hard core (not!) but we did enjoy some shots of makers mark and So-Co with pints of Stella Artois).  Around 6 or so the place got busy - but our service was still great and by then we were hungry so we ordered some terrific seared tuna apps ($12 each and worth it) and a mediocre and overly-salted bowl of french onion - which I had to send back.  It's a shame because I love a good french onion. This one was like eating a salt-lick.  The cute blonde female bartender was very sweet and gave us terrific customer service (and did not charge us for the salty soup).  Can't wait to come back for a full meal. This place is hoppin' at most time of the week and is packed on Summer waednesdays for "Dining under the stars".  (AKA "Chaos out in the heat")  I like this place much better than Sligo so far. A fun bar scene for middle-agers like me (ha ha!).
Similar to HoneyGrow, SweetGreen and other quick service salad/bowl joints. My basic Cobb was around $12 and tasted fine. I may be back.

Now that the Trenton Station has been renovated, America can still run on its Dunkin at the combined DD and Newsstand replete with junkfood and magazines.    While I, personally, do not partkae of the stale-tasting trucked-in caloric confectios, it is a good place to get a light ice, half-caff, french vanilla, extra milk and 2 splenda.

Much nicer than the Springfield location, but also we came on a weekday at 4:30 pm, so there was no line at the cutting table.  Definitely use the coupons and offers, as it really helps.  Lovely young lady at the front counter and a knowledgeable lady running the cutting table.  A great experience.   Clean restroom, too.

American may run on Dunkin, but Dunkin' does not run me! In the mean time - every once in a great while I get a hankerin' for a DD Iced Coffee - so if I am in Suburban station I go to this location.  Service is VERY quick and efficient (they have multiple lines) - even during the insane morning coffee rush.  I never get donuts - and very rarely food items (I actually kinda like the toast sandwiches there - but at 500 - 800 calories for BREAKFAST there is just no way!!), but I love the iced coffee - especially in the summertime.

This update and higher 4 star rating is for the IMPRESSIVE catered feast we had at my office today.  The lady who delivered it, set up the sterno, poured the raspberry (unsweetened) iced tea and catered to our every whim was terrific.  Large pans of spaghetti, meatballs, chicken parm, ravioli in a creamy-blushish-basilish sauce, 2 kinds of salad, 2 desserts.  WOW.  FOOD COMA.  And - it was all hot and very tasty.  Maggiano's - you have redeemed yourself.

Attention yuppy-families - the Froyo craze has come to the 'burbs!  (Media, PA) Service - 5 stars.  Yogurt and toppings - 4.  My 8 year old and her friend (also 8) stopped in with me for fro-yo and while the place was packed to the point of ridiculousness on Wednesday night (Dining Under the Stars aka "Chaos out in the Heat") it was peaceful and empty at 7PM on Thursday.  Do not come on Wednesdays in the summer. Come another night and oh - what a treat for the kiddies (and grown-ups who dig the froyo).  5 machines produce 10 flavors - that night 4 were non fat. The original tart - my litmus test for truly good froyo remains untried - but I did sample the coffee (non fat but who can tell?) and kiddo had Mango, peanut butter and one other (who can remember??).  The other kid had marshmallow and cookies 'n cream.  Toppings abound including the usual suspects, fresh berries, COLD whipped cream and a canister of HOT fudge.  3 Ghiradelli sauces include White chocolate, dark chocolate and caramel.  Pricey stuff when the kids get wild - we spent close to $12 for the 3 of us (And all I had was a "bowl o' whip").  Brand-spankin' new (opened about a month ago) includings a spotless restroom (YAY!) and cute hand painted Trompe-l'œil murals in progress.  Owner is "Mike" from Little Anthony's and allegedly an upstairs party-room (for pizza and froyo birthday bliss) is planned.  A welcome addition to State Street, Media.  WELL DONE!!!!! Please don't let it slip in 6 or 12 or 18 months.

Dr. Taylor was recommended to me by our pediatrician (Society Hill Pediatrics) as a place that would accept our Blue Cross Insurance.  My 4 year old had a small mole I wanted looked at . (Turned out to be, as I thought, no big whoop. Better safe than sorry.)  The administration of the office is very poor (long hold times on the phone, over booking, can't get an appt. for weeks, etc.)  - which is why I am giving her 3 stars.  Susan herself was a 4-5 star doctor though and was patient with my little one and gave (what I perceived to be)  sound advice.  Dr. Taylor was very, very nice during the 2-3 minutes she spend with us.  (Due to the rushed and over booked appointments of the aforementioned administration of the practice, Dr. T. had precious little time to spend with us.  This, alas, is typical, in the medical community.  Damned insurance!!)  Anyhow, I am glad we were able to see her and hope that she will be available should we need her services again.   P.S.  She has a skin care line on sale at Sephora.

A solid choice in this part of Media - and very convenient to Rt 1. Full bar - and pricey but good cocktails and many beers. A vast take out and catering section.  Don't miss their signature pistachio crusted chicken tender - especially if they have just made a fresh batch.  They really are delicious.  Salads are good too.

Wow - I remember when this used to be Tilly's. What an improvement.  Great spot for a diner-style breakfast or a basic lunch sandwich. I usually go for breakfast.  You can get home fries or a hash brown pattie.  Decent hot coffee, too. Not super expensive.  A good choice.

The 5 stars goes to John for his incredible customer service. He personally delivered meals for my and an office mate to our office up toward Claymont, all the way from New Castle.  My friend had the Penne Florentine with Chicken and I had a delicous Veal Platter with a side of fettucine.  Everything arrived piping hot.  (Unfortunately, so did my side salad - I put it in the fridge at work to re-chill.)  Wish they weren't so far away.  Inexpensive, SIMPLE (not 5 star fancy, but 5 star tasty), classic Italian/American faves.

My little girl enjoyed her 6th birthday so much that we are having her7th here as well later this year.  Meanwhile, DH, DD and I bowl a quick couple of games today and ordered a single order of tater tots.  A fun afternoon - and even worth the 25 minute wait for a lane.  I forgot that Saturdays can be a zoo here.  Best to come at a quieter time.  Good clean family fun (and mama can even get a cocktail).

My source for specialty food products - especially the fabulous selection of balsamic vinegar, a good cheese counter and swanky (pricey) prepared foods that taste as great as they look.  A small coffee is $1.99 - so not too bad. Fresh OJ for $2.99 in the AM with a carb-laden pastry?  (Try the flaky cinnamon stick - like dessert for breakfast). Catering, too!  Lines can get long but the move quickly.  Thank goodness we have Di Bruno's.
Bought some Hagar slacks for my elderly father - it's all he will wear any more.  No issues.

We had a luncheon here in one of the private banquet rooms for about 30 people.  The food and service were bith excellent.  Green salad, rolls and butter, a basic penne marinara pasta course followed by a choice of 2 entrees. Crab cake or Chicken Marsala.  Both were delicious.   Super creamy (was it homemade?) Vanilla ice cream fir dessert. Sounds like no big whoop,  but it was soooooo rich tasting. I put some in my coffee. Very good coffee, too.  Rob (server) and the young lady at the door were very kind.  I would definitely come here for dinner or plan a special event here. Plus they have their own parking lot.  Great!
Cody Y. says it perfectly - the pumps are at an angle and it is crazy-busy at rush hour. I really, really needed gas, so I was grateful to find it.
Stopped in here on a whim and ordered 1 pork belly Bao (very good) and a teriyaki Tofu Bento (Just OK, fried, too many carbs).  Good but not amazing.

Billie Jo is one of my favorite estheticians EVER and I, in fact, followed her here from another spa.  This place is so swanky - very nice.  A great relaxation room and a well thought out floor plan.    A facial here can run $149 and up (ouch) but it is wonderful to have Billie Jo work on you. They also offer a whole menu of med-spa services including laser treatments (hair removal, collagen rejeuvenation, etc.), fillers (Botox, Restylane, Juvaderm) and SculpSure (not Cool Sculpt - the other one.).  Packages run in the THOUSANDS so bring money.  Love it so far - but man, I guess I am in the wrong demographic. A teen facial (18 & under) is $99.  Lucky kids!

The staff here is friendly and wonderful - and although I can't do 100% of my "regular" grocery shopping here, I do come by a few times each month for "fun foods" and frozen treats.  They have some great lunch options, too, like salads, pomegranate arils and meats in the refrigerated case.  Unique products and tasty foods that are quick to prepare. Also a good source of holiday gifts for the food lover in your life.

I am attempting to review the Kohl's department store on route 611 in Warrington.  (Next door to Home Goods & in a strip mall.)  I hope this is the same place.  In any case, kohl's is the home of "disposable clothing" and also a good place to get inexpensive housewares and gift items.  The quality is much better than Kmart or WalMart - and some may argue that the clothing is nicer than arget - to me the quality and price points are about the same.  The nice thing I like about Kohl's is the incredilble deal I get on baby/kids clothes and shoes.   scored fabulous sneakers for my daughter at a fraction of retail price.  DFor myself - I am not a huge fan - but i have slowly started buying a few shirts & sweaters here due to my new budgetary restrictions on shopping.  Kohl's has been great also for my husband who bought some semi-precious jewelry (10 K gold and Topaz) for him mother (my mother in law) for Mother's day.  It was a bargain for sure.   I would not purchase "fine" jewelry here - but when them have sales - they realloffer deep discounts ant the jewelry department is always worth a look!

Well, now that Hong Kong Jack's is dead and gone - Chin's is THE only game in town for Classic Chinese-American.  (There are 2 small take out joints that keep changinbg hands down 611 toward Warrington).  Chin's offers perfectly safe Cantonese and a few Szechuan dishes - and all the classics you'd expect.  Service is fast (especially if you call in a take out order and then drive over to pick it up) and friendly.  Our only gripe?  They don't open until 2 PM on Sundays - so lunch on a Sunday is out.

OK, so this review is for the sales portion - we have yet to take delivery on our newly-purchased leather sofa.  Price was right, sale rep Alan was terrific and Reggie at the check-out was efficient.  Will update review once the couch arrives in about a month.  Hopefully not 4 months (some furniture stores have a 12 to 16 week wait time).  So far, so good.  Go during a sale!

I stick with the salads here, although a coworker gets the stir fry and likes it.  The Cobb Salad (I make a few changes to it using the touch screen ordering sustem) is a bit steep ($12 when I get through with it.) but the portion is immense and I can eat some at 3 or 4 PM if I get hungry again that day.  It will not keep well the next day.  The staff is underpaid and disinterested which I fear will cause long term service issues.  The 2 guys at the wok - working very hard - were clearly ticked off about something.  Then, the oven started to smoke.  Crispy-drama at lunch.

#ServiceStarShoutOut  Mike Cangemi has been my go-to plumber for almost a decade. He is fair, honest and does quality work. He has saved us in so many ways from a kitchen sink issue to a leaky old shower.  He even swapped out my shower head when I moved - and recommended exactly which shower head to get for my budget (There are hundreds out there.)  Can't say enough GREAT things about Cangemi and his crew.  #ServiceStarShoutOut
Came here many years ago to get a (cold) six pack. A nice selection of wines, liquors and beer by the case or six-pack.  Young guys running the counter. No issues.

OMG, Dunkin' has taking over the universe - including Suburban Station with multiple outposts.  That said I never eat donuts, but I do occasionally succumb to temptation and get a hot or ice latte as is seasonally appropriate.  Passero's in Suburban has far superior coffee and food but is also more money - natch.  It is still cheaper that Charbucks (FiveBucks?) and they have oodles of flavors/syrups (I pass on those.)  For a "regular" cuppa joe - Dunkin or Wawa are my go-to's. Thanks for being here when we need you, Dunkin. You are taking over the WORLD.

This is not a juice bar - it is a smoothie/sugar laden. fruity treat place that your kids will like.  Is it good for you?  Not really.  Large sizes and decent prices - but way too high of a sugar content in most of the drinks.  Bright cheery location and friendly service.

Something has slipped at Chin's, I'm afraid. And D-town has precious few Chinese places any more, so we are still using Chin's as our go-to take out spot.  The pepper steak with onions was mostly onions and peppers with very little (gristly) steak and drowning in salty brown sauce.    Nope.  The hot & sour soup was not very hot, but quite sour (like 2% acetic acid sour).  Nope.  Thankfully the Shrimp with Snow peas was excellent (5 shrimp in a small order) and out 9 year old devoured the sesame (deep fried white meat chunks of) chicken.  Fried pork dumplings are doughy but satisfying.  Classic Chinese take-out (The eat-in dining room is rather dark) but they need to up their game.  Please!!!  We need you!

Still amazing food at a great (cash only) price - but you gotta go before the 12 noon rush.  We were there at 11:30 on a Monday and the place was still busy - just not crazy yet.  I got a stuffed grapeleaf platter ($9.50) and my friend got a fried egplant sandwich (I love Mama's eggplant but I just wasn't feelin' the fried today.)  The condiments on the side bar are great - don't skip those!  Cool folks runnin' the show and keepin' the line moving. Great fun and food at Mama's! And they always play great music in the background (if you can hear it over the crowds).

Fantastic Thai - the same stuff as the now-closed Thai Chef in Philly. Tom Kha (Coconut) soup is divine and not too thick and not too watery. DUCK Pad Thai was a bit sweet but the noodles and duck were both perfectly cooked.  (MEAT of choice) - we opted for pork - in Thai Basil sauce was very mildly spicy (tolerable for even a light-weight).  Delish.  Casual, friendly service.

This Starbucks has a drive thru which is great - however there is nearly always a significant line.  Also if you come after 11 or 12 noon they are sold out of many "breakfast" type items so keep that in mind.   No real issues.  Keep in mind I have never set foot inside this particular store - but I have used the drive thru 3 or 4 times.  Convenient for me when I am heading North on 202.
I had a good experience browse-shopping here - but the prices were cost prohibitive.  Oh well.

While we have gotten some good deals at Best Buy (the chain) - this particular store is NOT fun to shop in.    Crowded, often Crazy lines, sub-par customer service. But - you can snag a Flat-screen TV, Smartphone, Digital Camera or laptop for a very cheap price here when ther are running a deal.  AVOID at Xmas time.

2 or 3.  I will be generous and give them 3 stars, as my little girl really enjoyed her short-stack of chocolate chip pancakes.  This is diner food - but alas, not at its finest.  My husband ordered a Chicken wrap with Ranch dressing and they got it wrong and gave him a Buffalo Chicken ranch with Blue cheese dressing, which he does not like.  The server was pleasant enough and the man (owner??) at the cashier desk was lovely, too, but the food just isn't that great.  They have an "odd" salad bar with some interesting looking prepared salads on it.    The french onion soup was good - but a bit on the salty side - and they used packaged coutons in it, not a bread "crouton".  We were in a jam and needed to eat - so this served the purpose, but I would not rush back here.

I am not a big pizza eater, but I lknow Pina's stuff is fresh and good.  Try to order a whole pie and eat it there for the freshest and best atsting pie.  Sometimes the slices on the counter get a little old and dried out.  My 3 year old loves it here - and I'll usually run next door to saladworks and get something for myself.  The staff at Pina's has been very gracious to us.

We came during an off-peak time and the park rangers were so kind to my then 5 year old who brought her easel and pencils - they let her sit and sketch - which I bet is unusual.  There was practically no line on the random weekday morning when we visited.

What?!?  Nobody yelped DVC yet?  Wow.  Where do I start?  Delaware Valley College is part of the backbone of the Doylestown/New Britain area.  In the 1800 it was started as a "Farm School" later re-named as an agricultural school, and it still overs terrific program in farming, equine and bovine studies, horticultre and floricultre.  Each year "A-Day" (Agriculture Day) is where the Aggies can flaunt their stuff. Everything from campus-grown produce to honey is displayed. As kids we could not WAIT for A Day each year.  The school now focuses on teaching and educatioon certificate and degree programs.  Its a good school.  (Not Ivy League, of course - but a good, solid college.)  For retired citizens (my Mom included) there are numerous non-credit courses and programs.  Foreign Languages, Art, Music and lots to choose from.  If you live near DVC, try to take advantage of all it has to over the community.  It is a great local resource.  (High school kids - you may be able to borrow books from the DVC library.)

We were dragged in here by our uber-artistic 7 year old and while there we got 4 pairs of fabric scissors (for $5 - SWEET), some fabric, embroidery thread, trimmings and a make-yyour-own "American Girl" style doll dress.  We though we were done when the "demo lady" (sweet as could be) who was cleaning up a beading workshop announced that they had free "make your own" head bands.  So we made some. Free.  Time killer - and fun for the kiddos.  You can also rent the party roon ($50) to have a crafts party for up to 15 kids. We'll think about this.  Just walking in here makes me feel so very "soccer mom".

We purchased our living room couch from R & F about 2-3 years ago after seeing it advertised on sale (and after shopping at nearby LazyBoy, Ethan Allen and other mid priced chain furniture stores.)  Furniture is expensive, and quality is not what it once was, but I am happy to say that our couch (which was delivered as promised and on time a few days after we ordered it - hooray!) is standing up to the major abuse our elderly pug and young child are giving it.  I just called the store today to see about replacement seat cushions.  I am hoping to get a favorable reply.  Customer service has been excellent.  (And for a cheap $600 couch - that says alot.)  This is not FINE nor designer furniture - but for day to day, middle class, family living - R&F is working for us.

Di Bruno's is kinda like the Philly version of Citarella or Agata & Valentna in NYC.  It's a gourmet & specialty food market with a vast catering arm and now an upstairs lunch-only weatery.  It also has a cafe/espresso bar with a small selection of artesenal gelato.  The pastries are good - but pricey.  The cheese counter is a good place to investigate a world of cheeses.  (I, of course, hjave been forever spoiled by Murray's in NYC -but this is a good Philly alternative.)  They also carry sushi, spreads, and pricey prepared dishes. Fresh produce is a plus - but the selection is limited.

Mike came to give us an estimate on several small plumbing jobs.  So far we had his team complete one of the jobs (a toilet repair).  We hope to work with them for all of our residential plumbing needs.

I contacted Pitruco about hosting a private event.  They were responsive and wonderful.  While my budget won't support it right now ($750 minimum for about 50 people at $15 per person), I will definitely consider them for future events. (The event I am having is for about 20-25 people only.)  If you are having a big graduation party or family reunion, it'd be so cool to have the Pitruco truck roll up and crank out fresh pies for your guests.  A gal's gotta dream... Maybe some day Pitruco will come rolling up to MY driveway.

The Chesterbrook Shopping Center is depressing with many vacant stores.  Aside from Diane's Deli (a hole-in-the-wall with dated decor but inexpensive and HUGE portions of classic deli), I only come here for Rite Aid.  And even then - only in a pinch.  I much prefer the Walgreens in Paoli (or maybe the CVS - but this Rote Aid is better than the Paoli CVS which has awful service and always has a line at check out even when the store is empty.  How is that even possible???  Anyhow this is your basic Rite Aid.  Pharmacy, OTC items, Candy/Snack & Beverages, Cosmetics.  No issues.  The whole area is being re-modeled (it sorely needs it) and there is a HUGE 2 year construction underway so parking will be a bit of a mess.  Be patient.  I bet the future will look brighter!

Ah, the ye olde Farm House Tavern - where (back - way back - in the day) one could get served alcohol underage.  Alas, those no-carding days are long over.  But the farmhouse seres decent bar food (it is by no means a gastro pub, and the regulars like it that way).  I preferred it here to Finney's back in the day - and often got a nice sandwich and fries to go with my beers or vodka-cranberry.  A good, old-time bar-lover's bar.

As a community resource for non-credit courses it seems just fine. I have never enrolled here in a degree program but many of my colleagues' kids attend here and some adult learners also.  The vast parking lots are STILL not enough parking (Imagine??).  There is a small café/coffee bar in the main building that serves a decent latte.  So far, I am still exploring all that DCCC has to offer.

First of all - I think this placed is now OWNED by La Tolteca - because that is how my credit card went through.  (Said Casa Tropical on paper receipt but on computer said La Tolteca).  Very dark/old school interior. Place was dead-empty for lunch on a summer Wednesday - even so my single order of mediocre ceviche took a while to be served.  Chips and salsa are fresh and delicious. Not the greatest food - and oh, how I wanted to love it here.  Service was very good - nice young man.  I will not be rushing back here - which is a shame as I love me some good Maduros.

The average of these reviews is spot on - about 3.25 - 3.5 stars. Please bear in mind that today was my first EVER experience with Positano Coast and I went for a luncheon as part of a group of 64 people.  We had a set menu - and service was quite good considering the difficult layout of the section of the room (PC does alot of large parties).  The meal cost $30 some dollars including tax 'n tip. Included were a salad (very boring - lightly dressed), entree choice (Branzino or Eggplant Parm served with angel hair pasta or a Penne Priamvera), canolli and coffee/tea/soft drinks.  The eggplant was very tasty and the food was nice and hot.  Would I rush back?  Not really - but i would consider this place for a party (150 is easily done here - and you can rent the place out for a group of 300).  A solid place with decent service (Shout out to Perry - our server who worked her a$$ off!) and good, tasty (nothing spectacular) Iltalinaish/Mediterraneanish fare.

So disappointed with our take-out order from Chin's - which is pretty much the "only game in town" for D-town Chinese nowadays.  The spare-ribs were burnt and just plain bad - we threw one away (You get 5 for $8/95.  The pepper steak with onion was loaded with onion and very little beef - although what was there tasted great.   The best part was the house special fried rice - made to order and very good but man, everything else was not great this time.  What happened? Chin's is our go-to and we'd hate to stop going.

This place is adorable but the prices are obscene.  For the price of my latte it had better be exceptional.  It was good - but in no way mind blowing.  For a similar price (high) I can get a La Colombe. Better yet I can get a small Au Lait here and it tastes better to me.  On par with Char-bucks, but slower service. Very friendly male barista.  Pastries looked wonderful but again - too pricey and I can't eat carbs. The almond croissant and almond biscotti (I sense a theme here) look so great.  Service was good - but a bit slower - it is a hand-crafted kinda place.

Finney's is a D-town original - and one of the few liquor licenses in town. I "dive-bar" feel with lots of regulars some of which have been coming here for 30 - 40 years.  Brings back so many memories.

Came here during the Covid19 crisis looking for paper products and they had some!!!  Alice at the front counter was cheerful and friendly amidst all the chaos.  This CVS is well managed, clean and well-run.  Great!

Stopped here on an early Saturday morning, with "mixed precipitation"  to use the restrooms and grab a Starbucks.  There was NO LINE at Starbucks - wow!  Usually there is a huge one.  Very pleasantly surprised with the Starbucks.  Bathrooms need a touch up - a few toilets had urine in them - unflushed.  Ick.

Cold Hiyashi Ramen (regular with Cha su or Vegetarian) is a summertime treat. I get mine with the sauce/dressing on the side.  Blissful carbo-loading.  I got there at 11:45 just before the lunch rush hit and got in and out with my take out bag.  Sweet!

3 or 4 stars depending on what you get.  Yes, you can eat there but there is zero atmosphere - so we get it as take-out.  My vegan kid likes the vegetable lo mein (no egg).  A little greasy, inexpensive - reminds us of the take out Chinese we used to get in Brooklyn.  No frills, no issues.  Is it the most amazing food ever?  Heck no, but it is cheap, fast and tasty and once in a while we will come here.  Counter-man/Manager is always kind to us - never had a problem with service.

Hornberger's delivered a lovely two-tiered mini wedding cake to our office for a wedding shower.  The buttercream icing and sugar flowers over a tasty (dense) vanilla (pound?) cake was delicious and gorgeous.  Easily fed 20 people (4 inch round over a 6 or 8 inch??).

Had a great take-out meal from Chin's on Monther's Day (did not want to deal with crowds at restaurants).  Beef and brocolli, chicken with cashew nuts, spare ribs, one egg roll (for my old-school relatives), pepper steak, house-special fried rice (really good) and chicken lo mein.  All were hot and fresh (They open at 2 on Sundays) and better than last time.  Tip:  ask for "light on the sauce" to mitigate the grease factor.

3.5 stars - I will be gracious and round up to 3. Creed's is reminiscent of a by-gone era.  (Seafood Shanty?  Conti's Cross Keys Inn?)  It definitely has an old-school vibe in décor, service and food.  The food itself was actually excellent. We went for lunch and it was around $45 including tax and tip for 2 (no booze, no desserts). I had a shrimp cobb salad and the ingredients were all super fresh and tasty.   My friend had a very nice looking (but small) crab cake over spinach.  Service was attentive and fine - but this is NOT a place to go if you are in a rush. Leisurely.  Sedate.  Safe.  (No nouveau cuisne here, no fusion)  A good place to take your parents - or rather have them take YOU.  Bring money!

Other than the extremely cramped seating (this place is hoppin' at lunch time), our party of 4 enjoyed our food very much.  I had the Burmese Crunch salad with tofu and it was delicious. 2 of my friends had it with grilled chicken.  A 4th colleague had the curry with large grilled shrimp which looked amazing.  We'll be back for sure.  I would like to try the wings.   Much improved over the Chinese place that used to occupy this spot.
Nice flowers for my birthday via internet ordering. They misdelivered me the wrong arrangement but quickly fixed the issue.  Lovely selection of fresh flowers in a classic glass vase.
Easy in and out here on most days - compared to other PennDOT locations. License renewals, testing, permits, etc.

I finally became a member in 2010 and now live much closer so I visit much more often.  The fireworks shows andconcerts are expensive - even formembers, but oh - the gardens and conservatory - every season is great. Spring with it's bulbs, orchid days and tulips, Summer with so much abundant flora and water lily\ies, Autmun with its crisp folliage, and Winter (the holidays here are amazing.)   LOVE IT HERE.

Located inside the Booth's Corners Farmers Market (Hours are limited to Fridays and Saturdays except during holidays and special events when there could be more hours).  Grecian Delights is an inexpensive and absolutely DELICIOUS counter-style restaurant.  Nikki - our server - was terrific and the gyros, grilled chicken, salad, tzatziki and especially that Avgolemono soup were all Yia-Yia approved.  I can't wait to dine here again - or get a $20 gyro special (with a big salad and baklava) to go for a quick dinner for 2.  I LOVE IT.

Not a happy camper. Went to El Rey at 4:40 PM - was told no dinner until 5 - but we could have a drink and chips & salsa ($3.50 - very tasty).  I ordered what i always get - the classic margarita.  Ugh - it was so bitter. I asked them to re-make it, explaining that it tasted unusually bitter.  they remade it - and it tasted the same - dreadful.  They remade it a second time and it was good - but not the smooth, limey-sweetness that it usually is.  So I drank it.  I got fish tacos ($9 for 3 tacos) and they are the exact same tiny tacos you get for $1 during happy hour - no rice or beans or anything with them.  So I got a side order of corn on the cob (good stuff!).  I am sticking to happy hour here from how on. My husband will stick with Qdoba.

Super yum!!!  There used to be 2 KC's but I think the one on 11th Street has closed. Thank goodness the 10th Street location still purveys oodles of freshly baked breads, cakes and sugar-y confections.  The fried donuts and buns are so good - and when you get them while they're hot - Oh what a treat.  I vote each election at the nearby Chinatown fire department - so I pass buy KC's on my way to work after I vote.  I always get a croissant (Chinese style) or a sponge cake "cone" wrapped in paper.  It is decadent to munch away on such a treat while riding the SEPTA bus west on Market.  And all for under $1.50!!!!  Sign me up!

For $11.95 the lunch special - includes drink and choice of Tom Yum soup, Dumplings, Egg Roll (fried) or Fresh Spring Roll (Summer Roll - not fried) is a very nice meal.  I have tried the Bun (Rice Vermicelli also, Masuman Curry (very good) and Tofu with Eggplant.  A little greasy and sweet - but solid Viet/Thai especially for out here. The Philly area's Thai choices are lacking.  This place is Vietnamese with a few Thai dishes also.  So far I have come 3 times for lunch - and that is after visiting Thai Orchid nearby twice.  This place - for me anyway - is better.
Average Acme at best. Kinda small.  Average prices - some items seem high and others lower than Giant.  Lines move slowly, but checkers are friendly (and chatty - thus line takes time).

Still love it and still a member.  I now buy 2 year memberships at a time (slightly cheaper).  Even with 10% off the cafe and gift shops are pricey - but all in all we just LOVE it there so much.  You must come during all seasons. Spring (orchids/bulbs) Summer, Fall (Mums) and CHRISTMAS is the best!  Note:  Main fountains CLOSED until 2017 for a MAJOR (and so needed) modernization.

I love Longwood Gardens.  (The do not accept a discount for PHS members though - Pennsylvania Horticultural Society).  So fork over the admission fee and wear comfy shoes.  It's an ALL DAY affair.  There is so much to see here - each season is special.  (Winter has a wonderful display in the conservatory.)  Spring is a must!  I love to wander the grounds when all my favorite bulb flowers bloom (tulips, hyacinths, daffodils, etc.)  What a national treasure.

We are members now at Longwood - as it is cost effective after 3 visits and we plan to visit 3 or 4 times this year.  The Christmas spectacular is truly amazing - but plan ahead and reserve early or you will see your favorite dates/times sold out.  Bring your own water/beverages and snaks as a hotdog is $6.50 here and the "good" food is even higher.  The over cans of beer for $8 - $10 each.  Whoa!   The foliage, Silver Garden, Pierce Woods, Meadow and Flower Garden walk are not to be missed.  We just love it here.  Wish they offered reciprocity with PHS and other garden clubs, but they don't.  They don't need to.  Bring money for the garden shop, too.

No good.  The dumplings are doughy and not good at all. Get your dumplings from Sang Kee right down the aisle.  We came here at 5:45 PM (RTM closes at 6 PM) and Sang Kee had already pretty much shut down and the little one HAD to have dumplings and even she said, "Mommy, I don;t like these.  I want Sang Kee."  Smart 5 year old.  That said, the (female) owner was really, really nice to us. It's a shame the dumplings were so heavy & mystery-meatish.

Much better to come here in the winter for some warm comfort food. I tried the chicken salad with green apples - very good but just a tad too mayonaise-y for my picky palate.  Next time I'll go back to the 1/4 chicken platter.  The counter gal who has been there from the start is amazing.  She is bright and friendly and works her tail off!  Friends all had 1/4 chicken meals - some had light, some had dark - all enjoyed.  Mac 'n cheese, corn muffins, kale chips, beet salad, collard greens and mashed sweet potatoes were enjoyed by all.  LOVE IT HERE.  (Boston Market for Yuppies?)

Too costly but a nice facility with great classes (like Zumba, Water Aerobics and Karate). Excellent pools and swimming instruction.  9 year old found the summer camp way too boring so we don't go any more.

Soooo cheap and very good cakes and sponge cones.  My daughter loves it here.  They also have numerous flavors of bubble tea.  We have come here 3 times now for the delcious cream cake, shrimp dumplings (fried and greasy - but pretty tasty, too.) and superb egg custard tarts.  2 tiny tables to sit at - so get it to go if you can.  DD & I tend to sit and people watch.  She just LOVES it here and the nice ladies behind the counter love her.  Very reasonble prices, too.  They treat my blue-eyed, sandy haired 4 year old like a rock star.  She's give it 6 stars!

Big shout out to Tina who treated my 7 year old so very well! My little one loves the chicken here (the two of us get the $12 1/2 chicken meal which is way more than we can eat.  The corn mini-muffins were a huge hit with DD.  I love the Kale Chips (DD not as much.).  Plus they now serve Reed's Ginger Brew.  I love this place more and more - and when I want roast chicken - this is where I come.

Another delectable lunch at Matyson - house made gnocchi were light and pillowy in a light garlic and wine sauce with fresh summer veggies.  Smoked Trout on black bread is always a hit.  Can't miss at Mat-y-son.
My little daughter & I stopped in here a few times for ice cream treats (they ahve alot of snacks for sale).  Nice to have them around - even if they close at 5 PM.

Saladworks is a hit or miss thing and varies location by rustied-lettuce location.  The one in my building (Commerce Square - was poorly managed and gross and went out of biz in 2007.)  If you get it on a clean day - and the lettuce looks fresh and green - go foor it, otherwise, skip the salad and stick to pasta or maybe a wrap.   I don't like the paninis at all - too "bread-y".  The one at 18 & Market is OK, too.

I was a Big OS catalog customer (website) back in tha day, so I went in to see if I could get some bone-in 14 oz. Strips.  There were 2 other customers and a delivery man ion the store all waiting to be helpeed.  So I browsed around a bit and left. Meh customer Service. I will order online if I need help quickly.  This location is gonna die. Horrible Parking lot.

Today (a Wednesday) was my first go at the East Norriton Salad Works. Since the mad rush was over on Tuesday (Every Tuesday all "standard" salads are $6.99), there was hardly any line on a Wednesday.  I got a "pick 2" combo - 1/2 an avocado BLT and a 1/2 salad. Everything was fine and even the lettuce mix was fresh.  No issues so far. I will be back - but NOT on a Tuesday.  It's worth 2 extra dollars to NOT wait in that line. I may experiment with online pick-up ordering.  But I fear the Tuesday crowds.

We stopped by Scoop on the day after "Hurricane Irene" when lots of places were closed.  The little one wanted fro yo - but Sweet Ending was closed as well.  So I got her a small ($3.00) choc & van froyo topped (.75 cents) with mini m & m's (they were out of kit kats).  Not awesome and not awful - but the LINE was so long (likely because they were one of the only retail stores open and they were also under staffed).  In future we will stick to Sweet Ending (we love capogiro but it's pricey and they don;t have toppings and my kiddo's just gotta have her toppings).  This place is A-OK but not spectacular.

OK, maybe 3.5 stars - but not 4.  I just was not impressed with the food.  We had several small plates - and a really bitter greens-based salad.  Also a dessert panini which sounded much better on paper than it actually tasted.  The cheese selection was nice.  The service was fine, if a bit dis-interested,  and the decor and vibe call for a 4 or 5 star rating but the food was not worth the price, and not especially memorable.  This location I like better than the 11th Street location.  Not sure why - but we had a better time here.

I am actually reviewing the new InnerVision at 1700 Sansom. I assume it's the same owners - but not sure.  Anyhow, even though I elected to pruchase my glasses elsewhere - I really liked the selection of fine frames and the GREAT customer service I received from Micha.  The frames are gorgeous - and of course pricey.  I would recommend looking here - but I have to say I found 1 place I liked better - and I wound up purchasing there.

I am very thankful to Kennedy Food Garden for being there over the years. Rebecca at the front counter and the deli guys are friendly and service oriented.  The shrimp salad is still a fave as well as the kasha and potato knishes.  I can get milk, juice and sliced fruits and veggies here in a pinch.  They are my winter savior!

It's not bad - I think the same people run it as ran my old cafeteria at JP Morgan (not Aramark - but some other big conglomerate food service thing).  They have a salad bar, a "Jazzman's Coffee" bar, a pizza station, grill (with greasy burgers and junk food), a hot entree (today it was fried fish), and several grab 'n go foods like salads, SUSHI (from Bumblefish - not bad!) and parfaits.  It a pinch - it's great as I live nearby.  Open from 6:30 AM - 7 Pm but by 6 PM the pickin's get slim - it's better for lunch.

We love you, Mai!  And we love the treats from BTH - especially the 70 cent egg tarts and $1 chocolate croissants.  The sponge cake treats in the fridge are a fave for our 7 year old.  Still some of the best tapioca pearl tea in the city!  BTH rocks!

Finally tried the pricey 1906 restaurant and had 5 star service (and 4 star fare) on the lovely outdoor deck.  Salmon was tender ($26 for lunch!!!!) and Burger ($18!!!) on a Brioche bun with sauteed mushrooms and onions was very good also.  Super pricey (even with 10% off for members) but a fun and special experience. Great for Mother's Day (come a different day and celebrate your mom) or a proposal dinner.
