Friendly staff convinced me to buy the $5 per year club card to get lower prices - a decent investment if you shop there as often as I do.  Professionals (bring your license) get an even better deal.  Combs, brushes, flat irons and nail supplies.  Skin care selection is limited.

Nope. Unimpressed.  Yes, it's inexpensive but you are MUCH better off going 1/2 a block down the street to the Asian (Vietnamese) place or across the street for Oasis Lebanese.  We stopped in because the Vietnamese place was closed and we figured we'd check it out.  Both of us had $9.95 bento lunch boxes and mine (Salmon Basil) was not good at all.  Frozen and fishy tasting salmon that was DEEP FRIED (Ick.).  I ate the other stuff.   Miso soup was fine.  $2.00 up charge for Thai Chicken Coconut soup insteadof Miso (also good).  Not a fan.  Sorry.

Everything tastes better on somebody else's dime...  Meanwhile I attended a "heavy app" holiday party at JG last night. Nathan - who took care of our raucous party of 22, kept the drinks flowing and I tried the FABULOUS Butterscotch (supposed to have a bit of bourbon in there??) Latte.  Dessert in a cup.  Beef sliders were cooked very rare - which I did not mind, but others complained. Charcuterie and cheeses (and heavenly fig jam) were artfuly displayed and delicious to eat.  Mini crab cakes (puffs) were fried and fattening.  Flatbread with mushrooms, truffle oil and fried ege was a BIG hit.  Try the beers here, too!  My faith has been restored.  Although I still don;t like paying $30 - $0 for lunch - I just might come here again pretty soon.  Gotta get me another of those $6 calorie-bomb lattes.

Had a much better time now that my little one is 6.5. She was too freaked out by the Spies & Saboteurs Exhibit (there is a KKK part that she found very disturbing)  But she LOVED the 17 minute show in the Kimmel Theater (Freedom Rising) and the "carpet game" for kids on the top floor.  We became members through Groupon, so from now through next June we'll be living there.

They had 1 of the 2 obscure items I needed (wish they carried both).  Helpful staff - friendly service.  No issues here.  Please stock "blue denim" doggie diapers.  My elderly pug needs then (we currently can only get the at MonsterPets in South Philly).

Not nearly as nice as the Union League - but the food is good and maybe even better here - plus you have those gorgeous views of the city.  For a holiday party ofr networking event - it's a great spot.  As long as someone else is paying - I'll be there.  But there is NO WAY I'd join as a a member.  Too much money.  They easily accomodate large or small groups and have some meeting rooms that are cozy for the small ones.

Even though I much prefer to shop at the Giant in Aston (or Whole Foods in Glen Mills when time and budget permits), I stopped in here and customer service was so, so, so much better than at Giant.  I bought a jar of jam for my dad and it turned out not to be the right kind. They took it back 5 days later (unopened, of course) with no receipt. This is a rare occurrence and I was hoping they would not give me any problems.  I am very pleased.

Nearly 5 stars - what a great place to sit and have a drink (try the house made ginger ale - so perfectly refreshing) or a franglo-pub lunch.  The house burger is quite good and comes with frites AND a nice green salad.  A good place to meet a client, conduct an interview or just hang out.

I really love Harvest - but during peak times the acoustics are LOUD!!!!! Our server Ian was terrific and explained the menu and dishes well.  My husband enjoyed the shortrib entree.  Potstickers ($10 - ouch!) were fried and IMO over cooked.  I enjoyed the quinoa salad - and a small was plenty for me ($6) and loved the shrimp (2 large deliciously seasoned shrimp) crabmeat cocktail served over gazpacho and a thick slice of yellow tomato.  Love it here - and can't wait to come back. A little pricey but great for a date or a family meal.

This 3 star rating is for the Deli Department.  I give a MUCH higher rating to the produce manager.  I had a part and ordered (well in advance) a $59.99 cold cut tray and a $19.99 Chocolate-dipped strawberry tray (excellent and a great value).  There were many issues with both quality and presentation of the (medium sized) tray. I spoke to the manager (LeighAnn) who was gracious and promptly refunded my $60 plus gave me a $10 gift card.  (Very nice to do that!).  5 star customer service - but I would have preferred a 5 star party tray. Please "step up your game", Acme Deli.    I am not likely to order trays from here again.  P.S.  We are still very, very grateful to this Acme for supporting our girl scout troop.  I would like to be supportive of Acme as well.  Sure wish that party tray had been good.

OMG - it's still here! This is the Taco Bell from my childhood - and it has been renovated a couple of times since the '90's.  Not a big T-bell fan - but in a pinch, it's here. I avoid fast food whenever possible.

This is such a cutesy place to shop for everything your pooch would ever need.  My daughter loves to browse in here, too.  I have a sweet 12 year old male puggy - and they are so nice to us.  Great advice on pet care, too.
Very bondage oriented but a good selection of toys and adult enhancement items in a no-pressure environment.  Fun to browse.

This place is kinda depressing. Server, Rae, was nice - and attentive. Place was nearly empty on a Monday night.  Salad that came with the meal was pretty bad - lettuce was overly wet, cut into tiny pieces and starting to rust (turn brown).  The 2 slices of tomato and 2 sliced of un-peeled waxy cucumber were at least edible.  The supposedly home-made russian dressing was just awful (thank goodness I ordered it on the side).  The entree itself was OK - veal francese (I know!  What possessed me -next time, if there is a next time as I am not prone to return, I will get a gyro or pancakes or something "easier").  Surprisingly good.  3 stars even - but the salad skeeved me.  Ugly interior - but at least they seem to be re-doing the ladies room.  As I said, I will not rush back.  I much prefer the court diner.

Food was fine - 4 star and service a little slow (2 star) by seasoned waitresses, like Eleanor. Decor?  Ick.  Like an old cafeteria.  Decent for burgers or sandwiches.  I enjoyed my onion rings and patty melt but our 10 year old did not like the Chicken Caesar salad at all.  BLT looked great - at $4.99.  Decent prices.

Horrid parking lot when this place is busy. Otherwise it's fine.  I was able to get the liquor I needed in a pinch for a Memorial Day party.  Usually we try to avoid PA and shop at Total Wine & More in Delaware.  Don;t get me started on PA's antiquated liquor laws.  I feel awful for bar owners, too!

A nice place to hang out and eat/drink/shop.  They've done a nice job with it.  I wonder though, if you live in one of those big, new buildings, does the noise level in the summer (especially on Saturday nights) preclude a quiet family life??  Just sayin'...

Visited 3 times in the summer of 2016 -Liberty Bell, NMAJH, Constitution Center, City Tavern and many local restaurants, cafes and shops.  I am proud and glad to live in the Greater Philadelphia area.

I get my cheapie manicures and polish changes here because they are clean and quick.  I am not feeling secure enough to get a pedicure here though as I am a complete hygiene snob and a pedi-connoisseur.  I used to go to Mint Julip for pedis - but my favorite vernisseur left.  I guess it's back to Salon Royale Court for pedi's from now on.  Meanwhile - need a quick eyebrow wax or a mani (or $6.00 polish change?)  Hurry.  Pick-color!

4.5 stars - just a hair shy of 5.  I just attended a private luncheon event at the Union League in the McMichael room.  The service was "White Glove" and so attentive and wonderful.  Food was good - with a great salad that contained dried cranberries, toasted oine nuts & crumbled bleu.  Also a stand-out were the individually plated pecan pies.  YUM-O!  The entrees, however were just "OK" my fish stuffed with crabmeat bechamel was a tad dry and OVERLY salty.  I can't speak to the other entree choice - roast pork - as I don't "do pig".  But it looked nice.  Great presentation and a great, historic space with lots of portraits to look at - one of George W. was being hung with great care the day I was there.  You can also (try to) have your wedding here - but you really "gotta know someone" to get on the list.  Oh - and there IS an enforced dress code - so don't be the bopob that I was and show up wearing sheakers.  (I KNEW I shoulda hauld my shoes along..)  They snuck me in thru the back.

I came here alone for lunch on a dead-to-the-world August Thursday at about 12:15 PM.  Place was nearly empty and thus, I had attentive and Stellar service from a lovely young lady (I forgot her name).  Good music on in the background (we had just lost Aretha Franklin today so lots of 50's and 60's tunes, including the Queen of Soul and BB King).  But even better was the $9.79 2 meat combo for lunch.  Wow!  I'm gonna need a nap at my desk fter that feast of ribs (2 - but very tender and delicious) and 1/4 chicken dark.   Those corn muffins taste like cake.  $2.99 for a diet soda seems way high though... In any case, Famous Dave's is a chain so you know what you are getting when you go. Decent 'cue in a chain-y environment.

Wow - I can't believe it took me this long to yelp the Constitution Center.  This really is a must-stop place for visitors & tourists as well as residents.  The exhibits are historically accurate and a bit of fun - although kinda dull for the very young (our 4 year old would rather run the halls).  The performance is not a great for young kids - too boring - but we, as parents, enjoyed it.   (And the respite of sitting down for a few!!)
I just can't stop raving about Matyson.  Just had lunch today - House made pappardele with kale and shortribs.  Delectable.    Go there NOW!

I shopped here twice today first before a meeting (didn;t have enough time to try on) and again after the meeting ended AND after a trip to BCBG (see my review on them).  I tried on an exquisite hot pink $248 trench coat (yes, really) and some cute tops.  I settled on a strectch black knit top.  Decent price, too - reduced from 59.98 to 29.98.  SOLD!!!!  Note:  I cam back about 2 weeks later and the tank tops were on sale. ($19.99 each) snagged 2 of 'em and another cute sleeves top marked $49.98 but reduced by 30%. - Morale of story? The sales are good.  Ryan and the other lady at the front counter were very nice and helpful - but probably because the place was nearly empty both times I visited today.  I think they are HURTING for sales.

Wow!!!!!  I am gonna go out on a limb here and give these fine people the full 5 stars (some may argue its a 4 star experience - but what we had last night was truly 5 stars all the way.)  NOTE:  We also went BACK on 4/4/09 and it was fabulous AGAIN!  Starting with the bar and terrific bartender who mixed me a fine Whiska-retto Sour (That's a Canadian Club Whisky Sour with a splash of Amaretto to sweeten it up. - YUM.).  The bar has a retro feel with colored shelves that slant at different angles to display the bottles of liquor.  Next we (there were 4 of us) were seated by our gracious host/waiter/manager (possibly owner?) and ordered lots of tasty treats.  We started with an appetizer course.  I had a terrific goat cheese (mild - not too goaty) and beet salad.  2 of us has the slightly salty but very tasty French Onion Soup, and we all tasted the Chicken Shumai (obviously frozen - but tasty nonetheless.).  Also the stuffed portabello mushroom is SO TERRIFIC.  Since one of the entrees - Pasta "Mikey" appealed to all of us - we ordered one order and split it 4 ways on 4 little plates as a pasta course.  The pasta was penne, coated in a rich, creamy pink sauce accented with shavings of proscuitto.  Very tasty and perfect as an app.  (May be too rich to eat a big plateful.)  For entrees the standout was the lamb - a gorgeous frenched rack of 8 chops total, served with airy riced potatoes and asparagus spears.  The meatlof entree (with more of the delicious mash) and my husband's "special" of flaky-crusted chicken pot pie, all disappeared.  We were nearly stuffed by now, but stayed for delicious rich cups of freshly brewed coffe and decaf.  And split amongst us 1 cheesecake (classic and creamy) and a decadent chocolate bourbon pecan pie.  (The crust of which was outstanding.).  We have returned twuce.  What lovely evenings we have had,  surrounded by gorgeous decorations and the classic portraits that adorn the walls.  This is a unique place that seems like "nothing" when you walk by.  Go INSIDE!!!  Go!!!  You will not be disappointed.

Solid!  A great new choice for lunch ($7 for dark, $8 for white 1/4 with 2 sides).  My BFF and I got a 1/2 chicken and 2 sides for $11.50 - 2 sides were plenty for us to share.  We chose the cornbread mini-muffins (so good) and mac 'n cheese (my friend loved it, I wasn't wowed.)  Meanwhile the chicken is the star of the show.  Not too salty, yet nicely seasoned and perfected rotisseried.  It was very warm in there - even with the A/C running.  (All those rotisseries)/  Decent service, too.

This place is kinda depressing. Server, Rae, was nice - and attentive. Place was nearly empty on a Monday night.  Salad that came with the meal was pretty bad - lettuce was overly wet, cut into tiny pieces and starting to rust (turn brown).  The 2 slices of tomato and 2 sliced of un-peeled waxy cucumber were at least edible.  The supposedly home-made russian dressing was just awful (thank goodness I ordered it on the side).  The entree itself was OK - veal francese (I know!  What possessed me -next time, if there is a next time as I am not prone to return, I will get a gyro or pancakes or something "easier").  Surprisingly good.  3 stars even - but the salad skeeved me.  Ugly interior - but at least they seem to be re-doing the ladies room.  As I said, I will not rush back.  I much prefer the Court diner or the new Aston Diner

Jamie sums it up - this is the Adult version of Plato's Closet. I found some cheap and cute (new with tags on) items but nothing that fit well. I will be back to try again.   Excellent service from Nyra (nyla?) from NYC.

Went to CVS (across the street and down a bit) too get passport pictures taken.  Their camera was broken so I came here.  Should have came here first - much cleaner and emptier store.  Meanwhile the lady running their photo center could not get the proper label to print.  I waited and waited for my pictures.  Finally she just let me HAVE them.  Free.    They need to figure out their photo procedures better.

Valentine's Day weekend and service by Laura was wonderful even if we could only get a 5 PM or 8:30 PM res.  We opted for 5 PM and there was still a huge crowd.  Appetizer sampler ($20) was great as well as Duck App. The kiddo devoured it. Sashimi was MUCH fresher and better this time including the ($27) Blue Fin lover's plate and a few pieces of toro ($8 a pop) and Ikura ($4.50).  No room for dessert but we left happy.

Dear Nail Salon,  I confess! Today I cheated on you, my usual nail salon, with Noble Nails. Kim is an excellent technician and gave me a straightforward, basic manicure with the new OPI Nail Envy Color Formula.  I am anxious to see how many days wear I can get out of it.  My hands were is dire need of cuticle care, and Kim is a true professional. The salon is clean and well run.  If I lived near here, I would DEFINITELY be back. $10 mani, $22 gel and $22 pedis.  (They also have $30 hot stone spa pedis.  YAY!!!!!)  They also carry CND - including my beloved Vinyluxx. I can get 6-8 days out of a Vinyluxx Mani!  Loving it here so far.

OK, I will be nice and cut them a break.  It should be 2 or 2.5 stars, but I am hoping they will work out the kinks and improve.  The menu sounded sooooo wonderful and my friend was keen to try Root - so we went.  The place was dead empty when we arrived, but throughout our meal about 8 people were dining.  Definitely BYO something - they have NOTHING to drink but water.  Turns out this is the site of the former Palate BYOB.  I guess they just couldn't make it.  The food is really not great.  (Which is a shame because they claim to use sustainable and local ingredients and I strive to support it.  The tattoo-covered chef and the server (a nice gal) were hospitable.  Here's what made the food more like 2 stars.  I started with the poached shrimp salad.  It came with 2 large, overcooked a bit rubbery shrimp.   The greens were shredded and appeared to be romaine and napa cabbage in a tangy vinaigrette.  The drizzle of (good quality) balsamic around the plate edge was good.  Now the strange entree.  (We skipped dessert  -  didn't want to chance it.)  I ordered the rabbit and oxtail raviolo with uni cream.  The Oxtail was the best part - rich, and meaty with a delicious flavor.  The rabbit really did taste like dark meat chicken.  And the sauce was heavy - but tasty.  Here's a the bad part - the crepes were heavy as lead.  Kinda like a cross between home-made paste (flour & water) and Bisquick.  Really strange.  Not deelicate at all, and certainly not like pasta - more like a home-made leaden buscuit that fell flat.  It's really a shame.  I am hoping they can figure it out - and they really, really need A/C or at least a few more fans.  Sadly I am not one of them...

This is a review of the Macy's located in the Cheryy Hill mall.  We had a fun day of shopping noth at Nordstrom and here at Macy's.  My friend got 2 amazing pair of shoes at great prices.  The sales are worth checking out.
Many thanks to the Acme on Baltimore Pike in Media for supporting our girl scout troops and graciously allowing them to seel Girl Scout cookies at their stores.  We are so grateful for this!

Took our 2012 Hyundai herefor annual inspection and a few minor repairs. Had a 9:30 AM appointment and arrived early - 9:15.  Inspection was done (including oil change) in about 1 hour while I waited.  Took another 90 minutes for repair work.  Killed the whole morning - but at least not the entire day. TV in waiting area with coffee and a water cooler.  Thankful we got out in about 3 hours.
Our 10 year old LOVES this store and we come in all the time now. Gonna ask for gift cards for her next birthday.  Check out the selection of nightlights of all things.  Wonderful things.

OK, now that my 3 year old is nearly 7 - this place is a wee bit more appropriate.  (Incidentally she had her 6th birthday party and will have her 7th also at North Bowl).  Meanwhile - we popped in for a quick game (she bowled - I watched - our poor server, Dennis (bless his heart) served us 2 glasses of water).  $11.00 for 1 game ($5.95) plus show rental.  Sheesh.  Glad I didn;t order a cocktail.  Meanwhile - the BASE price for a kis party here is now $25 a head.  The music was very loud - but they turned it down for us. Lanes are clean and seating is comfortable.  Very "clubby" - just as it was when we came here years ago.  The 7 year old loves it! (But - she did say that she likes North Bowl better - and so do I for many reasons.)  It sure ain't the crappy old bowling alley that I grew up with!

Did they re-model? Something seems better about this beer-stocked deli - snacks, sandwiches and all the usual suspects.  A wide selection of cold drinks.  Good location - and hours.  No issues from me.

Yup.  This is the place.  This place is worthy of my 600th review on yelp!!!  It has the sentimental factor (CHeck) - we ate here right after meeting with the Judge who would marry us.  It has the location factor (Philly burbs).  It has - most importantly -great Mexican food and free Margarita's in a strip mall.  You gotta love that loosely interpreted liquor law.  Go, Pennsylvania!  In any case we thoroughly enjoyed (and JUSt - I mean just barely - beat the dinner crowd by getting there at 5:25 PM on a weekday. ) our home-made salsa fresca, chips and terrific guac.  I had chicken in a mole sauce - but it was different some how - and really special.  My (then) fiance had lamb - which her really enjoyed.  Not cheap - but so worth it.  What a surprise and a pleasant one. By the time we left the place was PACKED - and i bet they will continue to pack 'em in.  By the way - free or not - the Margarita's were very good, indeed.

Woo Jung (Brother is Woo, Sister is Jung) is a Korean owned Japanese place (with Hwe Dup Bap on the menu!) in a strip mall in East Norriton.  I was honestly scared to even try it but I am so glad I did.  The staff is wonderful and my experience was terrific as a single diner on a dead-empty Friday lunch.  I ordered the $16.95 lunch special which came with 6 pieces of sashimi (all were excellent - included seared/sauced Chu-Toro!  Score!!!!!!) and 3 nigiri (Tuna, Salmon and a white fish - not sure which - not yellowtail).  The accompanying spicy tuna roll was delicious as well.  Miso soup had a slight sweetness of Mirin. Very nice.  I can't wait to return!!  BYO - and a little pricey for lunch but worth it for a special treat. Now, maybe they'll add some galbi to the menu???  Thank you, Jung!!!!!

The food is excellent but Soooooo pricey.  The cafe next door is a better value - and similar food choices.  But what really makes this place special are the sweeping views of Longwood gardens.    I love it there!
Convenient location but super crowded on weekdays during the lunch hour(s) as a result.  I got in and out fast.  THANK goodness they had what I needed.
Top-quality, good looking breakable gift items.  Lamps, baubles, shiny stuff and GOREOUS, gorgeous gifties.  It's been around forever and I love it.

OK - I take back some of what I said. After a year has passed - I returned to Tierra Mia today and found a few things have changed.  The icy-cold receptionist is gone (YAY) and I was treated very well during my visit today.  I started with a $58 pedicure with the coconut oil & fresh coconut shavings as the exfoliant.  It was done by Karina herself and was FANTASTIC.  I hope the polish will wear well - as my feet feel FAB-U-LOUS.  Again - I reiterate the pedicure chair she bought has sounds therapy - ask for the headphones - that vibrates in time to relaxing music.  It is a reall cool, wonderful pedicure chair.  I would pay money just to come and sit in it for a while.  After my pedi - which took about 60 minutes, I got the seasonal cucumber mani.  It was $28 and used pure shea butter, sea salt and cruished cucumbers (they put it in a food processor).  Very cooling and wonderful for summer.  Justin - Karina's fiance was there - and he is a very nice guy and runs things well.  It's a beautiful (pricey) spa.  I am fearful the polish will yellow or chip. (I told them about my previous experience with yellowing - and they said NO SUNSCREEN or bug spray.  Turns out I had, indeed, applied sunscreen after my services a year ago - MY BAD!)  I still wish we could bring our own polish - and I kinda thing it's ridiculous that for the MONEY we are paying (I dropped $100 even today including tip) we can't use our OPI or CND products for fear of destrying her air quality.  That still seems a bit wrong, but anyway - If I can get a decent wear out of her products (all water based polishes), I will come back again.  Definitely for pedis - not sure if I can justify a $28 mani every week - or even every 2.  Tierra Mia - you are a beatiful, unique place.  I am sure you will be very successful.
El kiddo is now 11 and still loves coming here.  Expensive but fun.

Yay to Rebecca Michaels for expanding the Flying Monkey empire.  The new space is small, but so cute - and the color scheme continues the theme.  You can get all the goodies you know and love from the Reading Terminal location here in the gayborhood.  Go, monkey, go!

I can not believe how clean, new, slick, friendly and pleasant my experience was at the new (actually 5 mos. old) Panda Express, fast-food Chinese in the Comcast Center.  Normally I can not stand sloppy, gloppy, steam-table, mall Chinese - so boy was I shocked when the food not only looked great (albeit lots of the choices and all of the shrimp choices are fried) but tasted good, too.  Trepidatious bynature I ordered only a small a la carte (1/2 pint) box of Honey Walnut Shrimp (Fried + Mayonnaise + Sugar = health BOMB) and instantly recalled the bygone era of late 1980's Chinese-American fare.  The Manager, Jay,  was very accomodating and said that now - for large orders (and within a few blocks) they will deliver and the offer party trays and catering.  The even have a deal they will do with schools for fundraising.  The wheels are turning...  Perhaps a Panda Feast (for $30 you get 3 large entress and 2 large sides - enough for 4 (easily) to 7 (tiny eaters) people.  A big pan entree $36 - $48 if you pick shrimp feeds about 8 people.  They also have a small catering package for $96 that easily feeds 16.  I am planning a prty soon and will update my review with the results - but so far I am shockingly pleased with Panda Express.

The Equinox cheese is fabulous!  Birchrun Hills Farm sells cheese at many local farmers market (I usually see them at Media and Headhouse. They also make blue and "Fat Cat" - a semi-soft cheese.  They also supply veal to local restaurants.  Good local stuff!

Still Excellent after all these years.  A gal-pal and I shared the potato latke app with our lunch today - what BLISS.  3 petite, crisp, flavorful (not too greasy) pancakes topped with lightly salted smoked salmon, applsauce and dill creme fraiche.  WOW.  My Kale salad was over-the-top delicious and lightly dressed with the perfect amount of lemon/oregano vinaigrette (You could taste juice and zest) with parmesan slivers and sweet, glorious butternut squash chunks.  I got a small for $7 - but next time I may just get the large ($10).  Good, good, good stuff.  Very nice server, too.  GO TO MATYSON.  So rockin' good.

Ok - I upgraded them to 5 stars based on our last visit (we have now been there about 4-5 times.)  This time we came with our 6 year old at night and had pancakes, a chef salad (with delicious FRESH cooked turkey breast) and FABULOUS home-made pierogi.  Do not miss them.  The re-modelled and added 2 new bathrooms (lovely) and I just love the Court Diner.

This place is more of a shop and less of a tea bar - for a tea bar see Remedy down the street and around the corner - but STEAP has a great selection of fine and rare loose leafs.  I like both Remedy and Steap - but I prefer to buy tea here and drink tea at Remedy.  The Iced Peach White I tried over the summer was terrific.  No sweetener needed.  It was naturally fruity and sweet with a clean finish.  YUM!  Oh - and teas and tea-gear from STEAP make for cute gifts.
An American classic and a Philadelphia GAYborhood staple.  Help save Giovanni's!  This place is a needed gem and a beacon for free-speaking, free-thinking Americans, gay or not.  Love it here!

A solid 4 stars (the Beet Salad was 5 star for me) with swanky decor, clean restrooms, great service from Tim and a healthy wine list.  (A few more sparklers by the glass would be nice.  I loved the beet salad app (Got a small for $5) served with pickled SWEET cippolini onions and served atop a small amount of tasty goat cheese cream (not too goaty).  I also enjoyed the mushroom papardelle - loaded with asparagus, garlic slices and of course - lots of 'shrooms.  My partner's food came out cold - but they promptly heated it up. His sweet potato mash was far to nutmegy for me - but the side of mac 'n cheese ($5) was terrific.  Bison meatloaf was $22 and served with baby carrots and broccolini (a bit salty).  Not 5 stars - but very close - a lovely lunch was $66 without booze and without dessert - so that is a bit pricey.  (My cappucino was $6 - OUCH.

I agree with Caroline AND Emily.  We take our little girl here and she LOVES it - especially all the animals.  They have activities in every season - even winter time. Xmas trees, Halloween Hay rides, Strawberry picking in spring.  Love it!  And yes - we make her wash her hands after petting the goats and before eating ice cream (or apple turnovers!!!)  Aliitle touristy and a few items in the market have HIGH prices - but hey - the loval produce is terrific.  We love it here.

I agree with Alice L.  (Though historically I have alsways enjoyed sampling the Violet and Rose flavors.)  The store is VERY old and has been a New Hope institution for years.  It COULD use a clean up.  I do enjoy the ice cream here - but willl not go during peak tourist season as I will NOT wait in a line for it.  The owner is a character - that said I have never had any bad experiences here.  Only tasy ice cream!

Had dinner at the sushi bar on a busy Saturday night (no reservation so no tables available - but plenty of sushi bar spots early on).  Excellent service by our server and expediter as well as the 2 "junior level" sushi chefs.  DH ordered edamame and chicken teri (yeah, I know) which he enjoyed. I had a small (which was huge - I can't imagine how enormous the large must be) Tom Kha which is one of my faves.  I have had Tom Kha at many places and the Tom Kha hear was overly sweet and thick with too much coconut milk and lacked the lemongrass and complexityy that a good Tom Kha should have.  That said - it was tasty but bland.  not exciting at all. Would not reorder it here unless I am having an intense Tom Kha Craving.  The Blue Fin lovers platter was deliciously fresh - and the complimentary veggie naruto roll was crisp and refreshing.  Since aside from Temaki in Media, this is the best sushi we have found (Yes, we've tried Margaret Kuo's and Azie)  we shall return.  And next time we'll make a reservation!  Oh - and the prices are on the high side.

OK, I am only reviewing the front lobby bar and the meeting facilities and food - all of which were solid and good.  I did not stay overnight here so I can't comment on the rooms.  Meanwhile, I attended a nice corporate event here last night (with dinner included) and a colleague drove - so he knew exactly where it was - BUT even he mentioned that the signage is weak and it's very hard to find this place if you don't know where to look.  We started with drinks at the lobby bar.  I had a fairly weak and not too spicey 3 star Bloody Mary.  It came with a slice of lemon and when I asked the female bartended (very sweet lady) for celery she said they did not have it.  OK.  Points off for that.  If you want a kickin' Bloody Mary by the way - try Bar North Third. but I digress...  Mmmn.  Now  I want a bloody mary.  OK.  Next it was off to the dinner/meeting.  The tables were pre-set with very warm butter (had been sitting out for quite some time).  The immediately plated chilled caesar salads that were very good - basic and crisp.  Not overly dressed.  The rolls were hot - which was a nice touch.  My entree - wild mushroom ravioli - was very tasty - and looked much better that the chicken marsala (1/2 a semiboned breast with a wing drumette attached - looked very banquet - and ONE mushroom.)  I was glad I did not order the chicken - but people ate it and seemed 3 -4 star happy.  Dessert was a moist carrot cake garnished with a single wilted strawberry.  All in all - things could have used a bit more polish and freshening up.  Service was very efficient - a bit too "hurry up and let the staff leave" for my taste.  Coffee was fresh and very yummy.  Meeting rooms was nice - standard hotel corporate stuff.  I have a feeling I'll be back for future events here.
Love coming here to bird-watch and walk around on a nice spring or summer day with el kiddo.  Free - and fun and can e educational.  Good for biking, too.

OMG! What a "scene"- if you want to people watch or have "dinner & a show" in tiny-cramped-Manhattan-style tables, this just might be the place for you.  A friend and I met for lunch - which wound up costing me $23.00 for an iced tea and a shrimp salad ($18.00 - ouch!).  She had a hair in her pizza - Eeeeew! Luckily the staff were gracious about it and whisked it away and didn't charge us for it.  The owners of Serafina chain (we used to go to the one on Madison in NYC and it, too, was a "scene"), were holding court with a bunch of leggy PR ladies.  Plus the Chairman of my old law firm was in the house.  What a freakish afternoon.  Decent, overpriced food served with a generous helping of hype - but so not my bag, baby.  Kudos to our lovely server Ayram - I pray does not have to suffer there too long.  Serafina should do well in Center City.   If you are a displaced Manhattanite and long for the old days - this place will do you right.  (Try the carpaccio - looks great.)

Free internet access and (as I happen to be an ING account holder) access to your banking.  Plus if you wear orange (like that EVER happens??) on certain days your coffee is free.  Kitschy come-ons and cool swag to be had here as well.  I really enjoy banking with ING Direct and the coffe shop is a nice addition.  But they need to clean those bathrooms more often - or else they'll be downgraded to 3 or even 2 stars.  They get GROSS!!!

My daughter enjoys the "square pizza" slices here (She refers to Sicilian as "square pizza") but even she at the astute age of 8 commented, "It's good - but not as good as Brooklyn".  Sums it up perfectly.  Smart kid.  Like her Momma.

Somewhere between Meh and A-OK. I attended a meeting here in the front bar area at the tables behind the bar.  Happy hour was ending so there were some luke-warm mozzarella sticks and dried out wings in a chafing dish.  Yuck.  (But free.)  The food I ordered (albeit a garden salad) was fresh but boring. Others plates looked unappetizing - fish & chips was a huge piece of fish in a THICK coating of batter.  (And chips which I don't eat).  Servers were pleasant and owner is a wonderful supporter of the community and my kid's school - but I am not impressed by the "classic" pub fare.  Also it gets LOUD in there, but that is a sign of a good pub.  Blah.
Surrisingly good food located in the bowels of Suburban Station. Breakfast wraps are made to order and fresh - $3.50 each.  Friendly cashier lady and cooks.

Matyson used to stand for Matt y Sonia - but, alas, the original owners have fled the coop.  However, the place is still run by a member of the family and for a BYOB - this place ROCKS.  I have been there for both lunch (many times) and dinner - just a few.  The $45 prix fixe is a deal - IF you like what they are serving.  Most times I pick and choose - and let me just say that you can not go wrong with the fish.  For lunch a delicious trout sandwich on fresh black bread with watercress for just $11 is terrific.  I have also tried the lobster pop-overs.  A warm, buttery pop-over (man I could eat about 4 of them plain) with large pieces of lobstermeat surrounded in a DECADENT (read: just a bit too much cream, for me) newburg style sauce with fresh chopped tomtato and presh green peas.  They also love morel mushrooms.  Dishes are complex without being "snooty" or "over the top". Desserts are great, too.  LOVE Mat-y-son - even under the new regime.
i went there with my daughters girl scout troop. the reason that i gave it a 3 is because the pancakes were sour and the fruit was not sweet.the rest was fine

Yum, yum, yum, yum, yum!  Yum.  Oh yeah.  Did I mention this is the real italian sorbetto / gelato.  The sorbettos are all dairy-free and still have a fabulous rich texture.  The flavors - sublime - like Blood Orange (the real McCoy), and Campari Grapefruit.  Last night they had a summertime offering of Lemon Opal Basil.  Want something fattening and decadent?  Get a cone (the euro-stle crisp cone) with a scoop of Dulce du Leche or Butterscoth and 1 scoop of deep, dark, ciocolatto sciurro (bitter dark choc.).  FREE home-made whipped cream is UNSWEETENED and compliments most selections.  Or - get a BRIOCHE, baby!  And fill it with frozen bliss.  The unsweetened whipped cream is complimentary.  You can feel your arteries clogging with each decadent mouthful.  OK, gotta go do cardio now...

This place used to be called Zai Fa and was mediocre then and is a touch better (In my opinion) now.  We ordered about $100 worth of food which easily fed our crowd of 10 adults and 2 little kids.  Fried Dumplings were better than the steamed - average and a bit "doughy".  Eggrolls and Shrimp Egg rolls were crisp, contained actual shrimp and lots of shredded cabbage.  Spare ribs were meaty and EXCELLENT. (Even better than Hong Kong Jack's which is our family's go-to for D-town old-school Chinese).  House special fried rice was just OK - Hong Kong Jack's is better. Chicken with Broccoli was ordered "light on the sauce" and thus was not nearly as greasy as it could have been.  They use brown sauce for their Chix 'n Brox.  My husband and Brother-in-law like hot food and enjoyed the General Tso's Chicken (looked very nice - text book Tso!) and Mongolian Beef. Combo platters are a good value and while they are heavy on the fried rice - there is a hefty portion of the entree (in our case Kung Pao Chicken) in there, too.  Very good egg drop, wonton and hot 'n sour soups (all are text book 1975 recipe Chinese American).  While not mind blowing - I can definitely see ordering Quart of Hot 'n Sour or Wonton the mext time I have the flu.  It is take out only (They might have 2 tiny tables out front) and be sure to grab your packets of duck, soy and mustard sauces on the way out.

4 stars for the spa - but 5 STARS for Cheryl Lee - the best damned nail technician that I have ever known.  Her spa pedicure is worth every penny and is like heaven on earth for me.  Well - I am one of Cheryl lee's faithful following.  Cheryl is just about the BEST nail tech you'll ever know.  I came to spa elysium on a very hectic, very icy, overbooked day before Xmas.  The expansive salon (spa is downstairs - nails & hair upstairs) was buzzing with activity and the front desk greeters were just not paying attention.  There was NOWHERE to sit in the waiting room (it was that packed) and many stylists were running late so people were getting grumpy.  Meanwhile, sunny Cheryl was running right on time.  (I arrived by train about an HOUR early.)  I started with a luxurious spa pedicure - which I can not recommend enough.  I also indulged and got a spa manicure ($25 vs. the regular $18 mani.)  Next time I will get a regular mani.  The extra exfoliating scrub was nice - but not needed each and every time.  I just love the way Cheryl does her nail services.  Very clean, thorugh and attentive to details.  My feet were smooth and cuticles neatly cleaned up. The polish was applied precisely and immaculately.  Cheryl - you are 5 stars in my book - but please tell the spa management teamt o shore up their front desk operations.  A busy spa/salon needs freindly attentive people at the front.
